details.body: TABAR, TABRET: paRavaH: v. Drum.
Tabard, s. tanutrAvAraH.
TABARD: tanutrAvAraH (?) and sim. comp. s.
Tabby, a. citra, Sabala, karburita.
TABBY: kalmAzita (f. tA): v. Dappled, spot- -ted.
TABBY , a. citraH -trA -traM, SavalaH -lA -laM. See BRINDLED
Tabernacle, s. pawaveSman n., pawamaMqapaH, dfzyaM; (fig.) acirasTAyI AvAsaH.
TABERNACLE: dUzyam: v. Tent.
TABERNACLE , s. maRqapaH, dUzpaM, pawamaRqapaH. See TENT.
Tabes, s. kzayaH, kzayaTuH.
TABES , s. kzayaH, kzayarogaH, kzayaTuH m., SarIraSozaRaM.
TABLATURE: a picture: AleKyam.

Table, s. PalakaH-kaM, ADAraH, maMcaH; ‘t(able) for writing’ leKanADAraH, lipisajjADAraH. 2 patraM. 3 (Of metal &c.), patraM, PalakaM; ‘sitting at the same t(able)’ sahaBojin, pAMkteyaH; ‘t(able) of contents’ sUcI-niGaMwa-patraM, sUci-cI f., anukramaRikA; ‘t(able) of numbers’ aMkapatraM-jAlaM; ‘be at t(able)’ Buj 7 A; ‘to keep good t(able)’ BojanaviSezAn upakxp c.; ‘t(able)-land’ aDityakA, UDvarBUmiUrDvaBUmi f., mAlaM kzetraM, sAnu m. n., prasTaH; ‘t(able)-talk’ viSraMBAlApaH-kaTA. Tablet, s. pawwikA, pawwaH, PalakaH, patraM; ‘on the t(ablet) of your heart’ hftpawwikAyAM. Tabular, a. patrAkAra.

TABLE: I Lit.:(1) Palakam;(2) patram (=leaf). II A picture: AleKyam.III Fig.: patram, t. of contents: nirGaRwapatram; interest-t. s: kusIdapatram. IV Of hand reKAvinyAsaH or reKAH (f. pl.).V A piece of furniture: no equiv.: *stammalam. Ph.: to keep a good t.: BojanaviSezAnupakalpayati (c. of kxp). T.-cloth: *stamBalAstaraRam.

TABLE , s. (For holding dishes, &c.) PalakaH -kaM, BojanaPalakaH -kaM, BIja- nADAraH, BojanAsanaM, maYcaH -YcakaH, BojanamaYcaH; ‘writing table,’ [Page794-a+ 51] liKanaPalakaM, lipiPalakaM, lipisajjADAraH, leKasADanADAraH. — (Per- sons eating at the same table) sahaBojinAM paMktiH f.; ‘un- worthy of eating at the same table with the good,’ sadBiH saha ekapaMktiBojanAnarhaH -rhA -rhaM. — (Of stone, metal, &c., for writ- ing) pawwaH, prastaraH, patraM -trikA. — (Tabular view) patrakaM, sAraRI, prastaraH, cakraM, see SYNOPSIS; ‘table of numbers, figures, &c.,’ aNkajAlaM, sAraRI, kozWakaM. — (Table of contents) anukramaRikA, sUcIpatraM, sUcI -cikA, patrapaYjI.
TABLE-CLOTH , s. lakAcCAdanaM, PalakAvaraRaM, PalakAcCAdanapawaH.
TABLE-LAND , s. sAnuH -nu m. n., aDityakA, prasTaH, samasTalaM, parvata- BUnikA, BfguH m., kawakaH, snuH m., snu n.
TABLE-TALK: I Lit.: *stamBalAlApaH.II Fig.: viSramBAlApaH, etc.
TABLELAND: mAlaM kzetram and sim. comp. s.
TABLET , s. patraM, patrikA, patrakaM, pawwaH, PalakaH -kaM, prastaraH.
To TABOO , v. a. upaBogAseDaM kf, BogAseDaM kf. See To INTERDICT.
Tabor, s. murajaH, mfdaMgaH.
TABOR , s. mfdaNgaH, pawahaH, paRavaH, praRavaH, AMkzI. See DRUM.
TABOSHEER , s. (Manna of the bamboo) vaMSakzIrI, vaMSarocanA, vaMSalocanA, tvakkzIrA -rI, karmmarI.
TABULAR: no equiv.: PalakIkfta (f. tA).
TABULAR , a. patrasTaH -sTA -sTaM, patrakArUQaH -QA -QaM, PalakasTaH &c.
Tacit, a. tUzRIM datta, mAnasa (sI f.); ‘t(acit) consent’ mAnasAjYA; ‘t(acit) obedience’ nirvikalpa-nirvivAda-AjYApAlanaM. [Tacit]ly, adv. tUzRIM, jozaM, mUkaBAvena, manasA; nirvikalpaM.
TACIT , a. vivakzitaH -tA -taM, arTasidDaH -dDA -dDaM, DvanitaH &c., anizeDa- rUpaH &c., mAnasaH -sI -saM; ‘tacit consent,’ mAnasAnujYA, mAnasaM.
TACITLY: (1) tUzRIm (= silently: q. v.);(2) manasA (=in mind).
TACITLY , adv. vivakzayA, anizeDena, manasA, DvanitArTatas, tUzRIM.
Taciturn, a. saMvftimat, mOnin, anAlApaSIla, tUzRIka, tUzRIMSIla, BAzaRavirakta, mitavAk-kaTa. [Taciturn]ity, s. saMvfti f., mOnaM, mUkaBAvaH, anAlApaH, mitavAk, kaTAvirakti f., vAgyamaH.
TACITURN: I Reserved: q. v.II Silent: q. v.: mOnin (f. nI).

TACITURN , a. anAlApaSIlaH -lA -laM, alpavAdI -dinI &c., tUzRIMSIlaH -lA -laM, kaTAviraktaH -ktA -ktaM, AlApavimuKaH -KA -KaM, BAzaRaviraktaH &c., parimitakaTaH &c., mOnI &c., anAlApaH -pA -paM, tUzRIkaH -kA -kaM. See RESERVED.
TACITURNITY: mOnam: v. Silence.
TACITURNITY , s. AlApaviraktiH f., anAlApaSIlatA, anAlApaH -pitA, mOnitvaM, mOnaM, kaTAviraktiH f., vAgyAmaH. See RESERVE.
Tack, v. i. A-baMD 9 P, pi-A-nah 4 P. 2 (a vessel) nOmArgaM pari-vyA-vft c. s. kIlakaH, guRaH. [Tack]ing, s. nOmArgaparivftti f.
TACK: I To fasten: q. v.: baDnAti (banD, c. 9.).II To turn: q. v.: vyAvartayati (c. of vft).II A nail: kIlaH.IV A rope: guRaH.
To TACK , v. a. (Fasten, attach) anubanD (c. 9. -baDnAti -bandDuM), AbanD, pinah, Anah, see To FASTEN, STITCH.
To TACK , v. n. nOmArgaM parivft in caus., nOmArgaparivarttanaM kf.
TACK , s. (Small nail) kzudrakIlaH, kIlakaH, kzudraSaNkuH m.
TACKING , s. nOmArgaparivarttanaM, nOmArgaparivfttiH f., nOpaTaparivfttiH.
Tackle, s. (nO-)sajjA, rajjvAdisAmagrI. v. t. sajjIkf 8 U, saMnah c. [Tackl]ing, s. See (s.) above.
TACKLE, -ING (subs.): majjA: v. Ship, equip- -ment.
TACKLE , TACKLING, s. nOkAsajjA, nOsajjA, sajjA. See RIGGING.
Tact, s. kOSalaM, nEpuRyaM, vEdagDyaM, yukti f., cAturyaM; See Skill. Tactics, s. yukti-kOSalaM; (of war) balavinyAsakOSalaM, vyUharacanAvidyA. Tactician, s. yuktikuSalaH, vyUhapaMqitaH.
TACT: perh. vEdagDam or kOSalam: v. Skill.
TACT , s. yuktiH f., kuSalatA, kOSalyaM, vijYatA, aBijYatA. See SKILL.
TACTICIAN: perh. yuktikuSala (f. lA): v. Skilful.
TACTICIAN , s. vyUharacanakuSalaH, vyUharacanABijYaH, vyUhapaRqitaH.
TACTICS: perh. yuktikOSalam: v. Skill, stra- -tegy.
TACTICS , s. vyUharacanavidyA, balavinyAsavidyA, sEnyavinyAsavidyA, vyUharacanA, sEnyaracanA, vyUhanaM.
TACTILE , a. sparSanIyaH -yA -yaM, spfSyaH -SyA -SyaM. See TANGIBLE.
Tadpole, s. BekaSiSuH-SAvakaH.
TADPOLE: BekaqimbaH and sim. comp. s.: v. Young.
TADPOLE , s. BekaSAvakaH, maRqUkaSAvakaH, bAlamaRqUkaH.
Tag, s. agraM.
TAG: I Subs.: agram (= point).II Put a t. to: v. To put.
Tail, s. lAMgU(gu)laM, pucCaH-cCaM, lUmaM; bAlahastaH, bAlaDiH (bushy end). [Tail]ed, a. pucCin, lAMgUlayukta.
TAIL: I Lit.:(1) lANgUlam;(2) pucCa (rarely picCa) (mn.);(3) bAlaH, -DiH;(4) laYjaH (rare).II Fig.: pucCa (mn.).

TAIL , s. pucCaH -cCaM, lANgUlaM, lANgulaM, laNgUlaM, bAlaH -lA, bAlaDiH m., bAlahastaH, lUmaM, lomaH, picCaH, laYjaH; ‘peacock's tail,’ varhaH -rhaM, picCaM, kalApaH, mayUrapucCaM, pracalAkaH; ‘to lift up the tail,’ utpucCa (Nom. utpucCayate).
TAIL-LESS , a. apucCaH -cCA -cCaM, pucCahInaH -nA -naM, pucCarahitaH &c.
TAILED: (1) lANgUlin (f. nI);(2) pucCavat (f. tI); and sim. comp. s.
TAILED , a. pucCI -cCinI -cCi (n), pucCavAn -vatI -vat (t), picCavAn &c., pucCAnvitaH -tA -taM, lANgUlI &c., picCilaH -lA -laM.
TAILLESS: (1) nirlANgu(NgU)la (f. lA);(2) pucCahIna (f. nA); etc.
Tailor, s. sOcikaH, tunnavAyaH, sUcikaH; ‘t(ailor)ʼs work’ sUcyA sevanaM, sUcikarman n.
TAILOR: (1) sOcikaH;(2) tunnavAyaH, Ram. ii. 83. 15.;(2) sevanakartf (m.) and sim. comp. s. com.
TAILOR , s. sOcikaH, sUcikaH, sOciH m., tunnavAyaH, vastraBedI m. (n), vastraBedakaH, sUcikarmmavid m.
TAILOR-BIRD: (1) caYcusUciH;(2) wuRwukaH.
TAILORING: (1) sUcikarman (n.);(2) sUcyAsevanam, etc.
Taint, v. t. duz c. (dUzayati), lip 6 P, kalaMkayati (D.). s. dUzaRaM, kalaMkaH, dozaH; See Stain.
TAINT (v.): dUzayati (c. of duz): v. To stain, pollute.
TAINT (subs.): I Corruption: q. v.: dUzaRam II Stain: q. v.: kalaNkaH.
To TAINT , v. a. duz (c. 10. dUzayati -yituM), lip (c. 6. limpati, leptuM), dozayuktaM -ktAM kf, dUzaRaM kf. See To CORRUPT, INSPECT, STAIN.
TAINT , s. dUzaRaM, dozaH, kalaNkaH, malaM, lepaH -panaM. See STAIN.
TAINTED , p. p. dUzitaH -tA -taM, liptaH -ptA -ptaM, kalaNkitaH -tA -taM, saka- laNkaH -NkA -NkaM; ‘as meat,’ pUtiganDikaH -kA -kaM, durganDI -nDinI &c.

Take, v. t. grah 9 U, prati-pari-° (in all senses) agfhIte rAkzase (Mu. 1); upa-deSaM gfhARa &c.; A-dA 3 A, prati-iz 6 P; svI-aMgI-kf 8 U. 2 Df 1 P, 10, A-ava-laMb 1 A. 3 (A word in a sense) pari-, grah; tatrATaSabda AnaMtaryArTaH parigfhyate (S. B. 23) ‘is taken in the sense of’ &c. 4 nI 1 P, vah 1 P, hf 1 P. 5 upalaB 1 A, avagam 1 P. 6 anuBU 1 P; See Suffer, Affect. 7 laB, prAp 5 P, aDigam, A-sad c.; See Get. 7 Captivate, q. v.; ‘t(ake) food’ AhAraM sev 1 A; ‘t(ake) the field’ raRa-BUmiM avatF 1 P, raRAMgaRe yuD 4 A; ‘t(ake) rest’ viSram 4 P; ‘t(ake) root’ mUlaM baMD 9 P; ‘t(ake) heart’ samASvas 2 P, DEryaM avalaMb-avazwaMB 9 P; See Courage; ‘t(ake) fire’ dah pass., agniM upa-i 2 P; ‘t(ake) in hand’ pratipad 4 A, u(U)rIkf ‘t(ake) place’; See Happen; ‘t(ake) part in’ hastaM dA 3 U, saMgin-sahakArin-sahAya a. BU; ‘took part in the massacre’ viSa-sane sahAyo baBUva; ‘t(ake) aim’ saM-DA 3 U; ‘t(ake) oneʼs way’ siD-sAD c. (sADayati), sADayAmo vayaM (S. 1); ‘t(ake) effect’ Pal 1 P, saPalIBU 1 P; ‘t(ake) possession of’ Akram 1 U, 4 P, AviS 6 P; ‘t(ake) to task’ nirBarts 10 A, paruzaM niMd 1 P. v. i. siD 4 P, saMpad 4 A, guRaM Avah. 2 ASri 1 U, vraj 1 P. [Take] away, apa-vi-nI 1 P, apa-, hf 1 P, apa-Uh 1 U, vinud c.; See Remove. [Take] back, saM-pratisaM-hf, pratyA-dA, pratyAnI. [Take] down, avaruh c., ni-ava-pat c., aDo nI. 2 liK 6 P. [Take] for, man 4 A; See Consider; ‘mischievousness is t(ak)en for assiduity’ cApalpamudyogitAM Bajate. [Take] in, grah, sev; (in the stomach) gras 1 A; ni, ga 6 P. 2 vipra-laB 1 A; See Cheat. [Take] off, apanI, avatF c., unmuc 6 P, avakfz. [Take] out, bahirnI, apanI. [Take] to, sev, ASri, avalaMb. [Take] up, pratipad, aMgI-svI-kf. 2 AraB 1 A, pravft c. 3 Occupy, Engross, q. v. [Take] upon (oneself), aMgIkf, pratipad, u(U)rIkf; (nirvAhaH pratipannavastuzu Mu. 2). [Tak]er, s. grahItf m., grAhin-hArin-hft in comp. [Tak]ing, a. mohin, manohArin, cittAkarzin, manojYa; See Charming. 2 grAhin, &c. s. A-dAnaM, grahaRaM, svIkAraH.

TAKE (v. t.): I In general:(1) gfhnAti (graha, c. 9.), t. ing and looking: gfhItvA nirIkzya, Mu. i.; t. up arms: gfhARa Sastram, R. iii. 51.; t. n but afterwards released: gfhItapratimukta (f. ktA), R. iv. 43.; he took the way of running pigs: jagrAha sa drutavarAhakulasya mArgam, R. ix. 59.; did she t. (it) from the hinds: tayA gfhItaM nu mfgANganAByaH, Ku. i. 46.; when he t. s your hand solemnly: anena pARO viDivad gfhIte, R. vi. 63.; intending to t. the arrow: SaraM jigfkzuH, Ki. xiii. 32.; without t. ing beetles: agfhItatAmbUla (f. lA), C. v.; took a few mouthfuls: katicit kavalAnyagfhRAt, C. v.; rustics t. (it) otherwise: anyaTA gfhRanti grAmyAH, C. vii.; do not t. advice: na gfhRantyupadeSam, K.; to t. all forms: viSvarUpatvaM grahItum, K.; to t. venerable men by service: grahItumAryAn paricaryayA, Si. i. 17.; so long as Rākṣasa is not t.n: agfhIte rAkzase, Mu. i.; when they t.ing your signs: tezu gfhItasaMjYezu, Mu. i.; are t.n as if by evils stars: grahEriva gfhyante, K.; t. the pride of [Page699] killing a woman: gfhARa vaDUvaDapOruzam, N. iv. 53.; His Majesty who has t.n his name well: tasya sugfhItanAmno devasya, C. vii.;(2) Adatte, sam-, (dA, c. 3.: physically), t.ing the girl by the hand: kanyAmAdadAnaH kareRa, Ku.; for t. ing is for spending: AdAnaM hi visargAya, R.: v. Also to catch, hold, view, understand.II Special. Ph.: to t. food: AhAraM karoti; t. rest: viSrAmaM karoti; t. aim at: lakzyIkaroti; t. root: mUlaM baDnAti; t. compassion: dayAM karoti; t. fire: agnimupEti; t. courage: samASvasiti; t. leave of: Amantrayati; t. oath: SapaTaM karoti; t. pains: pariSramaM karoti; t. place: v. To happen; t. part: hastaM dadAti; t. care of: rakzati; t. effect: saPalIBavati; t. wine etc.: madyaM etc. sevate, ni- (sev, c. 1.), Ni.; time for t.ing medicines: BEzajyasevanakAlaH, Bha.; it is time to t. bath and food: samayaH Kalu snAnaBojane sevitum. V. v. 11.III To conduct, convey: q. v.: nayati (nI, c. 1.),
TAKE (v. i.): I To have effect: to t. well: hitaM karoti.II To resort: q. v.: Srayati (Sri, c. 1.).III To please: q. v.

To TAKE , v. a. grah (c. 9. gfhlAti -hlIte, grahItuM), pratigrah, aBigrah, parigrah, sampragrah, upasampragrah, AdA (c. 3. -dadAti -datte -dAtuM), upAdA, laB (c. 1. laBate, labDuM), upalaB, DA (c. 3. Datte, DAtuM), pratAz (c. 6. -icCati -epituM), grahaRaM kf, AdAnaM kf. — (Seize) hf (c. 1. harati, harttuM), Df (c. 1. Darati, DarttuM), haraRaM kf. — (Captivate), see the word. — (Apprehend) grah, upalaB, avagam. — (Feel, experience, be affected by) upahataH -tA -taM BU, anuBU, upagam, upAgam, vid. — (Swallow) gF, nigF, gras, KAd, pA. — (Admit) grah, svIkf, aNgIkf. — (Gain possession of) Ap, prAp, arj, upArj, laB, Asad, aDigam, see To GAIN. — (Take possession of) Akram (c. 1. -krAmati -kramituM), AviS, samAviS. — (Require) AkAMkz, see To REQUIRE. — (Take away) apanI (c. 1. -nayati -netuM), nI, apahf, hf, see To REMOVE, v. a. — (Take back) pratyAdA; ‘lead back,’ pratinI. — (Take down), see To PULL DOWN, DEPRESS, WRITE. — (Take in), see To COMPREHEND, CHEAT. — (Take off) apanI, avatF or uttF in caus., utkfz, see To STRIP, DIVEST, IMITATE. — (Take up), see To LIFT, UNDERTAKE, OCCUPY, ENGROSS, COM- PRISE. — (Take upon one's self) svIkf, see To UNDERTAKE. Obs. The word ‘take’ in English has often no equivalent in Sanskrit, but must be rendered by some other form of expression. It may often be expressed by the roots kf or BU in conjunction with a noun, and is not unfre- quently inherent in the verb without being expressed at all, as in the following examples. — (Take aim) badDAnuSayaH -yA -yaM BU, lakzIkf, anusanDA. — (Take an airing) vAyuhetoH pari- kram or vihf. — (Take breath), see To PAUSE, REST. — (Take care, take heed), see To HEED. — (Take care of) rakza, see under CARE. — (Take a course), see To RESORT. — (Take effect) praBU, sapraBAvaH -vA -vaM BU, prabalIBU, saPalIBU, see EFFICACIOUS. — (Take hold), see To SEIZE, HOLD. — (Take in hand), see To UNDER- TAKE. — (Take leave) Amantr, AmantraRaM kf, see FAREWELL. — (Take notice), see To OBSERVE, NOTICE. — (Take pains), see under PAIN. — (Take part), see To SHARE. — (Take place), see To HAPPEN. — (Take root), see To ROOT, v. n. — (Take to task) nirBarts, see To REPROVE. — (Take the name) nAma grah.

To TAKE , v. n. (Betake one's self) ASri, see RECOURSE, RESORT. — (Gain reception, succeed) siD (c. 4. siDyati, sedDuM), sampad (c. 4. -padyate -pattuM), prasidDiM prAp, prasidDIBU, lokaprasidDaH -dDA -dDaM BU. — (Have effect) praBU. — (Take after) anukf.

TAKE AWAY: I To take, carry: q. v.: Adatte. II To remove: q. v.:(1) apanayati, vi-, the darkness of rage should be taken away: rozamayaM timiramapaneyam, Ki. ii. 36.;(2) harati, apa-, I will t. this fortune by gambling: dyUtena SriyaM harizyAmi, Mah. ii. 56. 1.;(3) apavahati (vah, c. 1.), t.ing away the bladder: klomapohya, D. viii.
TAKE DOWN: I Lit.: aDo nayati etc.II To write down: liKati (liK, c. 6.).
TAKE IN, INTO: I To take, as water: gfhRAti. II To cheat: q. v.: vipralaBate (laB, c. 1.). III To contract: q. v.
TAKE OFF: I To remove: q. v.:(1) apanayati, t.ing off their helmets: apanItaSirastrARAH, R. iv. 64.;(2) unmuYcati (muc, c. 6.: only of shoes, etc.), t. ing them (the shoes) off: tadynmucya, Vi.
TAKE ON: I To assume: gfhRAti.II To lament: q. v.
TAKE OUT: I Lit.: bahizkaroti, t. ing out his son from the granary: tatputraM kuSUlAdvahizkftya, H. ii. II To remove: q. v.: apanayati.
TAKE ROUND: pariRayati, Ku. vii. 80.: v. Take, round.
TAKE TO: sevate, (sev, c. 1.), everyday took to hunting: sadA sizeve mfgayAm, K. s. xi. 3.: v. Betake.
TAKE UP: I In gen.: gfhRAti, pari-.II To begin: q. v.
TAKE UPON ONESELF: svayaM vyavasyati (so, c. 4.). : v. To undertake.

TAKEN , p. p. gfhItaH -tA -taM, AdattaH -ttA -ttaM, AttaH &c., upAttaH &c. — (Gained) prAptaH -ptA -ptaM, AptaH &c., labDaH -bDA -bDaM. — (Taken away) apanItaH -tA -taM, apahftaH -tA -taM, hftaH &c., see REMOVED. — (Taken down) avapAtitaH -tA -taM, pAtitaH -tA -taM, see LOWERED, HUMBLED. — (Taken off, as clothes, &c.) avatAritaH -tA -taM, see STRIPPED. — (Captivated) mohitaH -tA -taM, hftacittaH -ttA -ttaM, vaSI- kftaH &c.; ‘let it be taken,’ gfhyatAM; ‘proper to be taken,’ grahaRIyaH -yA -yaM, AdeyaH -yA -yaM; ‘having taken,’ gfhItvA, AdAya; ‘having taken his bow and arrow,’ gfhItezukArmmukaH, Attezu- kArmmukaH.
TAKER: (1) grahItf (f. trI);(2) netf (f. trI); etc.: v. To take.
TAKER , s. grAhI m. -hiRI f. (n), grAhakaH -hikA, grahItA m. -trI f. (tf), AdAyI m. -yinI f., pratigrahItA m., harttA m., hArI m.
TAKING (adj.): mohana (f. nI): v. Charming, attractive.
TAKING , s. (The act) grahaRaM, grahaH, grAhaH, pratigrahaRaM, pratigrAhaH, AdAnaM, upAdAnaM, svIkaraRaM, svIkAraH; ‘taking away,’ apanayanaM, haraRaM, apaharaRaM, see REMOVAL.
TAKING , a. manohArI -riRI &c., hfdayagrAhI &c. See CAPTIVATING.
TALC: (1) aBram, -kam, calx of t.: aBrtakaBasman (n.); (2) ambaram;(3) girijam.
TALC , s. aBrakaM, aBaM, amalaM, nirmalaM, girijaM, girijAmalaM, meGajAlaM, meGanAlaM, SuBraM, svacCapatraM, ambaraM, antarIkzaM, BfNgaM; ‘calx of it,’ aBra- kaBasma m. (n).
Tale, s. kaTA, upa-, AKyAnaM, AKyAyikA. 2 pari-, gaRanA, saMKyAnaM; ‘t(ale)-bearer’ sUcakaH, karRejapaH; ‘t(ale)-bearing’ pESunyaM, upajApaH.
TALE: I Story: q. v.:(1) kaTA, narrate some t. to me: kaTAmAKayAhi me kAMcit, K. s. x. 3.; (2) AKyAnam, upa- (=narrative);(3) AKyAyikA (=romance).II Enumeration: gaRanA, pari-, Me. i. 22.
TALE , s. kaTA, upAKyAnaM, AKyAnaM, parikaTA, udantaH. See STORY.

Saying, rumour;(3) jalpaH, -nam or jalpitam (=idle t.); (4) kaTA, sam- (= chat), and having other t.: anyABiSca kaTAmiH, K.; I will hear their private t.: SfRomi viSvastakaTitAnyAsAm, Sa. iii.

To TALK , v. n. BAz (c. 1. BAzate -zituM), samBAz, vad (c. 1. vadati -dituM), saMvad, Alap, mantr, kaTozakaTanaM kf. See To CONVERSE.

TALK , s. kaTopaTanaM, saMvAdaH, samBAzA -zaRaM, AlApaH, kaTA, kaTAprasaNgaH, see CONVERSATION; ‘small talk,’ laGuBAzaRaM; ‘fine talk,’ Sabda- pARqityaM; ‘mere talk,’ vANmAtraM. — (Report) vadantiH -ntI f.

TALKATIVE , a. vAvadUkaH -kA -kaM, kaTanaH &c. See LOQUACIOUS.
TALKATIVENESS: (1) bahuBAzitA, etc.;(2) by adj.

TALKER , s. vaktA m. (ktf), kaTakaH, BAzI m. (n), AlAzI m., vAdI m.

TALLOW-CHANDLER , s. govapAvikrayI m. (n), mezAdivapAvyApArI m.
Tally, v. i. saM-vad 1 P, tulya-anurUpa-anu-guRa a. BU 1 P; ‘t(ally)ing of hands’ akzara-saMvAdaH. s. Match, q. v.
TALLY (v.): saMvadati (vad, c. 1.): v. To agree, fit.
TALLY (subs.): I Match: q. v.: anurUpa (f. pA). II *vyavahAradaRqaH.
TALMUD: ihudIyasaMhitA.
Talon, s. naKaH-KaM, naKaraH-raM.
TALON: naKaraH: v. Claw.
TALON , s. naKaH, naKaraH, kararuhaH, karajaH. See CLAW.
Tamarind, s. ciMcA, tiMtiqI-qikA, amlikA, Amli(mlI)kA.

TAMBOUR, -INE: qiRqimaH: v. Drum.
TAMBOUR , TAMBOURINE, s. mfdaNgaH, pawahaH. See DRUM.

Tame, v. t. vi-nI 1 P, dam c. (damayati), nigrah 9 P, vaSIkf 8 U; (fury) Sam c. (Samayati). a. vinIta, dAMta, vaSaga, aDIna. 2 grAmya, gfhapuzwa, gfhya-gfha-grAma- in comp.; ‘t(ame) dove’ gfhakapotaH; ‘t(ame) hog’ grAmyaSUkaraH, viwcaraH. 3 nistejas, nazwavIrya; nIrasa, niHsattva; See Spiritless. TAME (adj.): I Of animals:(1) gfhya (f. hyA = domestic: q. v. );(2) grAmya (f. myA = village: q. v. );(3) vinIta (f. tA).II Spiritless: nistejas (mfn.), and sim. comp.s. : v. Also dull.
TAME (v.): (1) damayati (c. of dam), t.ing all: sarvadamana (f. nI), Sa. vii.;(2) vinayati (nI, c. 1.), as if to t. the wild beasts: vanyAn vinezyanniva duzwasattvAn, R. ii. 8.

TAME , a. (Not wild) gfhyaH -hyA -hyaM, gfhyakaH -kA -kaM, grAmyaH -myA -myaM, gfhapuzwaH -zwA -zwaM, CekaH -kA -kaM, ahiMsraH -srA -sraM, gfha or grAma in comp.; ‘a tame pigeon,’ gfhakapotakaH; ‘tame hog,’ grAmya- SUkaraH, grAmaSUkaraH, viqvarAhaH. — (Subdued, trained) dAntaH -ntA -ntaM, damitaH -tA -taM, vaSaH -SA -SaM, aDInaH -nA -naM, SikzitaH -tA -taM, upa- SAntaH &c. — (Flat, spiritless), see the words.

To TAME , v. a. dam (c. 10. damayati -yituM), pradam, krUratAM Sam (c. 10. Sama- yati -yituM), krUratASAntiM kf, krUratAnASaM kf, krUratABaNgaM kf, vaSIkf, nigrah (c. 9. -gfhlAti -grahItuM), sannigrah.
TAMEABLE , a. damanIyaH -yA -yaM, damyaH -myA -myaM, sudamaH -mA -maM.
TAMED , p. p. damitaH -tA -taM, dAntaH -ntA -ntaM, vaSIkftaH -tA -taM, vaSIBUtaH &c., vaSaNgataH &c., SAntaH &c., SAntakrOryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM.
TAMELY: kApuruzavat: v. Meanly.
TAMELY , adv. kApuruzavat, klIvavat, kAtaravat, sakAtaryyaM.
TAMENESS: I Lit.: vinItatA: v. Tame.II Fig.: nistejaskatA: v. Also dullness, mean- -ness.
TAMENESS , s. gfhyatA, vaSatA, vaSyatA, ahiMsratA, vaSIBUtatA.
TAMER: (1) damayitf (f. trI);(2) vinetf (f. trI), etc.
TAMER , s. damakaH, damI m. (n), damanakArI m. See SUBDUER.
TAMING , s. damanaM, damaH, damaTaH -TaM, damaTuH m. See SUBJUGATION.
Tamper (with), v. i. Meddle, q. v. 2 (Witness &c.) kapawena-Calena-vaSIkf 8 U; duz c. (dUzayati), anyaTA kf, vikf.
To TAMPER , v. a. (Meddle), see To MEDDLE. — (Practise secretly) kukarmmasampAdanArTaM gUQavyavahAraM kf or gUQavyApAraM kf or gUQasaMsargaM kf, Calena vyApf in pass. or vyavahf.
TAMPER WITH (v.): I To meddle: q. v.: II To corrupt: q. v.:(1) dUzayati (c. of duz);(2) vaSIkaroti (=get over).
Tan, v. t. SyAmIkf 8 U, saM-DA 3 U, SuD c.; parizkf c. [Tan]ner, s. carmakAraH, carmaSoDana-kft m.

TAN-PIT , s. carmmasanDAnaBARqaM, carmmapAcanaBARqaM, carmmapAcanakuRqaM.

TANGIBLE , a. sparSanIyaH -yA -yaM, spfSyaH -SyA -SyaM, saMspfSyaH &c., sprazwavya -vyA -vyaM, sparSayogyaH &c., sparSArhaH -rhA -rhaM, sparSavedyaH &c., samparkIyaH &c.
Tangle, v. Entangle, q. v. [Tangl]ed, a. jawila, saMmiSra, saMkula, saMkIrRa.
TANJORE , s. (The country) colaH, colAH m. pl.

TANK: I Of water:(1) taqAgam;(2) dIrGikA (long t.);(3) vApI (= square t.);(4) jalASayaH (in gen.).II A vessel: kfRqam.
TANK , s. taqAgaH, jalADAraH, sarovaraH, veSantaH. See RESERVOIR.
Tankard, s. cazakaH.

TANNER: carmaSoDaka (f. DikA) and sim. comp.s.
TANNER , s. carmmakAraH -rI m. (n), carmmAraH, carmmasanDAnI m.
Tantalize, v. t. ASAM-tfzRAM-vfD c., ASAM varDayitvA vipralaB 1 A, jAtASAH KaMq 10 or BaMj 7 P. 2 (general) Cheat, q. v.

Tantamount, a. sama, tulya, samArTaka, tulyArTaka.

TANTRA , s. (A religious treatise, generally in the form of a dialogue between Siva and Durga, teaching peculiar and mystical formulæ for the worship of the deities, or the attainment of superhuman power. These works are very numerous, and their authority in many parts of India seems, in a great measure, to have superseded that of the Vedas) tantraM; ‘a follower of the doctrine taught in the Tantras,’ tAntrikaH.

TAP , s. laGuprahAraH, laDvAGAtaH, IzadAGAtaH, IzatprahAraH.
Tape, s. DIrGapawwaH-baMDanI.

Tapestry, s. citrayavanikA.

TAPIR: a pig-like animal: *tApIqaH.

Tar, s. a-, rAlaH, sarjjarasaH; See Pitch.

TAR , s. saraladravaH, saralarasaH, sarjjarasaH, arAlaH, rAlaH.
TARANTULA: a spider: *tArantakaH.
TARDILY: cireRa: v. Slowly.
TARDINESS , s. mandatA, mAndyaM, vilambaH -mbanaM. See SLOWNESS.
Tardy, a. cirakriya, dIrGasUtrin, maMda; See Slow.
TARDY: (1) cirakriyaH (yA, yaM: of men); [Page701] (2) with cira- in comp. or cireRa or vilambita (= delayed): v. Slow, late.

TARE: I A weed: kakzaBedaH.II In commerce: kzayaH.
TARE , s. kakzaH, SasyakzetraruhaH kakzaBedaH, vanyaGAsaH.
Target, s. kzudracarman n. 2 SaravyaM, lakzyaM-kzaM. [Target]eer, s. carmaDaraH.

Tariff, s. (paRya-)SulkapatrikA.
TARIFF: (paRya) SulkapatrikA and sim. comp.s. (?).

TARNISHED , p. p. malinitaH -tA -taM, kalaNkitaH &c., dUzitaH -tA -taM.
Tarpaulin, s. sarjarasaliptaM SARaM.
Tarry, v. i. vilaMb, cira(rA)yati (D.); avasTA 1 A.

Tart, a. amla, Sukta. s. amlIya.

TART , a. amlaH -mlA -mlaM, SuktaH -ktA -ktaM. See SOUR, SHARP.
TART , s. (Kind of pie) SazkulI, pizwakaM.

TASK-MASTER , s. kAryyaSAsakaH, kAryyakArayitA m. (tf), karmmaSAsakaH.
Tassel, s. kOSeyasUtragucCaH.

[Taste]less, a. nIrasa, virasa, rasahIna.

TASTE: I The act:(1) svAdaH, -nam, A-;(2) rasaH, -nam. Ph.: to have a t. of: v. To taste.II Flavour, relish:(1) svAdaH, A-; (2) rasaH, so t. of tongue: taTA raso rasajYAyAH, Par. III The sense: rasanam, of t. of sight: rAsanaM, cAkzuzam, Par.IV Critical judgment, liking: ruciH, men have different t. s: BinnarucirlokaH, R.
TASTE (v. t.): (1) svAdayati, A- (c. of svad), to t. blood: SoRitamAsvAdayati, Mu. i. 8.;(2) rasayati (ras, c. 10.), to t. wine: vAruRIM rasayati, Ki. ix. 54.
TASTE (v.i.): svadate (svad, c. 1.), N. iii. 93.

To TASTE , v. a. prAS (c. 9. -aSnAti -SituM), AsvAd (c. 1. -svAdati -dituM), svAd, lih (c. 2. leQi -QuM), avalih, rasam AsvAd, A- svAdanaM kf, rasAsvAdanaM kf, ras (c. 10. rasayati -yituM), rasavedanaM kf, rasaboDaM kf, rasajYAnaM kf, rasanaM kf. — (Perceive by the taste) svAdajYAnaM kf, svAdaboDanaM kf, svAdavedanaM kf.
To TASTE , v. n. (Have a taste or flavor) svad (c. 1. svAdate, svadate), sarasaH -sA -saM BU or as, svAdayuktaH -ktA -ktaM BU or as.

TASTE , s. (The sensation excited by applying any thing to the tongue or palate) svAdaH, AsvAdaH, rasajYAnaM, rasaboDaH, rasavedanaM. — (The sense) rasanendriyaM, AsvAdanaSaktiH f., rasanaSaktiH f., rasanaM, ruciH f. — (Flavor) rasaH, AsvAdaH, ruciH f.; ‘the six tastes,’ zaqrasAH m. pl.; these are, 1. sweet, maDuraH; 2. salt, lavaRaH; 3. pungent, kawuH; 4. bitter, tiktaH; 5. sour, amlaH; 6. astringent, kazAyaH. — (Relish, liking for) ruciH f., aBi- ruciH f., santozaH; ‘that husband was not to her taste,’ sa patiH santozAya tasyA nABavat; ‘according to taste,’ yaTAruci; ‘loss of taste,’ aruciH f., arocakaM; ‘of similar tastes,’ samA- naSIlaH -lA -laM. — (Nice perception, faculty of discerning beauty) rasaH, rasikatA, rasajYatA, rasajYAnaM; ‘devoid of taste,’ arasikaH -kA -kaM, arasajYaH -jYA -jYaM; ‘having taste,’ rasajYaH &c., rasikaH &c., sarasaH -sA -saM, rasI -sinI &c.
TASTE OF (v.t.): I To taste: q. v.: rasayati. II To smack of:(1) svadate with an adj. or adv., t. s of garlic: salaSunaH (nA, naM) svadate;(2) by comp. with svAda (= flavour).
TASTED , p. p. AsvAditaH -tA -taM, svAditaH &c., prASitaH &c., jYAtarasaH -sA -saM, gfhItarasaH &c., rasitaH &c., anuBavarasikaH &c.

TASTEFUL: I Savoury:(1) svAdu (f. also dvI), sand-water is cool and t.: cikiraM SItalaM svAdu, Bha.;(2) rucya (f. cyA = relishing);(3) rucikara (f. rI = 2.);(4) rocana (f. nI = 2.).II Showing good taste:(1) hfdya;(2) hfdaya- grAhin (f. RI) and sim. comp. s.
TASTEFULNESS: I Lit.:(1) svAdutA;(2) rucyatA; (3) rucikaratvam;(4) rocanatvam.II Fig.:(1) hfdyatA;(2) hfdayagrAhitA, and sim. comp.s.
TASTELESS: (1) nIrasa (f. sA);(2) virasa (f. sA);(3) arasa (f. sA);(4) rasahIna (f. nA).
TASTELESS , a. virasaH -sA -saM, nIrasaH &c. See INSIPID.
TASTER: Lit. and fig.: (1) rasayitf (f. trI); (2) svAdayitf (f. trI).
TASTER , s. AsvAdI m. (n), rasAsvAdI m., prASI m., rasI m.
TASTINESS , TASTEFULNESS, s. rasikatA, sarasatvaM, sOrasyaM, rocakatA.
TASTING , s. AsvAdaH -danaM, svAdanaM, prASanaM, rasanaM, lehanaM.

TASTY , TASTEFUL, a. rasikaH -kA -kaM, sarasaH -sA -saM, surasaH &c., rasavAn -vatI -vat (t), rasI -sinI -si (n), rocakaH -kA -kaM, ruciraH -rA -raM, rucyaH -cyA -cyaM, rucikaraH -rA -raM, rasitaH -tA -taM. See SAVORY.
Tatter, s. cIraM, cIracIvaraM, naktakaH, karpawaH; See Rag. [Tatter]ed, a. jIrRa, jarjarita.
TATTER: cIracIvaram: v. Rag. T.ed: jIrRa (f. rRA).
Tattoo, v. t. raMj c. s. pawahapraRAdaH.
TATTOO: I Subs.: pawahapraRAdaH and sim. comp.s.II Verb.: saMraYjayati (ranj, c. 10.) (?).
TAUGHT , p. p. SikzitaH -tA -taM, upadizwaH -zwA -zwaM, aDyApitaH -tA -taM, pAWitaH -tA -taM, jYApitaH &c., vijYApitaH &c., labDavidyaH -dyA -dyaM.

Taunt, v. t. A-aDi-kzip 6 P, niMd 1 P, upAlaB 1 A; See Censure. 2 solluMWanaM-sotprAsena-vad 1 P; ‘enough of t(aunt)ing’ alamalamupAlaBya. s. A-aDi-kzepaH, upAlaMBaH, solluMWanokti f. [Taunt]ing, a. sAkzepa, sopAlaMBaM, AkzepagarBa; See Sarcastic.
TAUNT: I Verb: aDikzipati (kzip, c. 6.): v. To censure, abuse.II Subs.: AkzepaH: v. Censure, abuse.
To TAUNT , v. a. upAlaB (c. 1. -laBate -labDuM), avakzip (c. 6. -kzipati -kzeptuM), Akzip, aDikzip, parikzip, tarj, see To REVILE.
TAUNT , s. AkzepaH, avakzepaH, kzepaH, upAlamBaH. See SARCASM.
TAUNTED , p. p. AkziptaH -ptA -ptaM, avakziptaH &c., upAlabDaH -bDA -bDaM.
TAUNTINGLY: (1) sAkzepam;(2) sADikzepam;(3) sopAlamBam.
Taurus, s. vfzaBaH, -rASiH.
TAURUS , s. (The sign or constellation) vfzaH, vfzaBaH, tAvuriH m.
Taut, a. dfQaM Atata.
TAUTOLOGICAL or TAUTOLOGOUS: t. (expres- sion): punarukta (f. ktA).
Tautology, s. punarukti f. punaruktatvaM, pOna-ruktyaM. [Tautolog]ous, a. punarukta, punaruktaBUta.
TAUTOLOGY: (1) punaruktiH;(2) punaruktam, -tvam (tA).
TAUTOLOGY , s. punaruktiH f., punaruktatvaM, anuvAdaH. See REPETITION.
Tavern, s. gaMjA, SuMqApAnaM, SuMqA; paTikA-SramaH; ‘t(avern) keeper’ SOMqikaH.
TAVERN: paTikASramaH.
TAVERN , s. gaYjA, madirAgfhaM, madyavikrayasTAnaM, see PUBLIC-HOUSE.
TAVERN-KEEPER , TAVERNER, s. SORqikaH, madyavikrayI m. See VINTNER.
Tawdry, a. bahirujjvala, bAhyaSoBana, miTyA-SoBAyukta.
TAWDRY: bahirujjvala (f. lA).
TAWDRY , a. kuSoBanaH -nA -naM, miTyASoBAyuktaH &c., miTyASoBanaH &c.
TAWNINESS , s. piNgalatA, kapilatA, piSaNgatA, tAmravarRatA.
Tawny, a. piMga, piMgala, piSaMga (gI f.), kapila, kaqAra, kadru.
TAWNY: (1) piNga (f. NgA);(2) piNgalaH (lA, laM); (3) piSaNga (f. NgI);(4) kapilaH (lA, laM);(5) kaqAraH (rA, raM);(6) kadru (mfn.).

TAWNY , a. piNgalaH -lA -laM, piNgaH -NgA -NgaM, kapilaH -lA -laM, piSaNgaH -NgA -NgaM, piSaNgI -NginI -Ngi (n), piYjaraH -rA -raM, tAmravarRaH -rRA -rRaM, aruRaH -RA -RaM, kabilaH -lA -laM, kadrUH -drUH -dru, ArUH -rUH -ru, SAvaH -vI -vaM.

Tax, s. karaH, baliH; SulkaH-lkaM, rAjasvaM. 2 BAraH. v. t. karaM nyas 4 P (with loc.) or dA c. (dApayati) or grah 9 U (with abl.). 2 Ayas c., atyaMtaM pIq 10. 3 niMd 1 P, dozaM grah 9 U; See Censure. [Tax]able, a. karArha, Sulka-kara-aDIna. [Tax]ation, s. kara-grahaRaM-ADAnaM, SulkasaMKyApanaM.
TAX: (1) karaH, M. viii. 307.: v. Revenue; (2) SulkaH: v. Custom.
TAX (v.): I Lit.: karaM nyasyati (as, c. 4.) or nidaDAti (DA, c. 3.) (with loc.).II Fig., as to t. one's energies: AyAsayati (nomi.). III To censure: q. v.: anuSAsti (SAs, c. 2.).
TAX , s. karaH, SulkaH -lkaM, rAjakaraH -raM, kAraH, rAjasvaM, see IMPOST; ‘exempt from it,’ akaraH -rA -raM. — (Burthen) BAraH.
To TAX , v. a. karAn dA in caus. (dApayati -yituM), karaM nyas (c. 4. -asyati -situM), sakarIkf. — (Impose a burthen) BAraM nyas. — (Charge, accuse), see the words.
TAX-GATHERER , s. karagrahaH, karagrAhI m. (n), SulkagrAhI m.
TAXABLE: (1) karayogya (f. gyA);(2) karArha (f. rhA), etc.
TAXABLE , a. karADInaH -nA -naM, SulkADInaH -nA -naM, karayogyaH -gyA -gyaM, karadaH -dA -daM; ‘taxable article,’ SulkasTAnaM.
TAXATION: indirect and direct t.: *vyavahitA- vyavahitakaraniDAnam or -sTApanam.
TAXATION , s. karAdinyAsaH, karAdivyavasTApanaM, SulkAdisTApanA.
TAXED , p. p. sakaraH -rA -raM, saSulkaH -lkA -lkaM, karadaH -dA -daM.
TEA: cahA, to take t.: cahAM pibati.
TEA , s. No Sanskrit equivalent, cahA may be used.
TEA-POT , s. cahApAtraM, cahADAraH, cahABAjanaM.

Teach, v. t. aDi-i c. (aDyApayati), Sikz c., paW c., upadiS 6 P, SAs 2 P. [Teach]er, s. aDyApakaH, SikzakaH, guruH, upadezwf m., SAstf m.; ‘religious t(eacher)’ upADyAyaH, AcAryaH. [Teach]ing, s. aDyApanaM, SikzA-kzaRaM, upadeSaH.
TEACH: aDyApayati (c. of i: with double [Page702] acc.), taught you the Vedantas: vedAntAnaDyajIgapat, An. iii. 13.; avyApitasyoSanasApi nItim, Ku. iii. 6.: v. To instruct.

To TEACH , v. a. upadiS (c. 6. -diSati -dezwuM), Sikz (c. 10. Sikzayati -yituM), anuSikz, aBiSikz, aDI in caus. (aDyApayati -yituM, rt. i), paW in caus., SAs &c., see To INSTRUCT. Sometimes the causal expresses the sense of ‘teach;’ as, ‘he teaches to dance,’ narttayati; ‘he teaches to read,’ pAWayati.
TEACHABLE: (1) aDyApanIya (f. yA);(2) SikzArha (f. rhA), etc.
TEACHABLE , a. SikzaRIyaH -yA -yaM, SikzyaH -kzyA -kzyaM. See DOCILE.
TEACHABLENESS , s. SikzaRIyatA, SikzyatA, suSikzyatA.
TEACHER: (1) avyApaka (f. pikA);(2) Sikzaka (f. kzikA);(3) Sikzayitf (f. trI). Religious t.:(1) upAvyAya (f. yI);(2) AcArya (f. ryAnI).
TEACHER , s. upadeSakaH, SikzakaH, aDyApakaH, boDakaH, avaboDakaH, see INSTRUCTOR; ‘of children,’ bAlADyApakaH, see PEDAGOGUE.
TEACHING (subs.): (1) avyApanam (the act);(2) SikzA (= instruction: q. v. ).
TEACHING , s. upadeSaH, SikzA, aDyApanaM. See INSTRUCTION.
TEADIOUSNESS: I Wearisomeness:(1) Keda- jananatvam, -tA;(2) by circumlo.II Slowness: manTaratA.III As of writings: dIrGasUtratA.
Teak, s. arRaH; ‘t(eak)-wood’ arRaM, arRakAzWaM.
TEAK: I The tree: arRaH.II The wood: arRam, -kAzWam.
TEAK , s. (Tree) arRaH, SAkaH, SAkAKyaH, karacCadaH, KarapatraH, arjuno- pamaH, halInaH.
TEAL: a bird: SmarAliH (tiH also -rI or lI).
TEAL , s. (Kind of duck) kalahaMsaH, kAdambaM.
Team, s. yugmaM or by pl.
TEAM: expr. by pl. or with yugya (f. gyA = yoked), t. of oxen: gAvaH; t. of horses: yugyAH (when sense clear).
TEAM , s. (Of horses) raTasaMyojitA aSvaSreRI; ‘of oxen,’ goSreRI.
TEAMSTER: expr. by vAhaka etc. (= driver: q. v. ).

Tear, s. aSru-sru n., bAzpaH, asraM, netrAMbu n. -jalaM-udakaM, nayanavAri, and sim. comp.; ‘with t(ear)s in eyes’ sabAzpaM, sAsraM, bA-zpAkulanayana. a. ‘starting of t(ear)s’ bAzpo-dgamaH, udbAzpatvaM; ‘flood of t(ear)s’ DArASru, aSruDArA; ‘having the eyes filled with t(ear)s’ bAzpAkula, aSrunayana, sAsra, aSrumuKa, aSrupariplutekzaRa, paryaSru. [Tear]ful, a. sabAzpa, sASru aSru-saMkula-pUrRa-paripluta. [Tear]fully, adv. sAsraM, sabAzpaM, sASru.

Tear, s. CidraM, vidaraH, BidA; See Rent. v. t. vi-, dF 9 P or c., vi-, SF 9 P, vidal c., Bid-nirBid 7 P; ‘she tore her hair for grief’ vilalApa vikIrRa mUrDajA (K. iv. 4); ‘t(ear) to pieces’ SakalIkf, cUrR 10. [Tear] down, ava-kfz 1 P, nikfz. [Tear] off, AcCid 7 P, apa-nI 1 P, vyapahf 1 P, nirhf 1 P; ‘t(ear) off the hair’ keSAn ulluMc 1 P; See Pull also; ‘I am unable-to t(ear) myself off from the cane-bower’ nirgaMtuM sahasA na vetasagfhAcCaktosmi (S. 3). [Tear] up, unmUl 10, ut-vi-paw 10, ud-Df 1 P, ucCid, utKan, vyaparuh c. v. i. vidF-viBid- pass. 2 savegaM cal 1 P. [Tear]ing, s. vi-, dAraRaM, viBedanaM, pAwanaM, &c.

TEAR (subs.): I Lit.:(1) aSru (sru, n.), shedding of t. s.: aSrupAtaH, Ve.; her breast starred with t.-drops: aSrubindutArakitapayoDarA, D. ii.; veiled with continuous flow of t.s; aSrusroto- 'vaguRWitaH (tA, taM) D. i.; with cool t.s (i. e. of joy): SiSireRASruRA, D. v.;(2) bAzpaH, -jalam, etc., the throat almost choked with t.s: bAzpa- kuRWakaRWaH, D. v.; drew t. s in the shape of sap from boughs; akarot......srutaSAKArasabAzpadUzitAn, R. viii. 70.;(3) asram(Sram), blinded by t.s: asrAnDatayA, R. xiv. 2.;(4) nayanajalam, and sim. comp.s.II Rent, fissure: Cidram.

TEAR (v.): I To rend, shatter: q. v.: vidArayati (dF, c. 10.).II As letters: Cinatti (Cid, c. 7. = to cut), torn garment: CinnaM vasram; t.s away (or off) in our presence: mizatAmAcCinatti naH, Ku. ii. 46.III To pluck, pull: q. v.IV Move violently: DAvati, pari- (DAv, c. 1.). Ph.: t. open: CitvA unmuYcati (muc, c. 6.): v. To open.

TEAR , s. (Of the eye) aSru n., asru n., aSraM, asraM, vAzpaH, netrAmbu n., netrajalaM, netrodakaM, netrajaM, nayanAmbu n., nayanajalaM, nayanavAri n., nayana- salilaM, vilocanAmbu n., locanAmbu n., rodanaM; ‘tear-drop,’ vAzpa- vinduH m., aSruvinduH m., abvinduH m., aSrukalA; ‘starting of tears,’ vAzpodBavaH; ‘flood of tears,’ aSruDArA, DArASru n.; ‘flow- ing of tears,’ aSrupAtaH, aSrusrAvaH; ‘tears of affection,’ premASru; ‘of joy,’ harzASru n.; ‘to shed tears,’ aSrURi pat (c. 10. pAta- yati -yituM) or sru in caus. (srAvayati -yituM) or vft in caus., vAzpa (nom. vAzpAyate), asra (nom. asrAyate), prarud, rud, rodanaM kf; ‘he shed tears of joy,’ harzAd aSrURy apAtayat; ‘in tears, having the eyes filled with tears,’ jAtASruH -SruH -Sru, aSrulocanaH -nA -naM, aSrunayanaH &c., aSrumuKaH -KI -KaM, vAzpopaplutAkzaH -kzI -kza, vAzpA- vilekzaRaH &c., paryyaSruH -SruH -Sru; ‘interrupted by tears,’ vAzyA- kulaH -lA -laM. — (Rent). see RENT.

To TEAR , v. a. dF (c. 10. dArayati -yituM, c. 9. dfRAti, darituM -rItuM), vidF, avadF, dAraRaM kf, vidAraRaM kf, viBid, see To REND, LACERATE, PULL. — (Tear down, off, out, up), see under To PULL. — (The hair) luYc &c., see To PLUCK.
To TEAR , v. n. (Rush along) mahAvegena cal. — (Be torn or rent) vidF in pass., viBid in pass., see To CLEAVE, DIVIDE, v. n.
TEARFUL: (1) sASru (mfn.);(2) paryaSru (mfn.); (3) aSrusaNkula (f. lA);(4) sabAzpa (f. zpA), etc.
TEARFUL , a. sASruH -SruH -Sru, sAsruH &c., sASraH -SrA -SraM, sAsraH &c., savAzpaH -zpA -zpaM, aSrupUrRaH -rRA -rRaM, vAzpyapUrRaH &c., aSrumayaH -yI -yaM.
TEARFULLY , adv. savAzpaM, sASraM, sAsraM, vAzpAkulavAcA, sASrupAtaM.
TEARING , s. dAraRaM, vidAraRaM, vidAraH, viBedaH -danaM, pAwanaM.
TEARLESS: (1) niraSru (mfn.) and sim. comp.s.
Tease, v. t. du 5 P, kzuB c., ard 1 P or c., bAD 1 A, pIq 10; See Injure.
TEASE: kzoBayati (c. of kzuB): v. To vex.
To TEASE , v. a. bAD (c. 1. bADate -DituM). See To ANNOY, TORMENT.
TEASED , p. p. bADitaH -tA -taM, pIqitaH &c., vyagraH -grA -graM.
Teat, s. vfMtaM. 2 cUcukaM, stanAgraM.
TEAT: vfntam: v. Also nipple.
TEAT , s. stanAgraM, stanaH, see NIPPLE; ‘having two teats,’ dvistanI.
Technical, a. pAriBAzika-sAMketika- (kI f.). [Technical]ity, s. pAriBAzikaSabdaH, pariBAzA. 2 pAriBAzikatvaM. [Technical]ly, adv. pariBAzA-nusAreRa.
TECHNICAL: I Lit.: pariBAzika (f. kI).II As of objection: kUwa- in comp.
TECHNICAL , a. lAkzaRikaH -kI -kaM, pAriBAzikaH &c., sANketikaH -kI -kaM, pariBAzitaH -tA -taM, viSezavidyAsambanDI -nDinI &c.
TECHNICALITY: I Lit.: pAriBAzikatvam (-tA). A t. term: pAriBAzikaSabdaH.III As of objec- -tion: kUwatA or tvam.
TECHNICALITY , s. lAkzaRikatvaM, pAriBAzikatvaM, sANketikatvaM. — (A tech- nical term) pariBAzA, lAkzaRikaH.
TECHNICALLY: (1) pariBAzAnusAreRa;(2) better by adj.
TECHNICALLY , adv. pariBAzAnusAreRa, viSezakalAnusAreRa.
Technology, s. pariBAzA. 2 Silpa-kalA-vijYAnaM; ‘school for t(echnology)’ SilpaSAlA.
TECHNOLOGY: I Of arts: SilpavijYAnam.II Of terms: pariBAzA, general t.: sAmAnyapariBAzA. Mit.

Tedious, a. atidIrGa, dIrGasUtra, dIrGatara; ‘passes the night grown t(edious) by sorrow’ gamayati rajanIM vizAdadIrGatarAM (S. 4). 2 SramAvaha, klAMti-Keda-kara (rI f.). 3 maMda, maMTara, dIrGasUtrin, cirakriya. [Tedious]ly, adv. ati-su-dIrGaM. [Tedious]ness, s. atidErGyaM, SramAvahatA; dIrGatA ex. by (a.).
TEDIOUS: I Tiresome, wearisome: q. v.: klAntikara (f. rI) and sim. comp.s, if it is not very t.: tad yadi nAtiKedakaram, K.II Slow: q. v.: manTara (f. rA).III As a writer: dIrGasUtra (f. trA).
TEDIOUS , a. dIrGasUtraH -trA -traM, atidIrGaH -rGA -rGaM, KedajanakaH -kA -kaM, SramajanakaH &c. See LONG, PROLIX, IRKSOME.
TEDIOUSLY: I So as to tire:(1) expr. by circumlo.;(2) atidIrGam (= very long).II Slowly: manTaram.
TEDIOUSLY , adv. atidIrGaM, dIrGasUtravat, sudIrGaM.
TEDIOUSNESS , s. dIrGasUtratA, atidIrGatA. See IRKSOMENESS.
Teem, v. i. Abound, q. v. 2 bAhulyena utpad c. or pra-sU 2, 4 A. [Teem]ing, a. paripUrRa, pUrRagarBa, AQya, samAkula, AkIrRa, pracura; See Abundant.
TEEM (v.): expr. with, pracuraH (rA, raM): v. To abound, abundant.
To TEEM , v. n. pUrRagarBaH -rBA -rBaM BU, atipUrRaH -rRA -rRaM BU. — (Bring forth abundantly) bAhulyena utpad (c. 10. -pAdayati -yituM) or jan.
TEEMING , part. pUrRagarBaH -rBA -rBaM, paripUrRaH -rRA -rRaM, sampUrRaH &c., pUrRaH &c., Akula in comp., AQya in comp. See PROLIFIC.
TEETH (v.): expr. by danta and a verb udgacCati (gam, c. 1.), jAyate (jan, c. 4.), etc., T.ing i.e. dentition: dantodgamaH.

TEETH , s. pl., dantAH m. pl., see TOOTH; ‘having teeth,’ dantI -ntinI -nti (n), sadantaH -ntA -ntaM, jAtadantaH &c.; ‘having good teeth,’ sudan -datI -dat (t); ‘woman having fine teeth,’ SuBadantI; having discolored teeth,’ arokadantaH &c.; ‘row of teeth,’ dantapaMktiH f.; ‘sensitiveness of the teeth,’ dantaharzaH.
To TEETH , v. n. jAtadantaH -ntA -ntaM BU, udBinnadantaH -ntA -ntaM BU.
TEETHING , s. dantodBedaH, dantodBavaH, dantasPowaH, dantotpattiH f., dantajananaM; ‘time of teething,’ dantodBedanakAlaH.
Teetotal, a. madyanivfttivizayaka. [Teetotal](l)er, s. madyAt nivfttaH, nivfttamadyaH.
Tegument, s. AvezwanaM, AvaraRaM, kavacaH-caM, puwaH-waM.
TEGUMENT: vezwanam, A-, Bha.: v. Covering.
TEGUMENT , s. AvezwanaM, kavacaH -caM, puwaH -wI. See INTEGUMENT.
Telegram, s. vidyutpreritavArtA, vidyutsaMdeSaH-vArtA. Telegraph, s. vidyudyaMtraM vidyudvArtAvahaH.
TELEGRAM: *tAqitI vArttA.
TELEGRAPH: I Subs.: *taqidvArttAvahaH.II Verb.: *tAqitena sandiSati (diS, c. 6.).
Teleology, s. mImAMsA, hetuvidyA.
TELEOLOGY: mImAMsA (?); hetuvidyA (?).
Telephone, s. dUraBAzaRayaMtraM.
Telescope, s. dUradarSanayaMtraM.
TELESCOPE: *dUravIkzaRam, -yantram.
TELESCOPE , s. dUradarSakayantraM, mahAdUradarSakayantraM, dUradarSanayantraM, cAkzuzayantraM, dfzwisADakayantraM.
TELINGANA , s. (The country) anDraH, AnDraH.

Tell, v. t. kaT 10, Acakz 2 A, SaMs 1 P, A-ni-yid c., A-, KyA 2 P or c. (KyApayati) (with dat.); varR 10, kFt 10, Sru c., ni-, gad 4 P, vyA-udA-hf 1 P, aBi-DA 3 U, nirUp 10; See Say also. 2 gaR 10, sa-parisaM-KyA; ‘t(ell) beads’ jap 1 P. v. i. siD 4 P, saPalIBU 1 P, guRaM-kAryaM-kf, yaSaH-sidDiM-dA 3 U. 2 (upon) guRaM-kAryaM-jan c. or utpad c.; avasad c.; apa-ci 5 U, kzi 5 P or c. 2 durbalIkf; See Impair; ‘t(ell)-tale’ sUcakaH, piSunaH, karRejapaH. [Tell]er, s. kaTakaH, AKyAyakaH. [Tell]ing, s. kaTanaM, SaMsanaM &c.

TELL (v.t.): (1) kaTayati (kaT, c. 10.), learnt without being told: akaTitaSikzita (f. tA), K.; when I tell the history of (his) former life: janmAntaravfttantaM mayi kaTayati, K.; that (my) internal wish is told by the eyes: yaccakzuzEva hfdayABilAza kaTyate, K.; whom should I tell: kasya kaTayAmi, K.;(2) Avedayati (c. of vid = inform, narrate), I will t. (you) everything from the beginning: AditaH praBfti sarvaM nivedayizyAmaH, K.: v. To say, relate.
TELL (v. i.): I In good sense: expr. with guRaH (effect) or valaM (strength) dfSyate.II In bad sense with on: durbalIkaroti.
To TELL , v. a. kaT (c. 10. kaTayati -yituM). See To RELATE, NARRATE.
To TELL , v. n. (Take effect) sabalIBU, saPalIBU, sapraBAvaH -vA -vaM BU, siD. — (Hit the mark), see under MARK. — (Tell of) sUc.
TELL-TALE: i.e. informer: sUcakaH.
TELL-TALE , s. sUcakaH, sUcI m. See TALE-BEARER, INFORMER.
TELLER: (1) kaTaka (f. TikA);(2) kaTayitf (f. trI);(3) Avedaka (f. dikA).
TELLER , s. kaTakaH, kaTikaH, AKyAyakaH. See RELATER.
TELLING , s. kaTanaM, upakaTanaM, AKyAnaM, see RELATION, NARRATION.
Temerity, s. sAhasaM, kziprakAritA, asamIkzya-avimfSya-kAritA; See Rashness.
TEMERITY: sAhasam: v. Boldness, rashness.
TEMERITY , s. sAhasaM, duHsAhasaM, vizamasAhasaM. See RASHNESS.

Temper, v. t. saMmiSr 10, saMyuj 10, saMsfj 6 P. 2 mfdUkf 8 U, snigDIkf, pra-, Sam c. (Samayati), laGUkf, laGayati (D.), niyam 1 P; See Moderate. s. SIlaM, prakfti f., sva-, BAvaH; ‘good t(emper)’ suSIlaM, sadBAvaH, sOjanyaM; See under Good. 2 samatA, akzoBaH, asaMBramaH, saMyamaH, rozABAvaH, citta-svAsTyaM, -samatA; ‘to lose t(emper)’ kzuB 4 P, kruD-kup 4 P. 3 Anger, q. v. Temperament, s. prakftiH, svaBAvaH, deha or SarIra-prakftiH or svaBAvaH; ‘of a choleric t(emperement)’ pitta-prakfti. Temperate, a. pari-, mita, samaryAda, niyata. 2 pra-, SAMta, akzubDa, DIra, ako-pana, acaMqa. 3 saMyata, saMyamin, saMyatavftti, saMyamaSIla; ‘t(emperate) in eating’ mitAhAra, alpA-hAra, mitASin, saMyatAhAra; ‘t(emperate) in drinking’ &c.; See Moderate. 4 sama-SItozRa, maMdozRa. [Temperate]ly, adv. DIraM, SAMtyA, akzoBeRa, nirudvegaM, SAMtacetasA. Temperance, s. saMyamaH, nigrahaH, parimitatA, niyamaH, niyatatvaM, mitAhAraH, mitASanaM, mita-pAnaM, pAnAprasakti f., &c.
TEMPER (v.): I To mix: q. v.: saMmiSrayati (miSr, c. 10.).II To soften, mollify: snigDI karoti.III Of steel, etc. mfdUkaroti (?).
TEMPER (subs.): I Character, nature: q. v.: SIlam. Ph.: bad t.ed: kopana (f. nA): v. Irritable,II Due mixture: samBedaH.
To TEMPER , v. a. Sam (c. 10. Samayati -yituM). See To MODERATE.

TEMPER , s. (Of mind) SIlaH, prakftiH f., BAvaH, svaBAvaH, saMvedanaM; ‘good temper,’ sadBAvaH, see GOOD-HUMOUR; ‘bad temper,’ asadBAvaH. — (Calmness, moderation) SAntiH f., SAntatA, samatA, saMyamaH, rozABAvaH. — (Anger) rozaH.
TEMPERAMENT: prakftiH: v. Nature, character.
TEMPERAMENT , s. prakftiH f., svaBAvaH, BAvaH, dehaprakftiH f., dehasvaBAvaH, [Page797-b+ 51] SarIraprakftiH f., janmaprakftiH f.; ‘bilious,’ pittaprakftiH f.
TEMPERANCE: perh. saMyamaH, t. in eating and drinking: pAnASanasaMyamaH (?); t. society: pAna- saMyamasaBA (?): v. Moderation.

TEMPERANCE , s. (Moderation) saMyamaH, yamaH, parimitatA, aprasaktiH f. — (In eating) mitASanaM, alpASanaM, mitAhAraH -ritvaM, mitaBojanaM, alpA- hAraH -ritvaM, parimitAhAraH, parimitaBojanaM -jitvaM. — (In drinking) parimitapAnaM, mitapAnaM, alyapAnaM, mAtrApAnaM.
TEMPERATE: I Moderate: q. v.: mita (f. tA).II Cool, calm: q. v.: SAnta (f. ntA). III Continent: q. v.: saMyata (f. tA), perh.: t. zone: *nAtiSItozRamaRqalam.

TEMPERATE , a. (Moderate) saMyamI -minI &c., saMyataH -tA -taM, saMyata- vfttiH -ttiH -tti, saMyamaSIlaH -lA -laM, see MODERATE. — (In de- sires) alpAkAMkzI -kziRI &c., aprasaktaH -ktA -ktaM, jitendriyaH -yA -yaM. — (In eating) mitASanaH -nA -naM, parimitAhAraH -rA -raM, mitA- hAraH &c., mitAhArI -riRI &c., yatAhAraH &c., alpAhAraH &c., alpAhArI &c., svalpAhAraH &c., mitaBojI &c., niyatAhArI &c., laGvAhAraH -rA -raM, laGvAhArI &c., alpASI &c., mitASI &c. — (In drinking) mitapAyI &c., parimitapAyI &c., alpapAyI &c., mitapAnI &c., pAnAprasaktaH -ktA -ktaM. — (Not excessive) parimitaH -tA -taM, atIvraH -vrA -vraM. — (Moderately warm) IzaduzRaH -zRA -zRaM, mandozRaH &c., acaRqaH -RqA -RqaM, agrIzmaH -zmA -zmaM. — (Calm, not violent) SAntaH -ntA -ntaM, arozaRaH -RA -RaM, SAntiprayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, acaRqaH -RqA -RqaM, DIraH -rA -raM, DEryyaSAlI &c.
TEMPERATELY (1) mitam;(2) SAntam;(3) saMyatam.
TEMPERATELY , adv. arozeRa, akroDena, atIvraM, acaRqaM, SAntyA.
Temperature, s. uzRa-Garma-parimARaM.
TEMPERATURE: uzRamAnam (?) DarmaparimARam (?) etc.
TEMPERATURE , s. uzRAnuzRamAnaM, uzRAnuzRapramARaM, uzRaSItamAnaM, uzRA- nuzRatA, uzRamAnaM, uzRapramARaM, grIpmAgrIpmatA.
TEMPERED , p. p. SamitaH -tA -taM, upaSamitaH &c., niyamitaH -tA -taM.
TEMPEST-TOST , TEMPEST-BEATEN, a. pavanAhataH -tA -taM, pavanakziptaH -ptA -ptaM, pavanAGAtapreritaH &c., vAtyAvegapreritaH &c., anilasaMkzubDaH &c.

Temple, s. devAlayaH, devatAyatanaM-niketanaM, sidDAyatanaM, devagfhaM-BavanaM-maMdiraM; and sim. comp.; maWaH, vihAraH (‘Jaina t(emple)’); ‘endowment of a t(emple)’ devasvaM. 2 kuMBaH, kapolaH, SaMKaH.

TEMPLE (subs.): I A sacred building:(1) devAlayaH and sim. comp.s, t. of Śiva: SivAyatanam Vet. 20.; empty t.: SUnyaM devakulam, Mr. ii.; t. of the mistress of the world (Durgā): BuvaneSvarI- devatAlayaH, Bh.; t. of Viṣṇu: vizRorniketanam, Kaj.: v. House, edifice;(2) sidDAyatanam, t. of Śiva: SUlapAReH sidDAyatanam K.;(3) maWaH, P.;(4) vihAraH (of Buddhas).II Of the head:(1) SaNKaH;(2) kumBaH.

TEMPLE , s. (Building dedicated to a deity) mandiraM, prAsAdaH, deva- mandiraM, devAlayaM, devagfhaM, devaBavanaM, maRqapaH -paM, devAgAraH -raM, devaveSma n. (n), devatAmandiraM, BajanAlayaM, devatAgAraH -raM, devatAyatanaM, devAvAsaH, mahAlayaH -yaM, surasTAnaM, suramandiraM, suragfhaM, devakulaM, yajYiyaSAlA, vIhAraH, vayunaM, vicCardakaH, vicCandakaH, svastikaH, sarvatoBadraH, nandyAvarttaH, rucakaH; ‘temple dedicated to Siva,’ SivAlayaM, SivamandiraM; ‘open temple,’ maRqapaH; ‘endowments of a temple,’ devasvaM; ‘worship at the entrance of a temple,’ dvArapUjA. — (Of the head) kapolaH, kenAraH, SaNKaH, SaNKakaH -kaM.
Temporal, a. Ehika-sAMsArika-EhalOkika-prApaMcika-lOkika- (kI f.).
TEMPORAL: I Worldly: q. v.: sAMsArika (f. kI).II Of the temple of the head: by comp., t. region: kumBadeSaH.
TEMPORAL , a. EhikaH -kI -kaM, EhalOkikaH -kI -kaM, lOkikaH &c., sAMsArikaH &c., dfzwArTaH -rTA -rTaM. See SECULAR.
TEMPORARILY: (1) svalpakAlam and sim. comp.s.
TEMPORARILY , adv. alpakAlamAtraM, kzaRamAtraM, acireRa, aSASvataM.
TEMPORARINESS , s. anityatA, acirasTAyitA, kzaRikatA.
Temporary, a. acirasTAyin, acira-alpa-kAlika (kI f.), aSASvata (tI f.), a-sanAtana (nI f.), acira, anitya, kzaRika. [Temporar]ily, adv. svalpakAlaM, aciraM, aSASvataM.
TEMPORARY: (1) acirasTAyin (f. nI);(2) svalpakAlika (f. kI); etc.: v. Also transient.
TEMPORARY , a. acirasTAyI -yinI -yi (n), acirakAlikaH -kA -kaM, aciraH -rA -raM, anityaH -tyA -tyaM, aSASvataH -tI -taM, kzaRikaH -kA -kaM.
Temporize, v. i. yaTAkAlaM-yaTAsamayaM-vyavahf 1 P, CaMdonuvft 1 A. [Temporiz]ing, a. samayAnu-vartin, kAlAnuroDin.
TEMPORIZE: I To be a time-server: Cando- 'nuruRadDi (ruD, c. 7.) or anuvartate (vft, c. 1.). II To delay: q. v.: vilambate (lamb, c. 1.).
To TEMPORIZE , v. n. samayAnuroDaM kf, samayAnuvarttanaM kf, kAlAnuroDaM kf.
TEMPORIZER: (1) Cando'nuroDin (f. nI);(2) samayAnuvartin (f. nI); etc.
TEMPORIZER , s. samayAnuroDI m. (n), kAlAnuroDI m., kAlAnuvarttI m.

sanskrit.slp1: vikArahetO sati vikriyaMte yezAM na cetAMsi ta eva DIrAH
sanskrit.word: विकारहेतौ सति विक्रियंते येषां न चेतांसि त एव धीराः
sanskrit.iast: vikārahetau sati vikriyaṃte yeṣāṃ na cetāṃsi ta eva dhīrāḥ

details.body: Tempt, v. t. pra-vi-luB c., vi-A-kfz 1 P, vi-, muh c.; See Allure. 2 parIkz 1 A. [Tempt]ation, s. pra-vi-loBanaM, AkarzaRaM, vikArahetuH, vikArahetO sati vikriyaMte yezAM na cetAMsi ta eva DIrAH (K. i. 59) ‘there being t(emptation)s &c.’; ‘liable to t(emptation)s’ praloBanAspadaM. [Tempt]er, s. pra-vi-loBakaH, mohakaH. [Tempt]ing, s. Akarzin, vi-, mohin, praloBin.
TEMPT: I To allure, entice: q. v.: praloBayati (c. of luB).II To attempt, try: q. v.

To TEMPT , v. a. (Entice to evil) praluB (c. 10. -loBayati -yituM), pari- luB, luB, Akfz (c. 1. -karzati -karzwuM), muh (c. 10. mohayati -yituM), praloBanaM kf, vimohanaM kf. — (Try, prove) parIkz (c. 1. -Ikzate -kzituM), parIkzAM kf.
TEMPTATION: (1) praloBanam;(2) viloBanam, who is not allured by other t. s: ahftasya viloBanAntarEH, R. viii. 69.
TEMPTATION , s. (Enticement to evil) praloBanaM, viloBanaM, AkarzaRa, AkfzwiH f., mohaH -hanaM, vimohanaM. — (Trial) parIkzA.
TEMPTED , p. p. praloBitaH -tA -taM, AkfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, mohitaH &c., ‘by avarice,’ loBAkfzwaH &c. — (Tried) parIkzitaH -tA -taM.
TEMPTER: (1) praloBaka (f. BikA);(2) viloBaka (f. BikA).
TEMPTER , s. praloBakaH, viloBakaH, mohakaH, parIkzakaH, parIkzAkfta.
TEMPTING , a. AkarzakaH -kA -kaM, vimohanaH -nA -naM. See ENTICING.
Ten, a. daSan; ‘in t(en) ways’ daSaDA; ‘t(en) times’ daSakftvaH. [Ten]th, a. daSama (mI f.).
TEN: daSan (mfn.), t.-armed: daSaBujaH (jA, jaM); twice t.: dvidaSAH; in t. ways: daSaGA; t. times: daSakftvaH, daSavArAn; in the t. quarters: daSasu dikzu R. viii. 29.
TEN , a. deSa m. f. n. pl. (n), daSakaH -kA -kaM, daSasaMKyakaH -kA -kaM; ‘aggregate of ten,’ daSakaM; ‘ten days,’ daSAhaM; ‘in ten ways,’ daSaDA.
Tenable, a. rakzaRIya, pratipAdanIya.
TENABLE: (1) rakzaRIya (f. yA);(2) by verb.: v. To keep.
TENABLE , a. rakzaRIyaH -yA -yaM, pratipAdanIyaH &c., sTApanIyaH &c.

Tenacious, a. grAhin, saMlagnaSIla. 2 DAraRAvat; See Retentive. 3 sAgraha, pratini-vizwa, Agrahin; dfQasaMkalpa, svamatAgrahin; See Obstinate. 4 SyAna, sAMdra, cikkaRa. [Tenacious]ness, Tenacity, s. grAhakatvaM, DAraRA-Sakti f. 2 grAhaH; (eko grAhastu mInAnAM), A-, grahaH, aBiniveSaH, dfQatA, SyAnatA.
TENACIOUS: I Pertinacious: q. v.: grAhin (f. RI).II Retentive: q. v.: DAraRAvat (f. tI).III Glutinous: q. v.: SyAna (f. nA).

TENACIOUS , a. (Holding fast) saMlagnaSIlaH -lA -laM, see RETENTIVE. — (Persistent in a course) aBinivizwaH -zwA -zwaM, AgrahI -hiRI &c., dfQaH -QA -QaM, dfQasaNkalpaH -lpA -lpaM. — (Of opinions) svamatA- grahI &c. — (Of life) durmaraH -rA -raM.
TENACIOUSLY: sAgraham: v. Persistently.
TENACITY: I Pertinacity: grAhaH.II Reten- -tiveness: q. v.: DAraRASaktiH.III Glutinous- -ness: SyAnatA, -tvam, A-.
TENACITY , s. aBiniveSaH, AgrahaH, grahaH, dfQatA, DftiH f., DAraRA.
TENANCY: BUmyaDivAsitvam or gfhADivAsitvam (?), a right of t.: BUmyaDivAsADikAraH (?).
Tenant, s. BUmyaDivAsin m.; (in general) gfhanivAsin. v. t. paraBUmiM aDivas 1 P or aDi-zWA 1 P.
TENANT (subs.): BUmyaDivAsin (f. nI) (?), t. of house: gfhADivAsin (f. nI).
TENANT (v.): (1) aDivasati (vas, c. 1.=inha- -bit: q. v. ;(2) BAwayati (=hire: q. v. ).
TENANT , s. aDivAsI m. (n), parasvAmikakzetrADivAsI m., parasvAmikagf- hADivAsI m., parasvatvayuktaBUmyaDivAsI m.
To TENANT , v. a. parasvAmikaBUmim aDivas (c. 1. -vasati -vastuM).
TENANTED , p. p. aDyuzitaH -tA -taM, aDizWitaH &c. See OCCUPIED.
TENANTRY: aDivAsivargaH and sim. comp.s (?).
TENANTRY , s. parasvAmikakzetrADivAsinAM gaRaH, aDivAsigaRaH.
TENCH: matsyaviSezaH.

Tend, v. i. pravaRI-BU 1 P, pravft 1 A, pravah 1 P, uddiS 6 P, aBisaM-DA 3 U; oft. by Alu, SIla in comp.; ‘t(end)ing to fall’ patayAlu, patanaSIla, pipatizu; ‘t(end)ing to the same object’ taduddizwa; ‘t(end)s to the centre’ keMdrABimuKIBavati. 2 (to) Avah 1 P; kxp 1 A, saMpad 4 A (with dat.), (nizpannaprAyamapi praBuprayojanaM na me DftimAva-hati Rat. 1); kalpase rakzaRAya &c.; oft. by dat. with or without BU; See Lead. v. t. car c., pA c. (pAlayati), rakz 1 P (of cattle only). [Tend]ency, s. pravftti f., prava-RatA, prAvaRyaM, svaBAvaH, SIlatA-AlutA in comp.

TEND: I To take care of:(1) cArayati (c. of car,: only of cattle, etc.), t. ing cattle at distance: cArayanto dUre gAH, V. p. v. 9. 3.;(2) pAlayati (pAl, c. 10.: gen.), t.ing cattle: gAH pAlayantO v. p. v. 8. 1.II To conduce; (1) kalpate, pari- (kxp, c. 1.), and tend to their protection: kalpase rakzaRAya, Sa. v. 8.;(2) upapadyate (pad, c. 4.), t.s to my state: madBAvAyopapadyate, G. xiii. 18.III Direct, aim: q. v.
To TEND , v. a. pAl, rakz, see under To KEEP; ‘cattle,’ gopAlanaM kf.

To TEND , v. n. (Aim at, be directed or incline towards) aBi- sanDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM), uddiS (c. 6. -diSati -dezwuM), aBipre (c. 2. aBiprEti -tuM, rt. i), pravaRaH -RA -RaM BU; ‘act which tends to a main object,’ pratyutkramaH, pratyutkrAntiH f., prayogArTaH. — (Conduce, contribute), see the words.
TENDENCY: (1) pravaRatA or prAvaRyam;(2) svaBAvaH.
TENDENCY , s. prAvaRyaM, pravaRatA, pravfttiH f., pravAhaH, SIlatA or AlutA in comp., see INCLINATION; ‘to descend,’ aDogatiSIlatA.

sanskrit.slp1: karuRArdrARi satAM Kalu Bavanti sadA cetAMsi
sanskrit.word: करुणार्द्राणि सतां खलु भवन्ति सदा चेतांसि
sanskrit.iast: karuṇārdrāṇi satāṃ khalu bhavanti sadā cetāṃsi

details.body: Tender, a. sukumAra, komala, mfdu, pelava; See Delicate, Soft. 2 sulaBavedana-duHKa, duHKajYa, mfdu. 3 bAla, kOmAra (rI f.). 4 sadaya, karuRArdra, karuRa, snigDa, dayAlu; ‘t(ender)-hearted’ karuRAtmaka, komala-mfdu-citta, klinnahfdaya, dayArdracitta. v. t. upAnI 1 P, upahf 1 P. 2 upakzip 6 P, upanyas 4 U. s. upanyAsaH, prastAvaH. [Tender]ly, adv. sakaruRaM, sadayaM, sAnukaMpaM, sAdaraM, karuRArdradfzwyA [Tender]ness, s. mArdavaM, komalatA, snigDatA, kAruRyaM, dayAlutA, vAtsalyaM, &c.

TENDER (adj.): I Soft, delicate: q. v.: sukumAraH (rA, raM), delicate weapon: sukumAramastram, K.; in this t. age: asmin sukumAravayasi. [Page704] II Compassionate, kind: q. v.: t. sentiment: karuRo rasaH, U.; the hearts of good men are always t.: karuRArdrARi satAM Kalu Bavanti sadA cetAMsi.
TENDER (v.): upanayati (nI, c. 1.): v. To offer.
TENDER (subs.): upanyAsaH: v. Offer.

TENDER , a. (Soft) komalaH -lA -laM, mfduH -dvI -du, ArdraH -rdrA -rdraM. — (Sensible of pain) sulaBaduHKaH -KA -KaM, suduHKitaH -tA -taM, see SORE. — (Delicate) sukumAraH -rA -raM, kOmAraH -rI -raM, pelavaH -vA -vaM, mfduH &c.; ‘having a tender frame,’ prakftipelavaH -vA -vaM, mfdvaNgaH -NgI -NgaM. — (Young) bAlaH -lA -laM, kOmAraH -rI -raM. — (Compas- sionate) dayAluH -luH -lu, kAruRikaH -kI -kaM, ArdraH -rdrA -rdraM, dayArdraH &c., sahArdaH &c., see PITIFUL.

TENDER-HEARTED , a. karuRAtmakaH -kA -kaM, komalacittaH -ttA -ttaM, koma- lAntaHkaraRaH -RA -RaM, komalahfdayaH -yA -yaM, sadayahfdayaH &c., dayArdra- BAvaH -vA -vaM, dayArdracittaH &c., klinnahfdayaH &c., klinnahfd, BAvArdraH &c.
TENDERLY: I Softly: q. v.: snigDam.II Kindly: q. v.: karuRam.
TENDERLY , adv. sakaruRaM, sakAruRyaM, karuRaM, sadayaM, sAnukampaM.
TENDERNESS: I Softness: q. v.: sOkumAryam.II Kindness: q. v.: karuRA.
TENDERNESS , s. (Softness) komalatA -tvaM, mfdutA, mArdavaM, sOkumAryyaM, kOmAraM, ArdratA. — (Compassion, kindness) kAruRyaM, karuRA, kfpA, dayA, anukampA, dayAlutA, vAtsalyaM, see PITY.
TENDINOUS: SirAla (f. lA): v. Sinewy.
TENDINOUS , a. SirAlaH -lA -laM, SirAmayaH -yI -yaM, snAyumayaH &c.
Tendon, s. Si(si)rA; snAyu f., snasA. Tendinous, a. SirAla; snAyumaya (yI f.)
TENDON: (1) SirA;(2) snAyuH: v. Sinew.
TENDON , s. snAyuH m., snAsA, SirA, sirA, snAvaH, sanDibanDanaM, granTi- banDanaM, nAqI, see MUSCLE; ‘of the neck,’ manyA.
Tendril, s. taMtuH; (of creepers) pratAnaM, kisalayaH-yaM; See Shoot.
TENDRIL: tantuH (=thread).
TENDRIL , s. (Of a vine or creeper) latAtantuH m., tantuH m.
Tenement, s. BavanaM, AyatanaM; ‘earthly t(enement)’ dehaH. 2 sTAvaraM.
TENEMENT: I In law: sTAvaram.II A house: Bavanam.
TENEMENT , s. AyatanaM, BavanaM, see DWELLING; ‘earthly,’ dehaH.
Tenet, s. mataM, aBiprAyaH.
TENET: matam: v. Opinion, doctrine.
TENET , s. mataM, sammataM, tattvaM, sTitiH f. See OPINION, DOGMA.
TENFOLD: expr. by adj. daSaguRa (f. RA).
TENFOLD , a. daSaguRaH -RA -RaM, daSaviDaH -DA -DaM, daSaDA indec.
TENNIS: krIqAviSezaH, t. ball: *vikzepakandukaH.
TENOR: I Lit.: BAvaH: v. Purport.II In music: maDyamasvaraH (?).
TENOR , s. (Course, drift) kramaH, anvayaH, prasaNgaH, pravAhaH, aBiprAyaH, tAtparyyaM, nidarSanaM. — (Voice) maDyasvaraH.
Tenour, s. BAvaH, BAvArTaH, aBiprAyaH, tAtparyaM. 2 kramaH, anvayaH.
Tense, s. kAlaH. a. Atata. [Tens]ion, s. A-, tati f.
TENSE (subs.): kAlaH (=time): v. Grammar.
TENSE (adj.): Atata (f. tA): v. Stretch.
TENSE , a. AtataH -tA -taM, tataH &c. See STRETCHED, TIGHT.
TENSE , s. (In grammar) kAlaH; ‘Present,’ varttamAnakAlaH; ‘Pre- terite,’ atItakAlaH; ‘Imperfect,’ adyatanaBUtakAlaH.
TENSION: I Lit.: AtatiH (?).II Severity, rigour: q. v.
TENSION , s. AtatiH f., AtatatvaM, tatiH f., aSETilyaM. See TIGHTNESS.
Tent, s. vastra-pawa-veSman n., dUzyaM-SyaM, pawamaMqapaH-gfhaM; ‘royal t(ent)’ upakAryA, upakArikA; ‘pitch a t(ent)’ dUzyaM rac 10 or upa-kxp c.

TENT (subs.): I Of canvas:(1) pawaveSman (n.) and sim. comp.s, in the way the lord's stays were in t.s: paTi praBornivAsAH pawaveSamaBirbaBuH Si. xii. 63.:(2) dUzyam, Si. xii. 65.II Roll of lint: perh. pawwaH.

TENT , s. dUzyaM, dUSyaM, pawamaRqapaH, pawagfhaM, pawavaSma n. (n), pawavAsaH, pawa- kuwiH f., vastragfhaM, SiviraM, sPulaM, potAcCAdanaM, gulmI, keRikA, kuwaru n., guRalayanikA; ‘tent-maker,’ dUzyanirmmARajIvI m.; ‘outer tent, or screen surrounding a tent,’ javanikA, yavanikA.
Tentative, a. parIkzArTaM kfta, tatkAlopayukta.

TENTH: I Adj.: daSamaH (mI, maM), t. (in descent) from Prajāpati: daSamaH prajApateH. Mah. i. 70. 1.; Hundred and t.: daSADikaSatatamaH (mI, maM).II Subs.:(1) daSamaH, a t. was collected by (her) lover: daSamakaH saMgfhItaH priyeRa, Li. 24.;(2) daSamAMSaH; (3) daSAMSaH.
TENTH , a. daSamaH -mI -maM; ‘tenth day of the month,’ daSamI.
TENUITY: tAnavam: v. Thinness.
TENUITY , s. tanutA, tAnavaM, sUkzmatA, sOkzmyaM, kzIRatA.
TENUOUS , a. tanuH -nuH -nvI -nu, sUkzmaH -kzmA -kzmaM. See THIN.
Tepid, a. kozRa, kavozRa, IzaduzRa, maMdozRa.
TEPID: (1) kavozRa, kaduzRa, or kozRa (f. zRA); (2) IzaduzRa (f. zRA);(3) kutapaH (pA, paM: rare).
TEPID , a. IzaduzRaH -zRA -zRaM, kozRaH &c., kavozRaH &c., mandozRaH &c., kutapaH -pA -paM, anuzRASItaH -tA -taM. See LUKEWARM.
TEPIDNESS: (1) kavozRatA;(2) IzaduzRatA; etc.: v.
TEPIDNESS , s. kozRatA, kavozRatA, mandozRatA. See LUKEWARMNESS.
Tercentenary, a. triSatavarzAvartin. s. viSatasAMvatsariko viDiH.
Tergiversation, s. vAkCalaM, apalApaH; See Prevarication.
TERGIVERSATION , s. apadeSaH, palAyanaM, apakramaH, parANmuKatA, CalaM.

Term, s. paryaMtaH, aMtaH. 2 maryAdA, avaDiH, sImA; ‘the utmost t(erm)’ paramAvaDiH; ‘t(erm) of life’ AyurmaryAdA, AyuHsImA; ‘the t(erm) of life is small’ svalpaM AyuH. 3 kAryanirvAhasamayaH-kAlaH. 4 padaM, SabdaH, saMjYA. 5 vyavahAraH, vftti f., BAvaH; ‘on friendly t(erm)s’ mitraBAvena, sadBAvena, prItyA, suKena; ‘ill t(erm)s’ aprIti f., viroDaH, asaMtozaH. 6 (Math.) padaM. 7 avayavaH (of a syllogism). 8 (‘T(erm)s’) samayaH, saMketaH, saMvid f., pratijYA. v. t. AKyA 2 P, aBiDA 3 U, Ahve 1 P; See Call, Name. [Term]less, a. niravaDi, anaMta. [Term]inable, a. aMtya, sImA in comp. [Term]inal, a. aMtya, aMtima. [Term]inus, s. aMtaH, sIman f. Terminate, v. t. avaso 4 P, samAp c. v. i. samAp pass. [Terminat]ion, s. aMtaH, avasAnaM, pariRAmaH, nizWA, samApti f., nivftti f. 2 pratyayaH.

TERM (subs.): Limit, end: q. v.: avaDiH. II A period of time:(1) kAlAvaDiH;(2) not expr.;(3) avaDiH (absol.), or if you wait for a term: aTa cedavaDiH pratIkzyate, Ki. ii. 16.III A word: q. v.: here the word paśu: atra paSupadam, Kav. viii.IV In plu. = agreement: q. v.: samayaH, as t.s (have support) in justice: nyAyamavaDaya iva, Ki. xii. 17.V State of intercourse: BAvaH, good t.s: sadBAvaH: v. Friendship; bad t s: asadBAvaH. v. Enmity.VI In arith.: padam, seven t.s: saptapadam, Li. 93.; first t.: vadanam, AdiH Li. 100; etc.
TERM (v.): aBiDatte (DA, c. 3.): v. To call, name.

TERM , s. (Limit, end) antaH, paryyantaH -ntaM, see LIMIT. — (Period) avaDiH m., kAlAvaDiH m., see PERIOD; ‘of days,’ ahargaRaH; ‘utmost term,’ paramAvaDiH m.; ‘of life,’ AyurmaryyAdA. — (Word, expression, appellation) saMjYA, padaM, vAkyaM, SabdaH, vacanaM, aBi- DAnaM, AKyA, nAma n. (n), padDatiH f. — (Conditions) saNketaH, pratijYA, niyamaH, niyamavAkyaM. — (State of intercourse) vyavahAraH, vfttiH f., paricayaBAvaH, paricayaH; ‘good terms,’ prItiH f., mEtryaM, saMvittiH f.; ‘ill terms,’ vituzwaM, atuzwiH f., aprItiH f. — (Time of business) vyavahArakAlaH, kAryyanirvAhakAlaH, see SESSION. — (Of a syllogism) avayavaH. — (Of an arithmetical series) padaM; ‘first term,’ AdipadaM, muKaM; ‘last term,’ antyapadaM.
To TERM , v. a. aBiDA, AKyA. See To NAME, CALL, STYLE.
Termagant, s. atikalahapriyA, karkaSA, caMqI; See Shrew, Scold.
TERMAGANT: durdAntakalahapriya (f. yA) and sim. comp.s. (?).
TERMAGANT , s. karkaSA, caRqI, duzwA. See SCOLD, SHREW.
TERMED , p. p. aBihitaH -tA -taM, smftaH &c. See NAMED, CALLED.
TERMINABLE , a. samaryyAdaH -dA -daM, pariCedanIyaH &c., see LIMITABLE.
TERMINAL: (1) antya (f. ntyA): v. Last;(2) sImA in comp.: v. Boundary.
TERMINAL , a. antasTaH -sTA -sTaM, pAryyantaH -ntI -ntaM, AntaH -ntI -ntaM.
TERMINATE: I Intrans.: expr. by subs., t.ing syllable: antyavarRaH: v. To end.II Trans.: samApayati (c. of Ap): v. To finish.
To TERMINATE , v. a. or n. avaso. See To END, CLOSE, LIMIT.
TERMINATION: (1) antam: v. End.;(2) ava- sAnam: v. Conclusion.
TERMINATION , s. avasAnaM, antaH, avaDiH m., pariRAmaH, nizWA, see END, CONCLUSION. — (In grammar) antaH, antyavarRaH.
Terminology, s. pariBAzA.
TERMINOLOGY: pariBAzA, Mit.
TERMLESS , a. niravaDiH -DiH -Di, anantaH -ntA -ntaM. See ENDLESS.
TERN: jalakukku waviSezaH.
TERNARY: T. number: trikam.

TEROUGHOUT (adv.): (1) sarvatra (= everywhere), in this poem the metre t. is mandAkrAntA: atra kAvye sarvatra mandAkrAntAvfttam, M. n. on Me.;(2) Adyantam (= from beginning to end);(3) aSezataH (= entirely: q. v.).
Terpsichorean, a. nftyasaMbaMDin.
Terrace, s. aliMdaH, -BUmi f., praGA(Ga)RaH. 2 Roof, q. v. 3 vitardi f., vedikA.
TERRACE: I Balcony: alindaH.II Roof: CadiH (m.).III Raised ground: perh. vapra (mn.).

TERRACE , s. (Before a house) AlindaH, alindaH, praGARaH, praGaRaH, gfhatawI, vITiH -TI f., dehalI -liH f. — (On the roof of a house) prAsAdapfzWaM, awwAlaH -likA, tamaNgakaH, pfzWaM. — (Covered terrace in the yard) vitardDiH f., vedikA.
Terraqueous, a. jalasTalAtmaka.
TERRAQUEOUS: (1) jalasTalamayaH (yI, yaM);(2) jalasTalAtmaka (f. tmikA); etc.
TERRAQUEOUS , a. jalasTalamayaH -yI -yaM, jalasTalAtmakaH -kA -kaM.
Terrene, Terrestrial, a. pArTiva (vI f.), BOmika (kI f.), BOma (mI f.), BU in comp. 2 lOkika, EhikaH (kI f.); See Worldly. 3 BUcara, sTalaja, BUlokasTa; ‘t(errestrial) globe’ BUgolaH.

TERRENE, TERRESTRIAL: I Pertaining to earth:(1) by comp., t. globe: BUgolaH;(2) pArTivaH, (vI, vaM);(3) BOmaH (mI, maM).II Rela- -ting to this life:(1) EhikaH (kI, kaM);(2) sAMsArikaH (kI, kaM);(3) lOkikaH (kI, kaM).

TERRESTRIAL , TERRENE, a. (Sublunary) lOkikaH -kI -kaM, EhalO- kikaH &c., see MUNDANE. — (Earthen, earthly) BOmaH -mI -maM, BOmikaH -kI -kaM, see EARTHLY, EARTHEN. — (Going or existing on the earth) BUcaraH -rI -raM, sTalacaraH &c., BUmijaH -jA -jaM, sTalajaH &c., BUlokasTaH -sTA -sTaM; ‘terrestrial globe,’ BUgolaH -lakaM.
TERRIBLE: (1) GoraH (rA, raM);(2) dAruRa (f. RA), ni-: v. Frightful.
TERRIBLE , TERRIFIC, a. BayAnakaH -kA -kaM, GoraH -rA -raM, dAruRaH -RA -RaM, BImaH -mA -maM. See FRIGHTFUL, FEARFUL, HORRIBLE.
TERRIBLY: (1) balavat;(2) gAQam (= deeply); (3) BfSam (= exccedinglyexceedingly).
TERRIER: kukku raBedaH; *BOmikaSvan (m.).
TERRIFIC: (1) BIzaRa (f. RA);(2) BImaH (mA, maM): v. Also terrible.
TERRIFY: BIzayate (c. of BI): v. To frighten.
To TERRIFY , v. a. tras in caus., BI in caus., see To FRIGHTEN.
TERRITORIAL: expr. by comp., t. boundaries: deSasImA, R. xvi. 1.
TERRITORIAL , a. rAzwrIyaH -yA -yaM, rAzwrasambanDI &c., dESikaH -kI -kaM.
Territory, s. pra-, deSaH, rAzwraM, rAjyaM, BUmi f. [Territor]ial, a. rAzwrIya; by (s.) in comp.
TERRITORY: (1) rAzwram: v. Kingdom;(2) deSaH, pra-: Country, province.
TERRITORY , s. rAzwraM, deSaH, pradeSaH, BUmiH f., rAjyaM, aDikAraH.

Terror, s. saM-, trAsaH, BayaM, sADvasaM, SaMkA. 2 BayahetuH-sTAnaM, SaMkAsTAnaM; ‘a t(error) to the wicked’ SaWAn vyaTayitA (Mr. 9). Terrible, Terrific, a. Gora, dAruRa, BIzaRa, BIma, ugra, karAla, vikawa. Terribly, adv. dAruRaM, balavat, GoraM, ugraM. Terrify, v. t. saM-, tras c., BI c.; See Frightful, &c.
TERROR: I Great fear: q. v.: trAsaH, saM-, pari-. II Object of dread: trAsakara (f. rI) and sim. comp.s, a t. even to the sages: trAsajanana- mapi tatvavidAm, Ki. xii. 6.
TERROR , s. trAsaH, santrAsaH, sADvasaM, BayaM. See FEAR, FRIGHT.
Terse, a. lAGavAnvita, saMkzipta, laGupada. [Terse]ness, s. lAGavaM, saMkzepaH.
TERSE: (1) lavu (f. also DvI), Si. ii. 23.;(2) lAGavAnvitaH (tA, taM), Ki. xi. 38.;(3) saMkzipta (f. ptA = brief, concise: q. v. ), Si. ii. 24.
TERSE , a. SudDaH -dDA -dDaM, saMskftaH -tA -taM, saMkziptaH -ptA -ptaM.
TERSENESS: lAGavam: v. Terse.
TERSENESS , s. SudDatA, SudDiH f., saMkziptatA, saMkzepaH, saMskftatvaM.
Tertian, s. tftIyakaH-jvaraH, tryEhikavizamaH (‘t(ertian) ague’).
TERTIAN: tftIyakaH, -jvaraH.
TERTIAN , s. tryAhikajvaraH, tryAhikaH, tftIyakajvaraH, tftIyakaH.
Tertiary, a. tftIyaka, tftIyin.
TESSELATED: vicitra (f. trA: (?).
TESSELATED , a. azwApadAnukAreRa nAnAvarRaprastaraKacitaH -tA -taM.

Test, v. t. parIkz 1 A, (mAyAM mayodBAvya parIkzitosi R. ii. 62), vimfS 6 P, (SAstre prayoge ca mAM vimfSatu M. 1). s. parikzA, vimarSaH, pratIti f. 2 pramARaM; (‘something whereby to t(est)’) nikazaH, nikazagrAvan m.; ‘this should be put to t(est)’ etatpratItirutpAdyA; See Touch.
TEST: I Verb.: parIkzate (Ikz, c. 1.): v. To examine.II Subs.: parIkzA: v. Exa- -mination.III Means of trial:(1) pramARam, you are the only t.: yUyameva pramARam, Sa. v. 25.; (2) by circumlo.

TEST , s. (Trial) parIkzA, -kzaRaM, kazwiH f., upaDA, kapaH -paRaM, AkapaH, nikazaH, pratItiH f., parIkzitaM; ‘this may be put to the test,’ etatparIkzA karaRIyA, etatpratItira utpAdyA. — (Means of trial) parIkzAsADanaM.
To TEST , v. a. parIkz (c. 1. -Ikzate -kzituM), jYA in des. See To TRY.
Testaceous, a. kaMbuviSizwa, SaMKavAsin.
TESTACEOUS , a. SaNKavAsI -sinI &c., kambuviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM, kambusTaH &c.
Testalor, s. mftyuleKakartf m.
Testament, s. mftyuleKaH-patraM, icCApatraM. 2 saMhitA. [Testament]ary, a. mftyupatradatta.
TESTAMENT: I A will: *icCApatrama.II Of the Bible: saMhitA, old: prAcInasaMhitA.
TESTAMENT , s. (Will) mftapatraM, maraRapatraM, mftyupatraM, mftaleKaH; ‘Old Testament,’ purAtananiyamaH; ‘New Testament,’ nUtananiyamaH.
TESTAMENTARY: *icCApatravihita (f. tA) and sim. comp.s.
TESTAMENTARY , a. (Pertaining to a will) mftapatrasambanDI &c. -vizayakaH -kA -kaM. — (Given by a will) mftapatradattaH -ttA -ttaM.
TESTATOR, TESTATRIX: *icCApatrakArin (f. RI) and sim. comp.s.
TESTATOR , s. mftaleKakarttA m. (rttf), maraRaleKakarttA m.
TESTATRIX , s. mftaleKakartrI, mftyuleKakartrI, maraRaleKakartrI.
TESTED , p. p. parIkzitaH -tA -taM, kftaparIkzaH -kzA -kzaM. See TRIED.
TESTICLE: aRqam, -kozaH(SaH); (2) muzkaH;(3) vfzaRaH, t. s: vfzaRO.

TESTICLE , s. aRqaM, muzkaH, vfzaRaH, kozaH -zakaH, koSaH, PalaM, muYcakaH, tIkzRaM; ‘testicles,’ aRqadvayaM, muzkadvayaM, aRqayugmaM, vfzaRadvayaM, vfzaRO m. du.; ‘enlargement of them,’ aRqavfdDiH f., aRqaSoPaH; ‘having them,’ savfzaRaH -RA -RaM, aRqIraH -rA -raM, aRqIlaH &c.
Testicles, s. aMqaH, -kozaH-SaH, muzkaH, vfzaRaH, PalaM (in dual).
Testify, v. t. sAkzyaM dA 3 U, pramARayati (D.), pramARIkf 8 U. 2 prakAS c., vivf 5 U, vyaMj 7 P or c., prakawIkf; Avizkf (by words) brU 2 U, vac 2 P &c.
TESTIFY: I As a witness: sAkzyaM dadAti (dA, c. 3.).II In gen.: bravIti or brUte (brU, c. 2.). if one t.ies falsely: aTa cedanftaM brUyAt, Mit.: v. To tell, speak.
To TESTIFY , v. a. or n., sAkzyaM dA or kf, pramARaM dA, pramARa (nom. pramARayati -yituM). See To DECLARE, CERTIFY, PUBLISH.
TESTIMONIAL: *praSaMsApatram, and sim. comp.s.
TESTIMONIAL , s. pramARapatraM, pramARaleKaH, prAmARikaleKaH.
Testimony, s. sAkzyaM, pramARaM, prAmARyaM Testimonial, s. pramARapatraM-leKaH.
TESTIMONY: sAkzyam, a witness giving false t.: sAkzI sAkzyaM mfzA bruvan, Mit.: v. Also evidence.
TESTIMONY , s. sAkzyaM, sAkzitA, pramARaM, prAmARyaM. See EVIDENCE.
TESTINESS , s. karkaSatA, kArkaSyaM, vakratA, kawutA. See PEEVISHNESS.
TESTY , a. karkaSaH -SA -SaM, kawuH -wuH -wu. See PEEVISH, FRETFUL.
Tetanus, s. DanurvAtaH.
TETANUS: DanuzwaNkAraH.
TETE-A-TETE , s. rahaHsaMlApaH, rahaHsamBAzA, rahaHpratyAsattiH f.
Tete-a-tete, s. rahaH-saMlApaH-pratyAsatti f.
Tether, s. baMDanarajju f. -sUtraM. v. t. (rajjvA) baMD 9 P.
TETHER: I Verb: baDnAti (banD, c. 9.).II Subs.: banDanarajjuH.
TETHER , s. banDanarajjuH m. f., banDanasUtraM, cAraRarajjuH m. f.
To TETHER , v. a. dIrGarajjunA badDvA car (c. 10. cArayati -yituM).
Tetrad, s. catuzwayaM, catuzkaM.
TETRAD: (1) catuzwayam;(2) catuzkam.
TETRAD , s. (Aggregate of four) catuzwayaM, catuzkaM.
Tetragon, s. caturBujaH, caturasraM. [Tetragon]al, a. catu-rasra, catuzkoRa.
TETRAGON , s. caturasraM, catuzkoRaH, caturBujaH.
TETRAGONAL , a. catuzkoRaH -RA -RaM, caturasraH -srA -sraM, caturBujaH -jA -jaM.
TETRARCH: maRqaleSaH (?): v. Chief.
TETTER: dadruviSezaH.
Text, s. mUlaM, mUlapaMkti f., mUlagraMTaH. 2 ukti f., sUtraM, vacanaM, vAkyaM [Text]ual, a. mOlika (kI f.), mOla (lI f.).
TEXT: I Original writing: mUlam, I shall not write any thing outside the t.: nAmUlaM liKyate kiYcit, M. n.II Of scripture:(1) vacanam;(2) Fc (f. of the Rigveda).

TEXT , s. (Subject of a comment) mUlaM, mUlagranTaH, pAMktagranTaH, pratIkaM, nidarSanaM, aBihitatvaM, prayogaH. — (Verse or passage of Seripture) vacanaM, vAkyaM, sUtraM, fk f. (c), viDiH m., pratIkaM, SrutiH f.; ‘of the Vedas,’ vedavacanaM, vedavAkyaM.
Textile, a. tAMtava (vI f.), taMtunirvita.
TEXTILE: (1) tAntava (f. vI);(2) tantunirmita (f. tA), etc.
TEXTILE , a. tAntavaH -vI -vaM, tantrI -ntriRI -ntri (n).
TEXTUAL: (1) by comp.;(2) mUlApekza (f. kzA) and sim. comp.s.
TEXTUAL , a. vAcanikaH -kI -kaM, mOlikaH -kI -kaM.
Texture, s. vinyAsaH, vi-, racanA-naM, Uti f., vApaH-yaH. 2 taMtu-sUtra-guRaH. 3 tAMtavaM.
TEXTURE: I Lit.: tAntavam.II Quality of threads: guRaH.III Arrangement: vinyAsaH.
TEXTURE , s. (Weaving) UtiH f., vApaH, vyUtiH. — (Web, that which is woven) tAntavaM, vastraM. — (Quality of the threads) tantuguRaH, sUtraguRaH.

details.body: Than, conj. Ex. by abl. of word following it; matireva balAdgarIyasI &c.; with ‘better’ ex. by na ca, na tu, na punaH; See Prefer, Better; oft. ex. by apekzya (with acc.), apekzayA in comp.

THAN: (1) by abl., the people of Mathurā are richer t. the people of Pātnā: mATurAH pAwalIputraBya AQyatarAH, S. k.; swifter t. the mind: manaso'pyA- Sutaram, Ki. xiii. 22.; and the king who gave more t. was asked for: nfpo'rTikAmAdaDikapradaSca, R. v. 31.; dearer to you t. I.: mattaH priyatarastava, K.; (2) sometimes by comp., more t. twenty times: aDikaviMSAn vArAn, Au.: v. Also more. N.B. In old books the ins. is often used for the abl.: ko'nvasti duHKitataro mayA duzkftakarmaRA, Ram. ii. 59. 30.

THAN , adv. or conj. Usually expressed in Sanskrit by the abl. c.; as, ‘a store of grain is better than all stores,’ DAnya- saMgrahaH SreyAn sarvvasaMgrahAt; ‘worthier than I,’ asmatto varIyAn. Or by na ca; as, ‘silence is better than speaking un- truth,’ varaM mOnaM na ca vacanam anftaM [i. e. better silence and not speaking untruth]. In modern Sanskrit ‘than’ is often expressed by apekzayA, or apekzya; as, ‘some of the organs of animals are stronger than those of men,’ jantUnAM kAnicid indriyARi manupyApekzayA pravalAni; ‘acid has a stronger attraction for iron than copper,’ amlarasaM tAsram apekzya loham aDikam Akarzati; ‘placing the cup on some place higher than one's head,’ svamastakam apekzya uccatare sTAne pAtraM vinyasya; ‘than him,’ tadapekzayA; ‘than me,’ madapekzayA.

Thank, v. t. upakfta-anugrahIta. a. asmi iti vad 1 P, (‘Say’, q. v.); kftajYatAM dfS c. or Avizkf 8 U, kftopakAraM stu 2 U or praSaMs 1 P; ‘t(hank)ed his deliverer’ BavatAnu-gfhItaH-upakftaH-asmi iti rakzitAramuvAda; ‘(I) t(hank) you’, ‘thanks’ anugrahI-tosmi, mahAnayaM prasAdaH. ‘t(hank) God’ dizwyA. s. (Thanks) kftajYatAdarSanaM-prakASanaM, upakArastuti f., DanyavAdaH; better ex. by (v.) ‘accept my t(hank)s’ by (v.). [Thank]ful, a. kftajYa, kftavedin, upakArajYa, kftajYatAdarSin. [Thank]fully, adv. kftajYatApUrvaM, kftajYatayA. [Thank]less, a. akftajYa, kftaGna. Thanksgiving, s. See (s.).
THANK: DanyavAdaM karoti (?).

To THANK , v. a. DanyaM vad (c. 1. vadati -dituM), kftajYatAkaTanaM kf, kftajYa- tAprakASanaM kf, kftajYatAdarSanaM kf, upakArastutiM kf, prAptopakArastutiM kf, upakArasvIkAraM kf, DanyavAdaM kf; ‘to give thanks to God,’ ISvaraM DanyaM vad, ISvaraguRAn vad, ISvarasya DanyavAdaM kf; ‘I thank thee,’ tvAM DanyaM vadAmi.

THANK , THANKS, s. pl. DanyavAdaH, kftajYatAdarSanaM, kftajYatAkaTanaM, kftajYa- tAprakASanaM, upakArastutiH f., upakArABivAdaH, upakArasvIkAraH; ‘many thanks to you for your kindness,’ anugfhIto'smi tavopakAreRa; ‘thanks to thee for the breakfast,’ kuSalaM te prAtarASasya.
THANKFUL: (1) kftajYa (f. jYA);(2) kftavedin (f. nI); etc.
THANKFUL , a. kftajYaH -jYA -jYaM, upakArajYaH &c., kftajYatAdarSakaH -kA -kaM, kftajYatAkaTakaH &c., kftajYatAprakASakaH &c., upakArABivAdakaH &c., DanyavAdI -dinI -di (n).
THANKFULLY: (1) DanyavAdapuraHsaram, and sim. comp.s (?).
THANKFULLY , adv. kftajYatApUrvvaM, saDanyavAdaM, kftajYavat, upakArajYavat.
THANKFULNESS: (1) DanyavAdaH or DanyavAditA (?): v. Gratitude.
THANKFULNESS , s. kftajYatA, upakArajYatA, upakftajYatA.
THANKLESS: I Of men: akftajYa (f. jYA): v. Ungrateful.II Of work. etc.: yaH (yA, yat) na praSasyate: v. To praise.
THANKLESS , a. akftajYaH -jYA -jYaM, kftaGnaH &c. See UNGRATEFUL.
THANKS: DanyavAdaH (?), thanksgiving: perh. stutipAWaH.
THANKSGIVING , s. DanyavAdaH, kftajYatAkaTanaM, kftajYatAdarSanaM.

details.body: That, s. tad (saH-sA-tat). 2 yat (yaH-yA-yat), oft. by comp.; ‘he t(hat) has strength’ sabala, balin &c. conj. iti (after assertions) yaTA, yat (at beginning) with or without iti; sometimes not ex. 2 (Purpose) iti with pot. mood or arTe-rTaM in comp.; ‘Oh t(hat)’ See Would.

THAT: I Demonstrative pronoun: tad, t. object: so'rTaH, D. iii.; in t. season: tasmin samaye, R. xvi. 53.; narrated all t.: tatsarvamAcaKyO, Mah.: v. Also this. Ph.: (a) t. is to say ......: ityarTaH, tasya yUno'pi vizayavErAgyAdiguRasampattyA jYAnato vfdDatvamAsIdityarTaH, M.n. (N. B. Use......: iti yAvat, when a full explanation is not given, manIziRo viduzo dozajYasyEti yAvat, M. p.); (b) t. is not expr., by object t. is by sound etc. M.n.II Relative pronoun=who, [Page706] which: q. v.III Conjunction, introduc- -ing clauses or sentences as object of the preceding verb.:(1) expr. with iti, would think t. they adore him out of fear: maMsyati BayAdarcanti mAmiti, Mah. v. 88. 3. (note the use of direct speech); t. he might allow the race of Nimi......: diSyatAM kulamidaM nimeriti, R. xi. 49.; we hear t. king has come to the Jana- sthāna: SrUyate rAjA janasTAnamAgata iti, U. iii. (N.B. Sometimes iti is understood as t. in English: “SrUyate tO mahAtmAnO naranArAyaRAvuBO . tapo GoramanirdeSyaM tapyete ganDamAdane ..”, Mah. v. 96. 14.):(2) by acc. after trans. verbs, know- ing t. his end was born: jAnannapi jAtamantamAtmanaH, Si. i. 67.; informed t. a golden shower had fallen from heaven: hiraRmayIM vfzwiM SaSaMsuH patitAM namastaH, R. v. 29.;(3) with yaTA or yat, Vaśisṭha said t. they would go and live in the hermitage of Vālmīki: vaSizWasya vAcaH ‘yaTA vAlmIki- tapovanaM gatvA tatra vatsyAma iti’, U. ii.; this is new rule t. one repents after killing an enemy: ayaM nUtano nyAyo yadarAtiM hatvA saMtApaH krIyate, H. ii. Ph.: granting t. expr. by: astu, stAm, santu.IV Introducing reason etc.: (a) so t.: yaTA... taTA, do so t. (he) hears from your messenger: yaTA tava sandeSaharAcCfRoti taTA viDIyatAm, R. iii. 66.; (b) in order t.: yaTA ..taTA: v. also for (II), to; (c) in t.= because: q. v. Ph.: oh that: expr. with kaccit: v. To wish.

THAT , pron. (Demonstrative) saH sA tat (t), ezaH ezA etat (etat) asO m. f. (adas); ‘that man,’ sa naraH; ‘at that time,’ tasmin kAle, see THEN — (Relative) yaH yA yat (yat) or expressed by a compound; as, ‘the man that has great wealth,’ mahA- Dano naraH, see WHO, WHICH. — (That is to say) arTAt, arTatas. vastutas. — (So that) taTA yaTA, see the next.

THAT , conj. Expressed by taTA yaTA, yaTA, yat, iti or by the accusative case, as in the following examples; ‘do you contrive that I may be liberated from my bonds,’ yaTA mucye banDanAt taTA saMviDAtum arhasi; ‘I did not expect that I should see you again,’ na ma AsId ASaMsA yaTA punarapi tvAM prekzipye; ‘do you not know that I keep watch in the house?’ tvaM na jAnAsi yaTA gfharakzAM karomi; ‘know that it is impossible to stand before him,’ avehi yad aSakyaM tasyAgre sTAtuM; ‘this is a new doctrine, that having killed an enemy remorse should be felt,’ ayaM nUtano nyAyo yad arAtiM hatvA santApaH kriyate ‘the pupils said that they had done their task,’ kftakftpa vayam iti SizyA UcuH; ‘having ascertained that it was a monkey who rang the bell,’ markawo GaRwAM vAdayati iti parijYAya; ‘his idea was that an increase of wealth ought to be made,’ arTavfdDiH karaRIyA iti matir baBUva; ‘reflecting in his mind that I am happy in possessing such a wife,’ Danyo'haM yasya etAdfSI BAryyA iti manasi niDAya; ‘I will inform the Guru that the hour of sacrifice has arrived,’ upasTitAM homavela gurave nivedayAmi; ‘they related that a golden shower had fallen from the clouds,’ hiraRyamayIM vfzwiM naBastaH patitAM SaSaMsuH; ‘thou sayest that my beloved is pining away,’ paryutsukAM priyAM me kaTayasi. — (In order that) expressed by arTaM in comp., or by the dative case; as, ‘what must I do in order that I may get money?’ DanaprApaRArTaM or DanaprApaRAya kiM mayA karttavyaM.
Thatch, s. Cadis f., pawalaM, tfRapawalaM-CadiH. v. t. tfRAdinA A-, Cad 10. [Thatch]er, s. tfRa-pawalakAraH.
THATCH: I Subs.:(1) CadiH;(2) CAdanam; (3) pawalam, A.II Verb.: (tfRAdinA) CAdayati, A-, (c. of Cad), t.ed: tfRAcCAdita (f. tA) and sim. comp.s or simply tfRa- in comp.
THATCH , s. CadiH f., tfRaCadiH f., CAdaM, pawalaM, tfRapawalaM, kawanaM, kuwalaM, kuwaNkaH, gfhAcCAdanI.
To THATCH , v. a. SuzkatfRAdinA or tfRapawalena gfhAcCAdanaM kf.
THATCHED , p. p. tfRAcCAditaH -tA -taM, SuzkatfRaCAditaH -tA -taM.
THATCHER , s. gfhAcCAdanakft m., tfRapawalakAraH, kowakaH.
Thaw, v. i. dru 1 P, vi-lI 4 A. v. t. dru c., dravIkf, vi-lI c.; See Melt. s. hima or tuzAra-sruti f. or srAvaH.
THAW (v.): I Intrans.: dravati (du, c. 1.): v. To melt.II Trans.: dravIkaroti.III Subs.: himasrutiH and sim. comp.s.
To THAW , v. a. dravIkf, vidru in caus., vidrAvaRaM kf. See To MELT, v. a.
To THAW , v. n. dravIBU, dru (c. 1. dravati, drotuM), vidru. See To MELT, v. n.
THAW , s. himadravaH, himadrAvaH, himagalanaM, himakzaraRaM.
