details.body: The, (Article) Ex. by tat (saH-sA-tat) or adas (asO-adaH); gen. not ex. 2 (With compar. adj.) by yaTA yaTA-taTA taTA; yaTA yaTA yOvanamaticakrAma taTA taTA ana-patyatAjanmA avarDatAsya saMtApaH (Ka. 59), ‘t(he) older he grew, t(he) greater his torment’ &c.; ‘t(he) sooner, t(he) better’ yaTA yaTA laGu kAryaM saMpAdyate taTA taTA aDikaM Sreyo Bavet; ‘t(he) more so’ viSezataH, viSezeRa.

THE: I The definite article:(1) not expr., I salute the parents of the world: jagataH pitarO vande, R. i. 1.; the kind said: rAjovAca, H.; in the house of Vasudeva: vasudevasadmani, Si. i. 1.;(2) by demonstrative pronouns, where shall I get the bird: kva prApyate sa patagaH, N. xiii. 40.; the day is advanced: kaWorIBUto'yaM divasaH, U. ii.II Of distinction: by tad or rarely adas, we are the Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa: AvAM tO rAmalakzmaRO, An v.; and you are the Lakṣmaṇa: tvaM punarasO lakzmaRaH, Vi. v.III With comp. adv.s:(1) with yaTA yaTA...... taTA taTA, the closer the sound of the drums came, the more excited the hostile army (became): upAgamadyaTA yaTA pawaharavaH samIpatAM taTA taTA hfzita- vapurdvizAYcamUH, Si. xvii. 43.; “romakUpanivahaM yaTA yaTA nEzaDasya dfgapAttaTA taTA citramApadapatfzRatA na sA”, N. xviii. 124.;(2) with yAvat yAvat......tAvat tAvat, M.n. Ph.: the more so: viSezataH (= specially).

THE . This definite article may be either expressed by the pronoun saH sA tat, or is more usually omitted altogether; as, ‘the man,’ sa puruzaH or puruzaH; ‘the woman,’ sA strI or strI; ‘the lion,’ sa siMhaH or siMhaH.
Theatre, s. raMgaH, -BUmi f., -SAlA, nftya-nAwya-SAlA, nAwakagfhaM. Theatrical, a. nAwaka, nAwya in comp.; ‘t(heatrical) performance’ nAwakaprayogaH.
THEATRE: (1) raNgaH (both lit. and fig.): v. Stage;(2) nAwyaSAlA and sim. comps. (the house);(3) raNgagato janaH and sim. comp.s. (the people).
THEATRE , s. raNgaH, raNgaSAlA, nAwakaSAlA, nAwyaSAlA, nAwakagfhaM, nAwa- kamandiraM, nftyaSAlA, raNgaBUmiH f., samAjasanniveSaH, AnarttaH.
THEATRICAL: (1) expr. by comp., t. tutor: nAwyAcAryaH;(2) nAwakIya (f. yA = dramatic), Si. ii. 8.
THEATRICAL , a. nAwakIyaH -yA -yaM, nAwyasambanDI -nDinI &c., nAwya- vizayakaH -kA -kaM, nAwakasambanDI &c., nAwyaSAlAsambanDI &c.
THEE , pron. tvAM acc. c.; ‘by thee,’ tvayA; ‘to thee,’ tuByaM, te; ‘of thee,’ tava, te.

THEFT: (1) cOryam, to commit t. at night: rAtrO cOryaM karoti, M. ix. 276.; implements of t.: cOryasADanam, Mit.;(2) steyam, and (taking) grass for cattle is not t.: tfRaYca goByo grAsArTam, asteyam, M. viii. 339.;(3) mozaH (rare).
THEFT , s. steyaM, cOryyaM, cOraM, cOrikA, stEnyaM, stEnaM, curA, tAskaryyaM, taska- ratA, muzwaM, muzwiH f., apahAraH, paradravyApahAraH, cOryyakarmma n. (n). See STEALING.
THEIR , pron. tezAM gen. pl. m., tAsAM f., etezAM gen. pl. m., etAsAM f., ezAM gen. pl. m., AsAM gen. pl. f.
Theism, s. ISvaravAdaH, AstikyavAdaH, AstikyaM. Theist, s. ISvaravAdin m., AstikaH.
THEISM: ISvaravAdaH and sim. comp.s.
THEISM , s. AstikyaM, AstikyamataM, AstikyavAdaH, ISvaravAdaH.
THEIST: ISvaravAdin (f. nI) and sim. comp.s.
THEIST , s. AstikaH, AstikyavAdI m. (n), ISvaravAdI m.
THEM , pron. tAn or etAn acc. pl.; ‘by them,’ tEH; ‘of them,’ tezAM.
Theme, s. vizayaH, prakaraRaM, vastu n., prabaMDaH.
THEME: (1) vizayaH: v. Subject;(2) vastu: v. Thing.
THEME , s. (Topic) prakaraRaM, vizayaH, see SUBJECT. — (Short disser- tation) alpaprabanDaH, alpaleKaH, alpaprasaNgaH.
THEMSELVES , pron. Expressed by AtmA m. (n). See MYSELF.

Then, adv. tadA, tadAnIM, tasminkAle. 2 tataH, anaMtaraM, aTa. 3 tarhi; tat; ‘now and t(hen)’ kadApi, kadAcit; ‘so t(hen)’ evaM, tarhi; ‘what t(hen)’ tataH kiM. Thence, adv. tataH, tasmAt, tasmAt sTAnAt; ‘t(hence)-forth’, ‘t(hence)-forward’ tataH praBfti-AraBya, tadApraBfti.

THEN: (1) tadA (of time, rarely of cause), when...t.: yadA...tadA, Ku. v. 18.; t. (he) knew: tadA viveda, Ki. iii. 18.;(2) tadAnIm (of time), but t. by the narration of the story of her life: tadAnIntu svavfttAntakaTanena, K.;(3) tataH (of sequence and cause), t. when your Highness came away: tataH KalvAgate deve, K.; what t.: tataH kim, K.; first of all splendour, t. sound, t. dust: pratApo'gre tataH SabdaH parAgastadantaram, R. iv. 30.; if she does not vanish from my sight, t. I shall ask her all these: tadyadi me darSanapaTAnnApayAti tataH...sarvametadenAM pfcCAmi, K.; and t. (as a question): tatastataH, Mr. ii.;(4) aTa (of sequence at the head of a sentence), t. at [Page707] the end of the song: aTa gItAvasAne, K.;(5) tarhi, (of time and cause: rare), t. the world is learned: tarhi paRqitaH saMsAraH, U. ii.; what t.: kiM tarhi, S. i. 2. 1.;(6) tat (causal), t. how is the gentle Rāma now to be consoled: tat kaTamidAnIM rAmaBadra ASvAsanIyaH, U. ii.
THEN , adv. (At that time) tadA, tadAnIM, tarhi, etarhi, tasmin kAle, tatkAle. — (After that) tataH, aTa, tadanantaraM, tadupari; ‘now and then,’ kadAcit, kadApi, see under Now.
THENCE: tataH and tasmAt (in every sense).
THENCE , adv. (From that place) tatas, tasmAt sTAnAt, tasmAd deSAt. — (For that reason) tasmAt, see THEREFORE.
THENCEFORTH, THENCEFORWARD: (1) tataH praBfti;(2) tadavaDi; etc.
THENCEFORTH , THENCEFORWARD, adv. tataHpraBfti, tadApraBfti, tatkAlA- dAraBya, tata AraBya, tadAraBya, tadavaDi, tatkAlAvaDi.
Theocracy, s. ISvarapraButvaM, ISvarakartfkatvaM.
THEOCRACY , s. ISvarakarttfkarAjyaM, ISvarakarttfkaSAsanaM, ISvarapraButvaM.
Theogony, s. devotpatti f. vaMSaH.
THEOGONY , s. devotpattiH f., devajanma n. (n), devavaMSaH -vaMSAvalI.
THEOLOGIAN: (1) paramArTavid (mfn.: (?);(2) ISvaravijYAnaviSArada (f. dA: (?); and sim. comp.s.
THEOLOGIAN , s. paramArTavid m., paramArTajYAnI m. (n), brahmajYAnI m., brahmavidyAjYaH, aDyAtmajYAnI m., aDyAtmadfk m. (S), SrotriyaH, SrutADya- yanasampannaH, DarmmaSAstrajYaH, vedAntI m.
THEOLOGICAL: expr. by comp., t. subject: aDyAtmavizayaH (?).
THEOLOGICAL , a. paramArTavidyAvizayakaH -kA -kaM, paramArTavidyAsambanDI -nDinI &c., aDyAtmajYAnavizayakaH &c., OpanizadaH -dI -daM.
THEOLOGICALLY: tatvavidyAnusAreRa and sim. comp.s.

Theology, s. ISvara-brahma-jYAnaM, paramArTavidyA, aDyAtma-jYAnaM-vidyA. [Theolog]ian, s. paramArTavid m., ISvarajYAnaviSAradaH, brahma-vid-jYAnin, vedAMtI, aDyAtmavAdI. [Theolog]ical, a. ex. by (s.) in comp., ADyAtmika-pAramArTika- (kI f.).
THEOLOGY: (1) paramArTavidyA (?);(2) ISvaravijYAnam; (3) tattvajYAnam.
THEOLOGY , s. paramArTavidyA, paramArTajYAnaM, SrutividyA, DarmmavidyA, devajYAnaM, brahmajYAnaM, brahmavidyA, tattvajYAnaM, tattvavidyA, aDyAtmajYAnaM, aDyAtmavidyA, SrotriyatA, parArTaprakaraRaM.
Theorem, s. prameyopapAdyaM.
THEOREM: (1) sampAdyam (?);(2) prameyopapAdyam, K.d.
THEOREM , s. (Proposition to be proved) prameyaM, prameyopapAdyaM.
THEORETIC , THEORETICAL, a. mAnasikaH -kI -kaM, kAlpanikaH &c., avyavahArikaH -kI -kaM, vyavahArAgamyaH -myA -myaM, manomayaH &c. See SPECULATIVE.
THEORETICALLY , adv. manaHkalpanAnusAreRa, manaHkalpanayA, kalpanApUrvvaM.
THEORIZE (v.): perh. mataM kalpayati, pra-, upa-. (c. of kxp).

Theory, s. mataM, sidDAMtaH; vAdaH; ‘t(heory) of evolution’ pariRAmavAdaH; nAstikamataM &c. 2 kalpanA, tarkaH, manaHsfzwi f. 3 AgamaH, SAstraM, upapatti f. (as opp. to; practice prayogaH), dvAvevApyAgAminO prayoganipuRO ca (M. 3) ‘well-versed in t(heory) and practice’; oft. maMtrataMtraM ‘t(heory) and practice’. Theoretical, a. vyavahArAyogya, kAlpanika-avyAvahArika- (kI f.). [Theoretical]ally, adv. kalpanApUrvaM. Theorize, v. t. mataM upakxp c.
THEORY: I Doctrine: q. v.: matam.II As opposed to practice: vijYAnam.III Exposi- -tion: q. v.: vivftiH.

THEORY , s. (Speculation, scheme) kalpanA, manaHkalpanA, mAnasaka- lpanA, mAnasasfzwiH f., tarkaH, kalpitaM, manaHkalpitaM, arTApattiH f.; ‘anxious to establish one's own theory,’ svakalpanAsADanecCuH -cCuH -cCu. — (Exposition of principles) vIjanirdeSaH, upapattiH f.
Theosophy, s. ISvaravAdaH-jYAnaM. [Theosoph]ist, s. aDyAtmavid.
Therapeutic, a. SAMtikara (rI f.), rogaGna (GnI f.); ‘t(herapeutic)s’ BezajaSAstraM.
THERAPEUTIC , rogaSamakaH -kA -kaM, rogapratikArakaH &c., see CURATIVE.
THERAPUTIC (adj.): SAntikaraH (f. rI), etc.: v. To cure.
THERAPUTICS: BEzajyavijYAnam and sim. comp.s.

There, adv. tatra, tasminsTAne, tatsTale. 2 (Expletive) by asti. interj. paSya, paSya; ‘here and t(here)’ itastataH; ‘t(here)about’ (‘t(hereabout)s’) tatrEva kutrApi; tatsTAnasamIpe; (with number) upa-Asanna in comp.; See Nearly, About; ‘20 or t(here)abouts’ upa-Asanna-viMSAH (narAH) &c., ‘t(here)after’ tataH, tadanu, tataH paraM, tadanaMtaraM; ‘t(here)at’ tena, tatra; tadupari; tataH; ‘t(here)by’ tena; tenopAyena, taddvAreRa; ‘t(here)fore’ ataH, tasmAt, tasmAt kAraRAt-hetoH, tataH; tat, iti hetoH, anena kAraRena-hetunA; ‘t(here)in’ tasminvizaye; ‘t(here)of’ tatratya, tatastya, tatrasTa (a.); tasya, asya, tadIya; ‘t(here)upon’ tataH, &c.

THERE: (1) tatra, of t.: tatratya (f. tyA: rare); (2) amutra (=yonder t.: rare), D. vi. N.B. Not expr. when used pleonastically, t. is a town called Valabhi in Saurāśṭra: asti sOrAzwrezu valaBI nAma nagarI, D. vi.

THERE , adv. tatra, tatsTAne, tasmin sTAne, tasmin deSe; ‘here and there,’ itastatas; ‘produced there, or relating to that place,’ tatratyaH -tyA -tyaM, tatrasTaH -sTA -sTaM; ‘the people residing there,’ tatrasTajanAH m. f., tatratyajanAH.
THEREABOUT, -S: I Of place: tatra kvacit.II Of number: upa- in comp., ten men or t.: upadaSapuruzAH.
THEREABOUTS , adv. (Near that place) tatropAnte, tatsTAnasamIpe -nikawe, tatrasamIpe, AdipaScAt. — (Nearly), see NEARLY, adv.
THEREAFTER: After that: tataH param. II = and then:(1) tataH;(2) tadanu;(3) tadanantaram.
THEREAT: (1) tatra;(2) tasmin (loc.).
THEREAT , adv. tena, tasmAt, tadupari, tatas, atas.
THEREBY: (1) tena;(2) by yena (= by which), t. I will play with you: yena dIvyAmyahaM tvayA.
THEREBY , adv. tena, tenopAyena, taddvArA, taddvAreRa, anenopAyena.

THEREFORE: (1) ataH (= for this), t. it is mere boldness to say...: ataH...iti vacanaM sAhasa- mAtram, S. 4.; t. spirit: ataeva prARaH, S. 23.; (2) tasmAt (= from that), t. brahmaRaH is objective genitive: tasmAd brahmaRa iti karmaRi zazWI.;(3) tataH (=2).: v. Then;(4) tat (=2: rare), t. here: tadiha, S. i. 2. 2.;(5) tena (=2), as regards this women are t. better: tenAtra varamaNganAH, V. m. 74. 12.
THEREFORE , adv. tena, tasmAt, anena hetunA, tena hetunA, tasya hetoH, tena kAraRena, tatkAraRAt, atas, tatas, ataHkAraRAt, atohetoH, tannidAnAt, tat, iti, iti hetoH.
THEREIN: atra (=in this: q. v. ) or tatra (=in that: q. v. ).
THEREIN , adv. tatra, tasmin, etasmin, asmin, asmin vizaye.
THEREINTO: tatra: v. That, into.
THEREOF: (1) asya (=of this: q. v. ) or tasya (=of that: q. v. );(2) by comp., arising t.: tatastaya (f. styA), Ki. i. 27.; men t.: tatratyA:
THEREOF , adv. tasya, etasya, tadIyaH -yA -yaM; ‘belonging to that place,’ tatratyaH -tyA -tyaM, tatsTAnikaH -kI -kaM, tatsTAnIyaH -yA -yaM, tatrasTaH &c.
THEREUPON: tatra: v. Then.
THEREUPON , adv. tatas, atas, tatropari, tadanantaraM, atrAntare.
THEREWITH: tena (=with that: q. v. ).
Thermal, a. uzRatAsaMbaMDin.
Thermometer, s. uzRamApanayaMtraM.
THERMOMETER: *tApamAnam, -yantram.
THERMOMETER , s. uzRAnuzRamApanayantraM, SItozRamApanayantraM.
THESE , pron. ete m. etAH f. etAni n. pl. (etat), ime m., imAH f., imAni n. pl. (idaM), amI m. pl. (adas); ‘these two,’ etO m. du., ete f. du.
Thesis, s. pratijYA, pUrvapakzaH. 2 prabaMDaH.
THESIS: I Proposition: pratijYA.II Disserta- -tion: prabanDaH.
THESIS , s. (Proposition) pakzaH, pUrvvapakzaH, pratijYA.
Thews, s. See Muscle, (1). 2 SarIrabalaM.
THEY , pron. te m., tAH f., tAni n. pl. (tad), ete &c., ime &c. (idaM), amI m. pl. (adas); ‘they two,’ tO m. du., te f. du.

Thick, a. Gana, nibiqa, avirala, sAMdra, gAQa; nIraMDra, SyAna. 2 sTUla, mahat, vipula; See Large. 3 maMda, jaqa, sTUla; See Dull; ‘t(hick)-headed’ maMdaDI; ‘t(hick)-skinned’ kaWina, sahizRu; maMda, sTUla. 4 paMkila, kaluzita, Avila. 5 (Of a solid body) Gana. s. tumulaM, Siras n., mUrDan m., saMkulaM; ‘in the t(hick) of the fight’ raRaSirasi, raRasaMmarde-mUrDni. adv. avirataM, niraMtaraM, aviralaM, nibiqaM, by (a.) in comp.; ‘t(hickly) sown’ Ganopta; sAMdrAcCAdita &c.; ‘t(hickly) set’ su-, saMhata, upacita. [Thick]en, v. t. GanIkf 8 U, nibiqIkf &c. v. i. GanIBU 1 P, nibiqIBU; ‘the horizon t(hicken)ed’ diNmaMqalaM (aBrapawalEH) GanIBUtaM, aBrapawalAkIrRaM. [Thick]et, s. gahanaM, gulmaH-lmaM, nibiqAraRyaM, vfkza-taru-gahanaM. [Thick]ly, adv. niraMtaraM, aviralaM, nibiqaM, gAQaM. [Thick]ness, s. GanatA, sAMdratA, saMhati f., &c. 2 veDaH, GanatA, piMqatvaM. 3 (Of voice) svaraBaMgaH.

THICK (adj.): I Dense: q. v.: Gana (f. nA), t. black hair: GananIlaSiroruhaH, Ri. iv. 16.II Muddy, dirty: q. v.: kaluzita (f. tA).III Large (as a t. volume): q. v.: bfhat (f. tI). IV Of voice: expr. by subs., the voice becomes t.: svaropaGAto Bavet, Sr. V. Dull: q. v.:IV In measurement: expr. with veDaH (=thickness).
THICK (subs.): maDyam (=middle): v. Also dense.
THICK, THICKLY (adv.): I Closely, densely: q. v.:expr. by comp., t. sown: Ganopta (f. ptA); t. covered: sAndrAvfta (f. tA); etc.II Qui- -ckly, uninterrupted: q. v.: nirantaram.

THICK , a. GanaH -nA -naM, sTUlaH -lA -laM, sAndraH -ndrA -ndraM, niviqaH -qA -qaM, aviralaH -lA -laM, nIranDraH -nDrA -nDraM, SyAnaH &c., styAnaH &c., see DENSE. — (As water, &c., turbid) kaluzaH -zA -zaM, anacCaH -cCA -cCaM, AvilaH -lA -laM.
THICK , adv. (In quick succession) nirantaraM, avirataM, see FRE- QUENTLY. — (Closely) nirantaraM, aviralaM, niviqaM.
THICK-HEADED: (1) sTUlaDI (n. Di);(2) jaqa- budDi (mfn.); and sim. comp.s.
THICK-HEADED , a. sTUlabudDiH -dDiH -dDi, sTUlaDIH &c. See STUPID.
THICK-SET: (1) saMhata (f. tA): v. Compact; (2) niviqa (f. qA): v. Dense.
THICK-SET , a. saMhataH -tA -taM, susaMhataH &c., nirantaraH -rA -raM.
THICK-SKINNED: Fig.: (1) kaWina (f. nA = call- -ous);(2) sahizRu (mfn. = forbearing).
THICKEN: I Intrans.: GanIBavati, etc.II Trans.: GanIkaroti, etc.
To THICKEN , v. a. vamIkf, sAndrIkf, sTUlIkf, SyAnIkf, niviqIkf.
To THICKEN , v. n. GanIBU, sAndrIBU, sTUlIBU, SyAnIBU, niviqIBU.
THICKENED , p. p. GanIBUtaH -tA -taM, GanIkftaH -tA -taM, sTUlIBUtaH &c.,
THICKENING , s. GanIkaraRaM, GanatA. See INSPISSATION.
THICKET: gahanam: v. Wood.
THICKET , s. gahanaM, vfkzagahanaM, tarugahanaM, vanagahanaM, JAwaH -waM, guhinaM, vipinaM, gahvaraM, sAndraM, prastAraH.
THICKLY , adv. nirantaraM, aviralaM, niviqaM, avirataM, susaMhataM.

THICKNESS: I Lit.:(1) GanatA;(2) sAndratA; (3) better by adj.II In measurement: (1) veDa (= depth), Li.;(2) vistftiH (= bre- -adth as of a heap of bricks), Li. 198.;(3) [Page708] piRqaH (as of wood), Li. 203.III Of voice: (1) svaropaGAtaH;(2) svaraBaNgaH; and sim. comp.s.
THICKNESS , s. GanatA -tvaM, sTUlatA, sTOlyaM, sAndratA, nEviqyaM, SyAnatA, pIvaratvaM, saMhatatvaM, see DENSITY. ‘Thickness,’ as a property of matter, is expressed by piRqatvaM.

THIEF: (1) cOraH, open t. ves such as merchants: prakASacOrA vaRigAdayaH, Viv.; t. -catcher: cOragrAhaH, Kat.;(2) taskaraH, for putting down t.s: taskara- pratizeDArTam, M. ix. 266.;(3) stenaH, who give food and lodging to t.ves: BaktAvakASadAtAraH stenAnAm, N. d.;(4) mozaH, -kaH, seeing a t.: mozABidarSane, M. ix. 274.;(5) kumBilaH, -kaH;(6) malimlucaH; (7) pAwaccaraH. N.B. 5 to 7 are rare.

THIEF , s. stenaH, cOraH, steyI m. (n), coraH, taskaraH, steyakft m., mozakaH, AmozI m. (n), mozwA m. (zwf), parasvApahArI m., adattA- dAyI m., paradravyahArakaH, cOryyakft m., EkAgArikaH, malimlucaH. See ROBBER, STEALER.
THIEF-TAKER , THIEF-CATCHER, s. cOragrAhI m. (n), stenagrAhI m.

Thieve, v. t. cur 10, muz 9 P, sten 10. [Thiev]ish, a. apaharaRa or cOrya-SIla or vftti, cOryAsakta. [Thiev]ishness, s. cOryAsakti f. Thief, s. stenaH, coraH, cOraH, taskaraH, dasyuH, mozakaH, kuMBI-lakaH, pA(pa)waccaraH, pratiroDiH, parAskaMdiH, malimlucaH, EkAgArikaH. Theft, s. steyaM, mozaH, cOryaM, co(cO)rikA, stEnyaM.
THIEVE: stenayati (sten, c. 10.): v. To steal.
To THIEVE , v. n. cOryyaM kf, steyaM kf, tAskaryyaM kf, paradravyaharaRaM kf.
THIEVISH , a. cOryyAsaktaH -ktA -ktaM, steyAsaktaH &c., cOryyaSIlaH -lA -laM, steyakArI -riRI -ri (n), adattaparaDanApahAraprasaktaH -ktA -ktaM.
THIEVISHNESS: cOryaSIlatA and sim. comp.s: v. Also secrecy.
THIEVISHNESS , s. cOryyAsaktiH f., steyAsaktiH f., cOryyaSIlatA, taskaratA.
Thigh, s. UruH (m.), sakTi n.; ‘having beautiful t(high)s’ vAmoruH-rU.
THIGH: (1) UruH, t.s: UrU, Ve.;(2) sakTi (n.), long-t.ed: dIrGasavaTa (f. vaTA:) v. Gram. A. 11. and 56).
THIGH , s. UruH m., sakTi n., jaNGA, jANGanI, Bazat m.; ‘fore part of [Page801-a+ 51] the thigh,’ pratijaNGA; ‘having long thighs,’ dIrGasakTaH -kTA -kTaM.
Thimble, s. aMgulitrARaM, aMgulimuKatraM.
THIMBLE: perh. aNgulitram or -trARam and sim. comp.s, Mah.
THIMBLE , s. aNgulyagratrARaM, aNgulimuKatraM, agrANgulitraM -trARaM, sUcicAlanI, sUcipraRodanI, sUcicAlanayogyayantraM.

Thin, a. pra-, tanu, sUkzma, virala, asTUla, SlakzRa. 2 kfSa, kzIRa, SAMta; ‘grown t(hin)’ tanvaMga-karSitAMga- (gI f.); ‘having a t(hin) waist’ tanumaDyama, kzIRamaDyama; See Slender. v. t. viralayati (D.), UnI-viralI-kf 8 U, saMKyAM apa-ci 5 U or kzi 5 P or c. 2 tanUkf, takz 1, 5 P, ulliK 6 P. [Thin]ly, adv. viralaM, asaMhataM. [Thin]ness, s. tanutA, sUkzmatA, vEralyaM, kArSyaM; kzIRatA.

THIN (adj.): (1) sUkzma (f. kzmA), t. oil: sUkzmaM tElam, Bha.: v. Fine.;(2) tanu (f. also nvI), t. dress: tanvaMSukam, Ri. iv. 3.: v. Slender, lean, little;(3) virala (f. lA: rare), having t. arrangement: viralaBakti (mfn.), R. v. 74.: v. Rare, scarce.
THIN (v.): (1) kraSayati (nomi.=make slender); (2) viralayati (nomi. = make less close).

THIN , a. (Not thick) tanuH -nuH -nvI -nu, pratanuH &c., vitanuH &c., sUkzmaH -kzmA -kzmaM, asTUlaH -lA -laM. — (Slender, lean) tanuH -nvI -nu, kzIRaH -RA -RaM, SIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, kfSaH -SA -SaM, kfSANgaH -NgA -NgaM, jEvAtfkaH -kA -kaM, pfSniH -SniH -Sni, SAtaH -tA -taM, amAMsaH -sA -saM; ‘having a thin waist,’ tanumaDyamaH -mA -maM, alpamaDyamaH &c., kzIRamaDyaH -DyA -DyaM, SAtodarI. — (Rare, subtil, fine) sUkzmaH -kzmA -kzmaM, SlakzRaH -kzRA -kzRaM, daharaH -rA -raM. — (Not close) viralaH -lA -laM; ‘a thin plank,’ sUkzmaPalakaH, sUkzmadAruH m.
TO THIN , v. a. tanUkf, sUkzmIkf, SlakzRIkf, SlakzRa (nom. SlakzRayati -yituM), leKanaM kf, takzaRaM kf. — (Make less, close, &c.) viralIkf.
THINE: tvadIyaH (yA, yaM): v. Thy.
THINE , a. tava gen. c., te gen. c., tvadIyaH -yA -yaM, tavakaH -kA -kaM, tAvakaH -kI -kaM, tAvakInaH -nA -naM, tvatkaH -tkA -tkaM, BavadIyaH -yA -yaM, tvat in comp.

sanskrit.slp1: kzataM BaNgAvamardO va kuryAdravyezu yo naraH
sanskrit.word: क्षतं भङ्गावमर्दौ व कुर्याद्रव्येषु यो नरः
sanskrit.iast: kṣataṃ bhaṅgāvamardau va kuryādravyeṣu yo naraḥ

details.body: Thing, s. vastu n., dravyaM, padArTaH, arTaH. 2 vizayaH, arTaH.

THING: (1) vastu (n.), sir, what t. is to be given to your preceptor: kiM vastu vidvan gurave pradeyam, R. v. 18.;...... why I have been confined or why I have been brought here, about these t.s my curiosity has not been removed: kimarTaM vAhaM badDo badDvA vA kimarTamihAnIta ityatra vastunyahamanapagatakOtuka eva, K.; (2) dravyam (=material), he who injures, breaks or crushes t.s: kzataM BaNgAvamardO va kuryAdravyezu yo naraH, Kat.;(3) vizayaH (=object: q. v. ).
THING , s. dravyaM, vastu n., arTaH, vizayaH, padArTaH, draviRaM, vasu n., vittaM, viBavaH, see SUBSTANCE; ‘things,’ dravyARi n. pl., vastUni n. pl.

Think, v. ciMt 10, DyE 1 P, vimfS 6 P, A-paryA-loc 10, vi-, tark 10, vi-car c., manasA kxp c., saM-, BU c. 2 man 4 A, gaR 10; See Consider; ‘t(hink) much of’ bahu man; ‘I t(hink) so’ iti me matiH; ‘does not t(hink) of going to his capital’ nagaragamanAya matiM na karoti (S. 2); ‘t(hink) of’ smf 1 P, manasi kf ‘I never thought of winter’ hemaMtaH samupasTAsyati iti ciMtA nEva manasi kftA, iti nEvAlocitaM. [Think]er, s. sUriH, muniH; (lit.) ciMtakaH; See Philosopher. Thought, s. (act) ciMtA, DyAnaM; Alo-canaM; (result also) vicAraH, vimarSaH, vi-cAraRaM-RA, BAvanA, manovyApAraH, cittacezwA. 2 mataM, aBiprAyaH, manoraTaH. 3 mati f., budDi f., kalpanA, vicAraH, saMkalpaH, manogataM, cittaM, manas n., tarkaH, citta-mano-vftti f., BAvanA; ‘oneʼs inmost t(hought)s’ aMtagartaM manaH; ‘evil t(hought)’ kumatiH; ‘benevolent t(hought)’ parahitabudDiH; ‘swift as t(hought)’ manojava; ‘beyond t(hought)’ aciMtya; ‘in t(hought), word or (actual) deed’ manovAkkAyakarmaBiH. [Thought]ful, a. ciMtASIla, vicAra-viveka-SIla, vimfSya-samIkzya-kArin, asAhasika (kI f.), sAvaDAna, apramatta. 2 ciMtA-kula-para-nimagna, DyAnapara. [Thought]fully, adv. viciMtya, vimfSya, vicArya, samIkzya, savivekaM, paryAlocya. [Thought]fulness, s. savi-cAratA, vivekitA, samIkzyakAritA. [Thought]less, a. pramatta, anavahita, asAvaDAna; See Negligent. 2 niSciMta, vItaciMta. 3 asa-mIkzya-avimfSya-kArin, kziprakArin, viveka-vicAra-hIna, saraBasa, mUQa. [Thought]lessly, adv. mohAt, raBasA, avimfSya, avivekena, avi-cAreRa. [Thought]lessness, s. avivekaH, avicAraH, raBasaH, mohaH.

THINK: (1) manyate (man, c. 4.), t.ing that title of lord only remains with you: matvA BavantaM praBuSabda- Sezam, R. v. 22.; if you t. much of what I say: asmAkamuktaM bahumanyase cet, B. iii. 53.: v. Consider, suppose;(2) cintayati, vi-, saM-, pari-, anu- (cint, c. 10. =reflect) he simply t.s of fears to come from you: sa cintayatyeva BiyastvadezyatIH, Ki. i. 23.; while I was thus t.ing: ityevaM cintayantam, K.;(3) DyAyati, anu- (DyE, c. 1.=2.) t. of the child in womb: prajAnizekamanuDyAyata, R. xiv. 60.;(4) smarati, anu- (smf, c. 1.=rem- -ember), to t. of heaven: divaH smartum, Ki. v. 28.;(5) aDyeti (i, c. 2.=5), t. s only of me: mAmevADyeti, Ki. xi. 74.

To THINK , v. a. or n. (Reflect) cint (c. 10. cintayati -yituM), saMcint, vicint, paricint, pravicint, tark (c. 10. tarkayati -yituM), vitark, DyE (c. 1. DyAyati, DyAtuM), anuDyE, upaDyE, aBiDyE, praDyE, saMDyE, vimfS, anumfS, parimfS, manasA vicar, BU in caus., samBU in caus., Aloc, Alok, nirUp, see To REFLECT. — (Suppose) man (c. 4. manyate, mantuM), see To IMAGINE; ‘to think of,’ anusmf, see To RECOLLECT; ‘to think to one's self,’ svagataM cint; ‘one who thinks that it is night,’ rAtrimmanyaH.
THINKER: (1) sUriH;(2) muniH (= sage).
THINKER , s. cintakaH, cintayitA m. (tf), cintanakft, mantA m.
THINLY: (1) tanu: v. Slenderly;(2) viralam: v. Rarely;(3) by comp., t. populated: viralajana or alpajana (f. nA).
THINLY , adv. viralaM, vEralyena, asaMhataM, asTUlaM, tanu, tAnavena.
THINNED , p. p. tanUkftaH -tA -taM, sUkzmIkftaH &c., tazwaH -zwA -zwaM, tvazwaH &c.
THINNESS: (1) tanutA: v. Slenderness;(2) sUkzmatA: v. Fineness;(3) viralatA or vEralyam (= scarcity).
THINNESS , s. tanutA, tAnavaM, sUkzmatA, kzIRatA, SIrRatA, kfSatA, kfSA- NgatA, sOkzmyaM, asTUlatA. — (Rareness) viralatA, vEralyaM.
THIRD (adj.): tftIyaH (yA, yaM), in the t. place: tftIyataH; for the t. time: tftIyavAram; there is no t. course: anyA gatirnAsti. Ph.: t. estate i. e. com- -monalty: prakftayaH (f. pl. (?).
THIRD (subs.): I A t. part:(1) tftIyAMSaH; (2) tftIyaBAgaH;(3) trimAgaH;(4) tryaMSaH, two-t. s: dvO tryaMSO, Li.;(5) trilavaH, two-t. s: trilavadvayam, Li.II In music: gAnDAraH (?).
THIRD , a. tftIyaH -yA -yaM, tritayaH &c., tftIyI -yinI -yi (n).
THIRD , s. (Third part) tftIyAMSaH, tftIyaBAgaH; ‘two thirds,’ dvO tftIyAMSO, dvO tftIyaBAgO; ‘having a third,’ tftIyI -yinI &c.
THIRDLY: (1) tftIyataH;(2) tftIyam.
THIRDLY , adv. tftIyatas, tftIyaM, tftIyapade, tftIyasTAne.

Thirst, v. t. tfz 4 P, (fig. also); pA desid. (pipAsati), udanyati (D.). s. tfzRA, (fig. also); dravyatfzRA, jIvitatfzRA &c.; pipAsA, tfzA, tfz f., udanyA, pAnecCA. [Thirst]y, a. tfzita, pipAsita, tfzArta-Akula-Atura, satfzRa, pipAsu, udakArTin, tfzRAvizwa-AkrAMta.

THIRST (subs.): (1) tfzRA (lit. and fig.), t. for wealth: DanAgamatfzRA, J.; t., you are still not satisfied: tfzRe nAdyApi santuzyasi, J.;(2) pipAsA (lit.), to quench t.: pipAsAM pratikartum, D. viii.; to remove t.: pipAsAmapanayati, D.; very great t.: atiprabalapipAsA, K.;(3) udanyA (=2: rare), quenching of t.: udanyApratIkAraH, Ve. vi.;(4) tfz or tfzA (=1: rare).
THIRST (v.i.): (1) tfzyati (tfz, c. 4.: lit. and fig.), Ki. xi. 74.;(2) udanyati (nomi.: lit. rare), B. iv. 44.

THIRST , s. tfzRA, tfzA, tfw f. (z), pipAsA, tarzaH -rzaRaM, anutarzaH, tfzitaM, pAnecCA, udakecCA, udanyA, apalAzikA, upalAlikA, DItiH f.; ‘exeessive thirst,’ atitfzRA; ‘of wealth,’ DanatfzRA, DanASA; ‘eating to excite thirst,’ avadaMSaH.
To THIRST , v. n. tfz (c. 4. tfzyati, tarzituM), vitfz, pA in des. (pipA- sati -situM), tfzArttaH -rttA -rttaM BU, tfzArttIBU, udana (nom. udanyati).
THIRSTING , part. tfzyan -zyantI -zyat (t), pipAsan -santI -sat (t). See the next.

THIRSTY: (1) tfzitaH (tA, taM), I am t.: tfzito'smi Ve. vi.;(2) tfzArta: (rtA, rtaM);(3) pipAsitaH [Page709] (tA, taM);(4) satfzRaH (zRA, zRAM);(5) pipAsu (mfn.);(6) tfzRAturaH (rA, raM);(7) tfzRAkulaH (lA, laM).

THIRSTY , a. tfzArttaH -rttA -rttaM, pipAsuH -suH -su, tarzitaH -tA -taM, tfzitaH &c., tfzRak m. f. n. (j), tfzAturaH -rA -raM, tfzRAturaH -rA -raM, pAnecCuH -cCuH -cCu, udakecCuH &c., udakArTI -rTinI -rTi (n), pAnArTI &c., pipAsitaH -tA -taM, satfzRaH -zRA -zRaM, satfw m. f. n. (z), tfwparItaH -tA -taM, satfzaH -zA -zaM, tfzAnvitaH -tA -taM, tfzAvAn -vatI &c., tfzA- kulaH -lA -laM, tfzAvizwaH -zwA -zwaM, tfzAkrAntaH -ntA -ntaM.
Thirteen, a. trayodaSan. [Thirteen]th, a. trayodaSa (SI f.).
THIRTEEN: trayodaSan (mfn.). T.-th: trayodaSaH (SI, SaM).
THIRTEEN , a. trayodaSa m. f. n. pl. (n), tridaSa m. f. n. pl. (n).
THIRTEENTH , a. trayodaSaH -SI -SaM, tridaSaH -SI -SaM.
THIRTIETH: (1) triMSaH (SA, SaM);(2) triSattamaH (mI, maM).
THIRTIETH , a. triMSaH -SI -SaM, triMSattamaH -mI -maM.
Thirty, a. triMSat f. [Thirt]ieth, a. triMSa (SI f.), triMSattama (mI f.).
THIRTY: triMSat (f.), t.-fold: triMSadguRaH (RA, RaM).

THIRTY , a. triMSat sing. f., triMSakaH -kA -kaM; ‘the aggregate of thirty,’ triMSakaM; ‘he reigned thirty years,’ triMSatam abdAn rAjyaM cakAra; ‘with thirty arrows,’ triMSatA SarEH; ‘thirty- one,’ ekatriMSat; ‘two,’ dvAtriMSat; ‘three,’ trayastriMSat; ‘four,’ catustriMSat; ‘five,’ paYcatriMSat; ‘six,’ zawtriMSat, see SEVENTY; ‘thirty-fold,’ triMSadguRaH -RA -RaM.
This, pron. a. etad (ezaH-ezA-etat), idaM (ayaM-iyaM-idaM); ‘t(his) way’, ‘t(his) way’ itaH itaH.

THIS: (1) by etad, who is t. Rāma: ka eza rAmaH, Pra.; t. speech of Uddhava: OdDavIM vAcamenAm, Si. ii. 118.; for t. I live: etadarTaM hi jIvAmi, Mah.;(2) by idam, through t. row of young plants: anayA bAlapAdapavITyA, Sa. iii.; t. way, gentlemen: ita ito BavantaH, Sa. ii.
THIS , pron. ezaH ezA etad (etad), ayaM iyaM idaM (idaM), asO m. f. (adas).
Thistle, s. gokzuraH-rakaH, gokaMwakaH, vanaSfMgAwaH, svAdukaMwakaH, palaMkazA, ikzugaMDA, SvadaMzwrA, (plant).
THISTLE: a plant: afgAlapucCaH (?).
THISTLE , s. gokzuraH -rakaH, goKuraH, goKuriH m., kzuraH.
Thither, adv. tatra. [Thither]ward, adv. taM deSaM prati.
THITHER: tatra. T. wards: taM deSaM prati and sim. expr. s.
THITHER , adv. tatra, tatsTAnaM prati, taddeSaM prati, taM deSaM prati.
Thong, s. varatrA, na(va)DrI, carmarjju f.
THONG: (1) varatrA;(2) vaDrI;(3) carmarajjuH, and sim. comp.s.
THONG , s. varatrA, carmmarajjuH m. f., carmmabanDaH, baDrI, bardDrI, vaDrI, vArdDrI, vArdDaM -rdDI, nadDrI, balisaNgaH, carmmanirmmito rajjuH, carmmapawwI.
Thorax, s. uraH-vakzaH n., sTalaM.
THORAX , s. uras n., vakzas n., vakzaHsTalaM, uraHsTalaM, vakzassTalaM, urassTalaM, pArSvaM.

sanskrit.slp1: aMtaH pratyuptaM SalyaM-kaMwakaM-iva sa tvAM pIqayati

sanskrit.iast: aṃtaḥ pratyuptaṃ śalyaṃ-kaṃṭakaṃ-iva sa tvāṃ pīḍayati

details.body: Thorn, s. kaMwakaH-kaM, SalyaM; SitAgraH, taru-druma-naKaH; (fig.) kaMwakaH, SalyaM; ‘he is a t(horn) in your side’ aMtaH pratyuptaM SalyaM-kaMwakaM-iva sa tvAM pIqayati; ‘there is no rose without a t(horn)’ suKaM nAma duHKamiSritamastyeva, duH-KAsaMBinnaM suKaM nEva prApyate. 2 kaMwalakatA-vfkzaH; ‘t(horn)-apple’ DattUraH, DustaraH, unmattaH, kitavaH, DUrtaH, kanakAhvayaH, mAtulaH, madanaH; (fruit) mAtulaputrakaH. [Thorn]less, a. nizkaMwaka. [Thorn]y, a. kaMwakAvfta, kaMwakAkIrRa, kaMwakita, sakaMwaka.
THORN: I A prickle: kaRwaka (mn.).II Fig.: kaRwaka (mn.), avoids heroes like t.s: SUraM kaRwaka- Biva pariharati, K.III A thorny plant: kaRwa- kin (f. nI), -vfkzaH (or latA).

THORN , s. (Tree) kaRwakavfkzaH. — (Prickle) kaRwakaH -kaM, drunaKaH, druma- naKaH, tarunaKaH, patrasUciH m., dalasUciH m., SalyaM, SitAgraH, sitAgraH, rANkalaH, valkilaH, vaNkilaH, panasaH, drumaraH; ‘extraction of thorns,’ kaRwakodDaraRaM, SalyodDaraRaM; ‘eater of thorns,’ kaRwakaBuk m. — (Any thing troublesome) kaRwakaH, SalyaM.
THORN-APPLE: I The tree: Dustu(stU)raH.II The fruit: Dusturam.

THORN-APPLE , s. DattUraH, DustUraH, DusturaH, DUstUraH, kanakaH, kitavaH, unmattaH, DUrttaH, mAtulaH, madanaH, mAraH, hemataruH m., purImohaH, KaradUzaRaH, kAha- lApuzpaH, tIkzRakaRwakaH; ‘its fruit,’ mAtulaputrakaH.
THORNLESS , a. nizkaRwakaH -kA -kaM, akaRwakaH &c., kaRwakahAnaH -nA -naM.
THORNY: (1) kaRwakin (f. nI);(2) kaRwakAvfta (f. tA), and sim. comp.s.
THORNY , a. kaRwakitaH -tA -taM, kaRwakI -kInI -ki (n), sakaRwakaH -kA -kaM, bahukaRwakaH &c., pracurakaRwakaH &c., kaRwakayuktaH -ktA -ktaM.

Thorough, a. saMpUrRa, samyac, sAdyaMta, paryApta; See Complete; ‘t(horough)-bred’ aBijAta, atikulIna; (horse) AjAneyaH, kulInaH; ‘t(horough)-fare’ rAjamArgaH, GaMwApaTaH, saMsaraRaM; sarvasAmAnyapaTaH, sarvagamyamArgaH. [Thorough]ly, adv. samyak, saMpUrRaM, sAdyaMtaM; by pAra in comp., ‘who has t(horoughly) learnt the lores’ vidyAnAM pAradfSvanaH (R. i. 23); ‘t(horoughly) mastered all lores’ tatAra sarvA vidyAH (R. iii. 30). [Thorough]ness, s. pUrRatA, paripUrti f., niHSezatA.
THOROUGH: (1) samyak (mIcI), t. instruction: samyagavinayanam, D. ii.;(2) sampUrRa (f. rRA = full, complete: q. v. ), Pr.; t. master:(1) pAraga (f. gA);(2) pAradfSvan (mfn.).
THOROUGH , a. sAdyantaH -ntA -ntaM, paryyAptaH -ptA -ptaM. See COMPLETE.
THOROUGH-BRED , a. (Horse) AjAneyaH, kulInaH, see under HORSE.
THOROUGHBRED: (1) AjAneya (f. yI);(2) mahAkulIna (f. nA); etc.
THOROUGHFARE: rAjamArgaH: v. Street, road.
THOROUGHFARE , s. sarvvasADAraRamArgaH, sarvvasAmAnyapaTaH, sarvvagamyamArgaH, lokagamyapaTaH, apratiroDapaTaH; ‘a great thoroughfare,’ lokayAtrA, sarvvalokayAtrA, janAkIrRamArgaH, janAkIrRaM.
THOROUGHLY: (1) samyaka, after being t. instru- cted: samyag vinIya, R. v. 10.;(2) Adyantam (= from beginning to end): v. Also fully.
THOROUGHLY , adv. sAdyantaM, paryyAptaM, sAkalyena. See COMPLETELY.
THOSE , pron. te m., tAH f., tAni n. pl. (tad), amI m. pl. See THESE.
Thou, pron. tvaM; ‘to t(hou) and thee’ tvaMkf 8 U; ‘do not t(hou) your elders’ guruzu tvaMkAraM na prayojayet. Thine, a. tvadIya, tAvaka (kI f.), tAvakIna, tvatka, BavadIya, tvat in comp.
THOU: I Subs.: tvam (G. ch. xviii.).II Verb: tvaMkaroti, one should avoid t.ing and calling seniors by name: tvaNkAraM nAmaDeyaYca jyezWAnAM parivarjayet, Mah. xii. 193. 25.
THOU , pron. tvaM (yuzpat); ‘to thou and thee,’ tvaNkf.
Though, adv. api, yadyapi; ‘as t(hough)’ iva.
THOUGH: -api: v. Although.
THOUGH , conj. yadyapi, api, taTApi, yadi. See ALTHOUGH.

THOUGHT: I In gen.:(1) cintA, with hun- dreds of t.s: cintASatEH, K.;(2) vicAraH (= consideration);(3) DyAnam (=meditation). II Idea, notion: q. v.: matam.III = mind: q. v.: budDiH, evil t.s: drohabudDiH; she could not express her t.s: manogataM sA na SaSAka SaMsitum, Ku. v. 51.

THOUGHT , s. (Operation of the mind, act of thinking) cintA -ntanaM, vicAraRaM -RA, vicAraH, DyAnaM, aBiDyAnaM, ADyAnaM, BAvanA, carcA, mananaM, manovyApAraH, antaHkaraRavyApAraH, cittavyApAraH, cittacezwA, manaScezwA, antaHkaraRacezwA, see REFLECTION, MEDITATION. — (That which is formed in the mind) budDiH f., matiH f., mataM, manas n., boDaH, manogataM, kalpanA, manaHkalpanA, manaHkalpitaM, saNkalpaH, manoguptaM, manasijaM, manovfttiH f., cittavfttiH f., hfdgataM, BAvanA, tarkaH; ‘inmost thoughts,’ antargataM manas; ‘evil thoughts,’ kukalpanA, kutarkaH, apaDyAnaM; ‘speed of thought,’ manovegaH, manojavaM; ‘swift as thought,’ manojavaH -vA -vaM, manoyAyI -yinI &c.; ‘beyond thought,’ acintyaH -ntyA -ntyaM, acintanIyaH -yA -yaM; ‘in thought, word, or deed,’ manovacanakarmmaBiH inst. pl.
THOUGHT , p. p. cintitaH -tA -taM, mataH &c., BAvitaH &c., kalpitaH &c.
THOUGHTFUL: I Of men:(1) cintASIla (f. lA);(2) cintAparAyaRa (f. RA), and sim. comp.s.II Attentive, careful: q. v.III Full of thought: cintAkula (f. lA), and sim. comp.s: v. Waking.

THOUGHTFUL , a. (Contemplative) cintAparaH -rA -raM, see MEDITA- TIVE. — (Considerate, attentive) vicAraSIlaH -lA -laM, vicAravAn vatI &c., savicAraH -rA -raM, sacintaH -ntA -ntaM, cintAvAn &c., cintAyuktaH -ktA -ktaM.
THOUGHTFULLY: (1) vicintya;(2) vicArya; (3) vimfzya.
THOUGHTFULNESS: (1) cintASIlatA;(2) cintA- kflatA; etc.: v. Adj.
THOUGHTFULNESS , s. vicAraSIlatA, savicAratA, sacintatA, mAnasatvaM.
THOUGHTLESS: I Lit.: niScinta (f. ntA).II Careless: q. v.: pramatta (f. ttA).
THOUGHTLESS , a. niScintaH -ntA -ntaM, vivekahInaH -nA -naM, vicArahInaH &c., avicAraSIlaH -lA -laM, anUhaH -hA -haM. See HEEDLESS, NEGLIGENT.
THOUGHTLESSLY: I Lit.: niScintam.II Carelessly: q. v.: avimfzya.
THOUGHTLESSLY , adv. acintayA, niScintaM, avicAreRa, avivekena; ‘thoughtlessly done,’ avicArakftaH -tA -taM, avivekakftaH &c.
THOUGHTLESSNESS , s. avicAraH -ratA, avivekatA, avivekaH, vicAra- hInatA, vivekahInatA, pramAdaH. See HEEDLESSNESS.

Thousand, a., s. sahasraM, daSaSataM; ‘t(housand)s of times’ sahasraSaH-vAraM; ‘in a t(housand) ways or parts’ sahasraDA; ‘ten t(housand)’ ayutaM; ‘hundred t(housand)’ lakzaM; ‘by t(housand)s’ sahasraSaH. [Thousand]th, a. sahasratapta (mI f.).

THOUSAND: (1) sahasram, not less than four t. verses: anyUnacatvAri SlokasahasrARi, V. m. 107. 11.; two t.: dve sahasre; ten t.: daSa sahasrARi; t. arms: dozRAM sahasram, Mah.;(2) daSaSatam (tI) (rare). T. times: sahasrakftvaH; t.s of times: sahasraSaH; in t. ways or parts: sahasraDA; ten t.: ayutam; hundred t.: lakzam; the t.-eyed (Indra): sahasrAkzaH; the t.-armed (Arjuna): sahasrabAhuH; the t.-rayed (sun): sahasrAMSuH; the t.-headed (sun): sahasraSIrzaH.

THOUSAND , a. sahasraM n. sing., daSaSataM. The word sahasraM may be used with the nom. pl. or gen. pl.; as, ‘a thousand an- cestors,’ sahasraM pitaraH or sahasraM pitFRAM; ‘ten thousand,’ ayutaH -taM; ‘one hundred thousand,’ lakzaM -kzA; ‘a thousand times,’ sahasrakftvas; ‘in a thousand ways,’ sahasraDA; ‘thousand eyed,’ sahasranayanaH -nA -naM; ‘a regiment of a thousand men,’ sahasrI m. (n), sAhasraH; ‘the aggregate of a thousand,’ sAhasraM; ‘thou- sand-fold,’ sahasraguRaH -RA -RaM; ‘by thousands,’ sahasraSas.
THOUSANDTH: I Adj.: sahasratamaH (mI, maM).II Subs.: sahasrAMSaH.
THOUSANDTH , a. sahasratamaH -mI -maM, sAhasraH -srI -sraM.
THRALDOM or THRALDOM: dAsyam: v. Slavery.
Thrall, s. dAsaH. [Thrall]dom, s. dAsyaM, dAsavftti f., dAsatvaM; See Slave, [Slav]ery. 2 vaSatA, pArataMtryaM, aDInatA.
THRALL: dAsaH. v. Slave.
THRALLDOM , s. dAsyaM, vaSatA, pAratantryaM, see SERVITUDE, SLAVERY.
Thrash, v. t. paruzaM-balavat-taq 10 or pra-hf 1 P. 2 nistuzIkf 8 U, pU 9 U; See Thresh.
THRASH: I Lit.: nistuzIkaroti.II To beat soundly: paruzaM praharati (hf, c. 1.), t. ing: paruza- prahAraH and sim. comp.s.
To THRASH , v. a. nistupIkf, kaRqanaM kf, pU, taq. See To THRESH.

Thread, s. sUtraM, taMtuH, (fig. also), (ASA-taMtuH), guRaH, taMtraM; ‘t(hread) of a story’ kaTAprabaMDaH-anubaMDaH-saMdarBaH-anvayaH, anu-, saMDAnaM, prabaMDArTaH; ‘t(hread)-bare’ sUtradaridra; ayaM pawaH sUtradaridratAM gataH (Mr. 2), sUtraSeza; jarjara. v. t. sUtr 10; gu(guM)P 6 P, graMT 9 P; ‘t(hread) oneʼs way’ maMdaM maMdaM prasfp 1 P. [Thread]y, a. sUtra-taMtu-maya (yI f.).
THREAD (subs.): (1) sUtram, golden t.: suvarRasUtram, Si.;(2) tantuH; t. of hope: ASAtantuH, Ma. ix. 25.
THREAD (v.): I To string: q. v.: sUtrayati. II To t. one's way: prasarpati (sfp, c. 1.): v. To go, move.

THREAD , s. sUtraM, tantuH m., tantraM, guRaH, sUtratantuH m., sarat n., sarit f., kubraM, cInaH, KAtraM; ‘point of a thread,’ pakzma n. (n), sUtrAgraM; ‘thread of a story or subject,’ prabanDArTaH, arTaprabanDaH, anvayaH, arTAnvayaH, arTasandarBaH, kaTAsandarBaH, kaTAprabanDaH, sanDAnaM, anusanDAnaM; ‘thread of hope,’ ASAtantuH m.; ‘sacrificial thread,’ see under SACRIFICIAL.
To THREAD , v. a. sUtra (Nom. sUtrayati -yituM), gumP, see To STRING.
THREADBARE: I Lit.: sUtradaridra (f. drA), Mr. ii. 7.II Fig.: SUnyagarBa (f. rBA).
THREADBARE , a. jarjarIkaH -kA -kaM, jarjaraH -rA -raM, sUtradaridraH &c.
THREADED , p. p. sUtritaH -tA -taM, gumPitaH &c., granTitaH &c., graTitaH &c.
THREADY: (1) sUtramaya (f. yI);(2) tantumaya (f. yI);(3) tAntava (f. vI).

Threat, s. tarjanaM, tarjitaM, BartsanaM, apakAragir f. [Threat]en, v. t. saM-, tarj 1 P, 10 A, nir-, Barts 10 A, BI c. v. i. pratyA-sad 1 P, lagna. a. saMpad 4 A, unnam 1 P; ‘war t(hreat)s’ pratyAsIdati raRaprasaMgaH; See Impend. [Threat]ening, a. Bartsatakft; anizwAvedin; pratyAsannamaya, viBIzaka. [Threat]eningly, adv. tarjayat a.
THREAT: (1) viBIzikA, by various t. s: viBIzikABirbahvIBiH Mah. ii. 41. 1.;(2) tarjanam or tarjitam, saM-.(3) mIzA, M. n.
THREAT , s. BartsanaM, nirBartsanaM, tarjanaM, daRqamUcanaM. See MENACE.

THREATEN: I Lit.:(1) tarjayati, saM- (tarj, c. 10.), t. ed much against Dhanamitra: Danamitra- mullaNGya bahvatarjayat, D. ii.; t. ed them: tAvatarjayat, R. xii. 41.;(2) BIzayati (c. of BI = frighten: q. v.).II Fig.: expr. by circumlo.: it t. s rain or t. ing weather: vfzwyASaMsi divasam; weather is t. ing: pratyAsIdati BkaYBka: v. To bespeak, impend.

To THREATEN , v. a. Barts (c. 10. Bartsayati -te -yituM), nirBartm, tarj, see To MENACE. — (Declare purpose of punishing) daRqasUcanaM kfM, daRqapradarSanaM kf, daRqasaNkalpapradarSanaM kf. — (Exhibit the appearance of something evil approaching) anizwasUcanaM kf, anizwAvedanaM kf, see To PREBODE.
THREATENED , p. p. BartsitaH -tA -taM, nirBartsitaH &c., tarjitaH -tA -taM.
THREATENING , part. BartsanakArI -riRI &c., anizwAvedI -dinI &c.
THREATENINGLY: tarjayat (f. ntI), saM-: v. To threaten.

Three, a. tri (tisf f.); ‘aggregate of t(hree)’ trayaM, tritayaM, trikaM, trayI; ‘t(hree) months’ trimAsaM, mAsatrayaM; ‘two or t(hree)’ dvitra, tri-catura, &c.; ‘t(hree)-cornered’ trikoRa; ‘t(hree)-eyed’ trilocanaH, trinayanaH; &c.; ‘t(hree)-fold’ triguRa; ‘t(hree)-fourths’ tripAdaH, pAda-trayaM; ‘2 and t(hree)-fourths’ pAdonatrayaM. Third, a. tftIya. s. tftIyaBAgaH-aMSaH. [Third]ly, adv. tftIyasTAne. Thrice, adv. triH, trivAraM.

THREE: tri, by the t. states: tisfBiravasTABiH, Ku.; t. times: triH; in t. ways: triDA or treDA; t. or four: tricaturAH (n. pl. Ri); interest at t. percent per mensem: trikaM SataM mAsasya vfdDiH, M. viii. 143.; the t. Vedas: trayI; the t. objects of life (virtue, wealth and love): trivargaH; the t. spices (cinnamon, nutmeg, and cardamoms): trijAtakam, D.; a heifer t. years old: trihAyaRI; for t. nights: trirAtram. trayam is often affixed to express t.: t. years: varzatrayam. T. score: v. Sixty.

THREE , a. trayaH m. pl., tisraH f. pl., trIRi n. pl. (tri); ‘the three worlds,’ triBuvanaM; ‘the aggregate of three,’ trayaM, trayI, trikaM, tritayaM. The word trayaM is often used at the end of a com- pound to express ‘three;’ as, ‘three months,’ mAsatrayaM; ‘three years,’ varzatrayaM; ‘three steps,’ padatrayaM; ‘the three properties,’ guRacayaM; ‘he was seen by three rogues,’ sa DUrtta- trayeRa dfzWaH; ‘two or three,’ dvitrAH -trAH -trARi (tra being here put for vi); two or three or any number,’ dvitrAdisaMKyA, dvitrAdyAH m. pl.; ‘three or four,’ tricaturAH -rAH -rARi; ‘rule of three,’ trErASikagaRitaM, see under RULE, s.
THREE HUNDRED: triSatam, T. th: triSataH (tI, taM) or triSatatamaH (mI, maM).
THREE-CORNERED: (1) trikoRaH(RA, RaM);(2) tryasraH (srA, sraM).
THREE-EYED: (1) trinayanaH (nA, naM);(2) trinetraH (trA, traM);(3) trilocanaH (nA, naM).
THREE-FOLD , a. triguRaH -RA -RaM, triviDaH -DA -DaM, trivft m. f. n.
THREE-FOOTED: (1) tripadaH (dI, daM).(2) tripAdaH (dA, daM).
THREE-FOURTHS , s. pl. trayaS caturTAMSAH m. pl., tripAdAH, tryaMSAH.
THREE-HEADED: (1) trimUrDa (f. rDI) (the form trimUrDan is also found);(2) triSiras (mfn.); (3) triSIrzakaH (kA, kA).
THREE-LEAVED: (1) tripatraH (trA, traM);(2) triparRaH (rRA, rRaM), etc.
THREEFOLD: triguRaH (RA, RaM): v. Also three.
THRENODY , s. yamagATA, yamagItaM, yamagAnaM.

Thresh, v. t. mfd 9 P, pari-, pU 9 U, nistu-zIkf 8 U, kaMq 10. 2 taq 10, pra-hf 1 P. [Thresh]ed, a. nistuzita, nistuza, pUta, bahulIkfta. [Thresh]ing, s. pAvanaM, bahulIkaraRaM, kaMqanaM, nistu-zIkaraRaM; ‘t(hreshing)-floor’ KalaDAnyaM; ‘t(hreshing) instrument’ musalaH-laM, ayograM, kaMqanI.
THRESH: mfdrAti or mardayati, saM-, pari-, (mfd, c. 9. and 10.). Ph.: t. ing floor: KalaH (lI).
To THRESH , v. a. (Corn) DAnyAdi mfd (c. 9. mfdnAti, mardituM) or pU or paripU or nistunIkf, DAnyAdimardanaM kf, DAnyAdikaRqanaM kf, avaGAtaM kf. — (Beat) taq (c. 10. tAqayati -yituM), tAqanaM kf.
THRESHED , p.p. marditaH -tA -taM, mfditaH &c., nistuzitaH &c., nistupAkftaH &c., pUtaH &c., paripUtaH &c., apahataH &c., bahulIkftaH &c.
THRESHING , s. DAnyAdimardanaM, DAnyAdikaRqanaM, kaRqanaM, nistupIkaraRaM, ava- GAtaH, pAvanaM, tAqanaM.
THRESHING-FLOOR , s. DAnyAdimardanasTAnaM, DAnyAdikaRqanasTAnaM, DAnyamardana- BUmiH f., KalaH, SasyamardanasTAnaM.
Threshold, s. dehalI, dvArapiMqI, grahAvagrahaRI; (fig.) prAraMBaH.
THRESHOLD: I Lit.:(1) dehalI;(2) dvArapiRqI; (3) gfhAvagrahaRI;(4) uqumbaraH (rare).II Fig.: prAramBaH: v. Beginning.
THRESHOLD s. dehalI, gfhAvagrahaRI, gfhatawI, SilA -lI, dvArapiRqI, ruRqikA, amburaH, uqumbaraH.
THRICE: (1) triH;(2) trivAram. T. seven (i. e. twentyone) times: triHsaptakftvaH; t. ploughed: triguRAkftaH (tA, taM) or trihalyaH (lyA, lyaM), t. as long as that: tasmAttriguRadIrGaH (rGA, rGaM).
THRICE , adv. trivAraM, vAratrayaM, triH, trikftvam, triguRaH -RA -RI -RaM, tri in comp.; ‘thrice ploughed,’ trisItyaH -tyA -tyaM, trihalyaH -lyA -lyaM, triguRAkftaH -tA -taM.
Thrift, s. mitavyayaH-vyayitA. 2 saM-vi-vfdDi f. [Thrift]y, a. mitavyayin, alpavyaya; See Frugal.
THRIFT: I Thriftiness: mitavyayaH, -yitAH v. Frugality.II Growth, increase: q. v.: (1) saMvfdDiH;(2) vivfdDiH.
THRIFTY: mitavyayin (f. nI): v. Frugal, sparing.

Thrill, s. pra-, kaMpaH, sPuraRaM, harzaH; (of joy, horror, &c.) romAMcaH, pulakaH; udDarzaH; ‘t(hrill) of joy’ harzaromAMcaH, pulakodgamaH, romaharzaH, ‘a t(hrill) came over her body’ tasyA gAtraM romAMcitaM-pulakitaM-kaMwakitaM-baBUva; ‘with a t(hrill) of horror’ sADvasaromAMcitagAtraH. v. sPur 6 P, hfz 4 P, pra-, kaMp 1 A; gen. ex. by pulakrita, romAMcita, kaMwakita, (a.); ‘he t(hrill)ed with joy’ AnaMdapulakitatanurbaBUva. [Thrill]ing, a. lo(ro)maharzaRa (RI f.), pulakita, romAMcita, &c.

THRILL: I Subs.:(1) vepaTuH (= shivering); (2) romAYcaH, and sim. comp.s (=horripila- -tion), a t. came over the bodies of the sages: munInAmaNgAni romAYjaM biBarAmbaBUvuH, Ki. xv. 53.II Verb: expr. by subs. T. ing: lo(ro)maharzaRa (f. RA), Mah.
THRILL , s. sPuraRaM, sPUrttiH f., sPuritaM, harzaH; ‘of joy,’ romaharzaH -rzaRaM, romodDarzaRaM, romodgamaH, romodBedaH, romAYcaH, pulakaH, pulakodgamaH.
To THRILL , v. n. sPur (c. 6. sPurati -rituM), hfz (c. 4. hfzyati, harzituM).
THRILLING , part. sPuran -rantI -rat (t), sPuritaH -tA -taM; ‘with joy,’ hfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, harzI -rziRI -rzi (n), pulakitaH -tA -taM, romA- YcitaH &c.
Thrive, v. i. pra-, vfD 1 A, pra-upa-ci pass., saMfDsamfD 4, 5 P, unnatiM-utkarzaM-prAp 5 P; See Prosper, Flourish. [Thriv]ing, a. varDizRu, pra-upa-cIyamAna, samfdDa.
THRIVE: vardDate (vfD, c. 1.), t. ing: varDizRu, (mfn.), Si. v. 14.: v. Also prosperous.
THRIVING , v. n. samfdDaH -dDA -dDaM. See PROSPEROUS, FLOURISIHNG.
Throat, s. kaMWaH, galaH, kfkaH, nigaraRaH; ‘relating to t(hroat)’ kaMWya; ‘up to the t(hroat)’ AkaMWaM, AkaMWAt.
THROAT: (1) kaRWaH;(2) galaH: v. Neck.

THROAT , s. kaRWaH, galaH, grIvA, kanDaraH -rA, kuharaM, kfkaH, nigaraRaH, see NECK; ‘relating to it,’ kaRWyaH -RWyA -RWyaM; ‘seated in it,’ kaRWasTaH -sTA -sTaM, kaRWagataH -tA -taM; ‘up to the throat,’ AkaRWAt; ‘dryness of it,’ kaRWaSopaH.
Throb, v. t. pra-, spaMd 1 A, sPur 6 P, vep 1 A; kaMp 1 A. [Throb]bing, s. spaMdaH, spaMdanaM; sPuraRaM, sPuritaM, kaMpaH.
THROB: I Verb:(1) PurPurAyate (nomi.), Mr. 1.;(2) duradurAyate (nomi.);(3) vepate (vep, c. 1.): v. To palpitate.II T. bing:(1) PurPurAyitam;(2) duradurAyitam;(3) vepanam (= quake).
To THROB , v. n. sPur (c. 6. sPurati -rituM), visPur, spand (c. 1. spandate ndituM), pratispand, parispand, kamp, vikamp, vep. See To PALPI- TATE, BEAT.
THROB , THROBBING, s. sPuraRaM -RA, sPuritaM, spandanaM, spanditaM, vizpandaH, spandaH, kampaH, sPoraRaM, sPuraH, sParaRaM, sPAraRaM, sPulanaM; ‘of the eye,’ cakzuHspandaH.
Throe, s. yAtanA, vedanA, vyaTA; (of delivery) prasavavedanA, prasavakAlavyaTA.
THROE: yAtanA: v. Pain.
THROE , s. (Of child-birth) prasavavedanA, garBavedanA, veDanA.

Throne, s. siMhAsanaM, nfpAsanaM, &c.; BadrAsanaM; ‘ascended the ancestral t(hrone)’ Beje pEtf-kamAsanaM (R. xvii. 28); ‘getting the t(hrone)’ rAjapadAvApti f.; ‘having lost his t(hrone)’ CatraBrazwaH. v. t. aBizic 6 P, rAjye aBizic, siMhAsanaM Aruh c.; ‘t(hron)ed king’ aBizikto rAjA.

THRONE: I Lit.: siMhAsanam and sim. comp.s, seated on t. s: siMhAsanasTAn, R. vi. l.; ascended the paternal t.: Beje pEtfkamAsanam, R. xvii. 28. II Fig.: Catram, one who has lost his t.: CatraBrazwa (f. zwA), Mah.: v. Kingdom.
THRONE , s. siMhAsanaM, nfpAsanaM, rAjAsanaM, uccAsanaM, BadrAsanaM, rAjaSayyA, mahASayyA, maYcaH, rAjAsanamaYcaH.
Throng, s. janasaMmardaH-saMkulaM, lokanivahaH. v. t. A-samA-kF 6 P, saMbAD 1 A. v. i. janAkIrRa-janasaMbADa a. BU; See Crowd. [Throng]ed, a. A-samA-kIrRa, janasaMkula-saMbADita.
THRONG: I Subs.: janasaMmardaH and sim. comp.s: v. Crowd, multitude.II Verb: expr. by janAkIrRa (f. rRA) and sim. adj.s: v. To crowd.
THRONGED , p. p. saNkIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, samAkIrRaH &c., bADitaH -tA -taM.
Throttle, v. t. galaM nizpIq 10, galanizpI-qanena vyA-pad c., galahastayati (D.).
THROTTLE (v.): galaM nizpIqyati (pIq, c. 10. = press) or nizpIqya mArayati (=t. to death).
To THROTTLE , v. a. galagrahaM kf, galahasta. See To CHOKE, SUFFOCATE.

Through, prep. Ex. by instr. or abl. 2 maDyena, aMtareRa; ‘t(hrough) the branches’ viwa pAMtareRa. 3 pAraM, tIrAMtaraM yAvat. 4 muKena; dvAreRa, dvArA, in comp.; saKImuKenoce ‘spoke t(hrough) her friend’. adv. samagraM, sAdyaMtaM, SezaM yAvat, AsamApteH; oft. by pAraM gam or dfS 1 P; ‘he has learnt the Vedas t(horoughly)’ SrutipAraM gataH, SrutipAradfSvA, ‘to get t(horough)’ tArayati-pArayati (D.), samAp c. Throughout, prep. Ex. by sarva, samasta; See All; A or yAvat in comp.; ‘t(hroughout) oneʼs life’ yAvajjIvaM-vena, AjIvitAMtAt ‘t(hroughout) the town’ aKile nagare, nagare sarvatra. adv. sarvatra, aSezataH; sarvatra vEtA-lIyaM CaMdaH ‘the metre is Vaitālīya t(horoughout)’

THROUGH (prep.): I On account of: q. v.: [Page711] t. fear: BayAt: v. For.II By the agency of:(1) -muKena (= by the mouth of), I have asked his Majesty t. Nipuṇikā: mayA nipuRikA- muKena yAcito mahArAjaH, Mal. iii.;(2) dvAreRa or dvArA (from dvAra and -r = door), I shall spread some snare t. her: taddvAreRa kiYcijjAlamAraceyam, D. iii.III Throughout: q. v.IV With verbs of motion: by ins., t. this row of young plants: anayA bAlapAdapavITyA, Sa. iii.; now passes t. the region of clouds: kvacitpaTA saYcarate GanAnAm, R. xiii. 19.V From the other side of: -antareRa, to listen t. a clink: CidrAntareRA- karRayati.
THROUGH (adv.): expr. by adj. all: q. v.: to read a book t.: samagraM granTaM paWati; to see t.: sarvaM paSayati; etc.

THROUGH , prep. (From one end or side to the other) pAraM, ApArSvAntarAt, pArSvAntaraparyyantaM, pArSvAntaraM yAvat, tIrAntaraM. — (Denot- ing passage) maDyena, antareRa or expressed by the inflection of the noun; ‘he goes through a fissure in the rock,’ giriranDramaDyena gacCati; ‘through the branches,’ viwapAntareRa. — (By means of, through the agency or influence of) ex- pressed by the abl. or instr. case; as, ‘through ambition,’ loBAt, loBena; ‘through anger,’ kopAt, rozaRatayA; ‘through him,’ tena, see under BY, prep.

THROUGH , adv. (From the beginning to the end) sAdyantaM, AdyantaM. — (To the end) SepaparyyantaM, SezaM yAzat, samAptiparyyantaM, avasAnaparyyantaM, AsamApteH, ASepAt, see THROUGHOUT; ‘to carry through, get through,’ pAr (c. 10. pArayati -yituM), tIr (c. 10. tIrayati -yituM), see To FINISH, v. a.
THROUGHOUT (prep.): t. the town: sarvatra nagare; t. the year: samaste varze; t. one's life: AjanmanaH (= from birth); t. the world: yAvatsaMsAramaRqalam: v. Also all.

THROUGHOUT , adv. (From the beginning to the end) sAdyantaM, [Page803-a+ 51] AdyantaM, SezaparyyantaM. — (Of time) expressed by paryyantaM, yAvat or A in comp.; thus, ‘throughout the month,’ mAsaparyyantaM; ‘throughout the year,’ varzaparyyantaM; ‘throughout the whole year,’ AvarzAntAt or varzAntaM yAvat (i. e. to the end of the year); ‘throughout life,’ yAvajjIvaM, jIvanaparyyantaM, AjIvanAntAt.

Throw, v. t. pra-, kzip 6 P, pra-, as 4 P, pat c., pra-, muc 6 P, visfj 6 P, Ir c. prez c., (with loc. of place); ‘t(hrow) a glance’ dfzwiM-cakzuH-kzip or dA 3 U or pat c.; ‘t(hrow) into disorder’ piMjalI-AkulI-kf 8 U, vyUhaM BaMj 7 P; ‘t(hrow) dice’ akzAn Avap 1 P or pat c. [Throw] about, ut-vi-kzip, ita-stataH cal c.; bAhUtkzepaM ‘t(hrow)ing about the arms’. [Throw] away, niH-vi-kzip, apAs, apa-hA 3 P, apavyaD 4 P, tyaj 1 P; (time) kzip, hf 1 P, yAMyA c. (yAMpayatiyApayati). 2 niras, pratyAKyA 2 P; See Reject; ‘it was t(hrow)ing words away’ nirarTakaM-moGaM-eva tad BAzaRaM, vAgAyAsamAtrakaM BAzaRaM; ‘kindness was not thrown away upon him’ sonugrahaM kftajYatayAsmarat; ‘to be thrown away upon’ viPalIBU 1 P, viPalatAM gam 1 P, layaM-kzayaM-nASaM-gam-yA &c.; gatA nASaM tArA upakftamasADAviva jane (Mr. 5); asatpuruzaseveva dfzwirviPalatAM gatA (Mr. 1). [Throw] down, pat c., aDaH kzip or pat; pra-BraMS c., pracyu c. [Throw] off niH-pra-kzip, ava-nir-DU 5, 9 U, nirAkf, apavyaD, apa-sf c.; ‘t(hrow) one off his guard’ asAvaDAna a. kf; ‘t(hrow) off the veil or mask’ svarUpaM prakawIkf or vi-vf 5 U or prakAS c. [Throw] out, Reject, q. v. 2 niH-, sf c., apAs. 3 (Hints) sUc 10, upa-kzip, upanyas, vyaMj c. [Throw] up, udas, utkzip &c.; (from the stomach) udvam 1 P, ud-gF 6 P; ‘I have thrown a wall around’ upakzipto mayA BittibaMDaH (M. 5). s. pra-, kzepaH-paRaM, prAsanaM, preraRaM; &c. [Throw]er, s. kzeptf m., prAsakaH.

THROW: (1) kzipati, threw a mace at the prince: rAjaputrAya cikzepa daRqam, M. p. 127. 18.; to t. (him) on the ground: kzeptukAmamavanO, Ki.; who has thrown her eyes on the bed: Sayane niHkziptAkzI, Gi. vii. 1.;(2) asyati (as, c. 4.), threw a dirt on him: tasminnAsTadizIkAsram, R. xii. 23.;(3) pAtayati (c. of pat = fell), t. ing of dice: akzapAtanam, Mah. ii. 59. 4. com.; SrutO pAtayati, V. iii. 13.(4) vapati (vap, c. 1.: only of dice), t. ing dice: akzAnuptvA Mah.: v. Also to cast, discharge.

THROW (subs.): kzepaH, vi-, pra-, niH- (the distance of), an arrow's throw: izuvikzepaH, Mah.; t. ing away of a moment: kzaRakzepaH, Si. xii. i.; t. ing off: kzepaRam, V. p. v. 20. 54.; t. ing down: avapAtanam, B. p. x. 44. 4.

To THROW , v. a. kzip (c. 6. kzipati, kzeptuM), prakzip, as (c. 4. asyati -situM), prAs, muc (c. 6. muYcati, moktuM), pramuc, Ir (c. 10. Irayati -yituM), samIr, udIr, pat (c. 10. pAtayati -yituM), sfj, prahf, prez in caus. — (Throw away) apAs, vyudas, apavyaD, tyaj, apahA, vihA, naS in caus., see To LOSE, REJECT; ‘one's time,’ kAlaM kzip, kAlakzepaM kf. — (Throw about) vikzip, itastataH kzip. — (Throw behind one's back) pfzWataH kf or kzip. — (Throw down) pat in caus., avapat, aDaHpat, aDaH kzip, aDaH kf, BraMS in caus., praBraMS, cyu in caus., pracyu. — (Throw into disorder) vyUhAn BaYj or Bid, piYjalIkf. — (Throw off) avaDU, nirDU, viDU, niras, nirAkf, apavyaD. — (Throw out) niras, nirAkf; ‘as hints, &c.,’ sUc, sUcanAM kf. — (Throw up) utkzip, utkzepaM kf, see To VOMIT. — (Throw up), see To RESIGN. — (Throw one's self down) svadehAvapAtaM kf; ‘from a cliff,’ giriSiKarAd avapAtaM kf or prapatanaM kf.
THROW , s. kzepaH -paRaM, prakzepaH, AkzepaH, asanaM, pAtaH -tanaM, kziptiH f.
THROW ABOUT: (1) vikzipati, as if t. ing about the light of the sun: pramAM ravervikzipanniva, Ki. xvi. 50.: v. To scatter.
THROW AROUND: parikzipati: v. To encircle.
THROW AWAY: I To spend, squander, waste: q. v.: kzipati, pra-, niH-, vi-.II To reject: q. v.:(1) nirasyati;(2) apAsyati.
THROW DOWN: (1) pAtayati (c. of pat = fell), seizes (him) by the hair and t. s (him) d.: keSezu gfhItvA pAtayati, Mr. vi.;(2) aDaH kzipati, etc.
THROW OFF: I Lit.: kzipati, pra-, niH-, t. ing off the collyrium of (her) eyes: akzRorniHkzipadaYjanam, Gi. xi. 11.: v. Throw.II To discard, drive out: q. v.
THROW OUT: I To reject, dispel: q. v.: nirasyati.II To t. up: q. v.
THROW TOGETHER: I Lit.:(1) saMkzipati; (2) samasyati.II To bring together: v. Together.
THROW UP: (1) utkzipati, t. n up for a moment: kzaRotkzipta, Si. i. 4.;(2) udasyati, t. ing up for- titude: udasya DEryam, Ki. viii. 50.
THROWER: (1) kzeptf (f. ptrI);(2) kzepaka (f. pikA) : v. To throw.
THROWER , s. kzepakaH, prakzepakaH, kzeptA m. (mf), prAsakaH, kzepaRakft.

THROWN , p. p. kziptaH -ptA -ptaM, prakziptaH &c., astaH -stA -staM, prAstaH &c., IritaH -tA -taM, pAtitaH -tA -taM; ‘away,’ apAstaH &c., vyudastaH &c., apavidDaH -dDA -dDaM, apasAritaH -tA -taM, tyaktaH -ktA -ktaM, nazwaH -zwA -zwaM; ‘a kindness is thrown away on bad men,’ sukftam asatsu nazwaM; ‘thrown down,’ pAtitaH -tA -taM, nipAtitaH &c., aDaHpAtitaH &c., aDaHkziptaH -ptA -ptaM, aDaHkftaH -tA -taM, BraMSitaH -tA -taM; ‘thrown into disorder,’ BagnavyUhaH -hA -haM, BinnavyUhaH &c., piYjalaH -lA -laM, samutpiYjalaH &c.; ‘thrown off,’ nirDUtaH -tA -taM, avaDUtaH &c., apavidDaH &c.; ‘as from a horse, &c.,’ nirastaH -stA -staM.
Thrum, s. daSAH-vastayaH (pl.).
THRUM (subs.): (1) daSAH (f. pl.);(2) vartayaH (f. pl.).
THRUM , s. (Ends of threads) daSAH f. pl., vastayaH f. pl. (vasti).
Thrush, s. sArikA, SarAri f.
THRUSH, THRUSTLE: pakziviSezaH; sArikA (?).
THRUSH , s. (Bird) sArikA, SArikA, madanasArikA, SalAkA, SarAriH f., SarAliH f., sarAtiH f., AwiH f., AqiH f., AtiH f.

Thrust, v. t. apavyaD 4 P, pra-sf c., pra-kzip 6 P; ‘t(hrust) away’, ‘t(hrust) out’ niras 4 U, niHsf c., bahizkf 8 U; (the hand &c.) pra-sf c.; ‘t(hrust) into’ pra-ni-viS c.; ‘t(hrust) on’ pracud c., pracal c. s. AGAtaH, prahAraH, tAqanaM; (with fist) muzwiprahAraH-AGAtaH.

THRUST (v. t.): AviDyati (vyaD, c. 4.): v. To push. Comp.s (a) t. at: AviDyati.: v. To attack; (b) t. away: nirasyati (as, c. 4.) : v. To dispel; (c) t. in, into: niveSayati, saM- (c. of viS): v. To put, enter; (d) t. off: AviDyati: v. To push; (e) t. on: pracodayati (cud, c. 10.).: v. To impel, encourage; (f) t. out: apasArayati (c. of sf).: v. Drive out; (g) t. through: minatti (Bid, c. 7.).: v. To pierce.
THRUST (subs.): I Blow, stroke: q. v.: ADAtaH.II With the fist: muzwiH.III A wound with a pointed instrument: Binnam, Ni.
To THRUST , v. a. taq (c. 10. tAqayati -yituM), pramf (c. 10. -sArayati -yituM), prasAraRaM kf; ‘aside,’ apasf, see To PUSH.
THRUST , s. tAqanaM, AGAtaH, aBiGAtaH, prasAraRaM, prahAraH, see PUSH.
THUD: nirGozaH: v. Loud noise.
Thumb, s. aMguzWaH; ‘under oneʼs t(humb)’ Ayatta, vaSya. v. t. aMguzWena parAmfS 6 P or spfS 6 P or aMk 10.
THUMB (subs.): (1) aNguzWaH;(2) vfdDANguliH.
THUMB (v. t.): aNguzWena spfSati (spfSa, c. 6.=to) [Page712] touch) etc. (Comp. nyubjANguzWena tantrItAqanam, M. n. on Si. i. 9.).
THUMB , s. aNguzWaH, aNgulaH, vfdDANguliH f.; ‘thumb and forefinger,’ santozaH.
To THUMB , v. a. aNgulIBir aNk (c. 10. aNkayati -yituM) or parAmfS or spfS, aNgulyaNkitaM -tAM kf. See To FINGER, v. a.
THUMBSCREW: *aNguzWamardanI.
Thump, v. t. Ahan 2 U, taq 10, pra-hf 1 P. s. A-aBi-GAtaH, prahAraH.
THUMP: I Verb: Ahanti (han, c. 2.).: v. To strike.II Subs.: AGAtaH: v. To blow.
THUMP , s. AGAtaH, prahAraH, karaGAtaH, muzwipAtaH. See BLOW.
To THUMP , v. a. taq (c. 10. tAqayati -yituM), prahf, Ahan. See To BEAT.

Thunder, s. meGagarjanaM, GanaDvaniH, jImUtasta-nitaM, meGagarjitaM; and sim. comp.; vi-, sPUrjaTuH-TUH, sPUrjitaM, stanitaM, rasitaM; garjitaM, garjanaM-nA; ‘t(hunder)-bolt’ vajraH-jraM, kuliSaM, BiduraM, paviH, aSani m. f., SatakowiH, svaruH, SaMbaH, hrAdinI, daMBoliH; ‘t(hunder)-clap’ vajranirGozaH-nirGAtasvanaH nizpezaH; See (s.); ‘t(hunder)-storm’ aSanivarzaH-pAtaH; ‘t(hunder)-struck’ aSanitAqita, vajrAhata, See Astounded. v. garj 1 P, stan 1 P, vi-sPurj 1 P; ‘shouldst t(hunder) reproof’ yattvaM (sAkzepamiva) nadasi siMhanAdEH (Mr. 5). [Thunder]er, s. vajrin m.; kuliSaBft, vajrapARiH.
THUNDER (subs.): I The noise: q. v.:(1) meGanirGozaH;(2) GanaDvaniH;(3) sPUrjaTuH, vi.II Roar: q. v.: garjitam.III T. -bolt: q. v.
THUNDER (v.): garjati, pari- (garj, c. 1.).: v. Roar. T. out: sagarjitam udgirati (gF, c. 6.) : v. To utter, emit.

THUNDER , s. garjanaM -nA, garjitaM, meGagarjitaM, meGanAdaH, meGaSabdaH, meGani- rGozaH, sPUrjaH, sPUrjanaM, sPUrjaTuH m., visPUrjaTuH m., visPUrjitaM, meGavi- sPUrjitaM, stanitaM, meGastanitaM, stananaM, meGastananaM, stanayitnuH m., GanaSabdaH, GanasvanaH, GanaravaH, meGaDvaniH m., pariGozaH, gamBIranAdaH, garjiH m., garmaM, rasitaH.
To THUNDER , v. n. garj (c. 1. garjati -rmituM), parigarj, sPurj (c. 1. sPUrjati -rmituM), visPurn, stan (c. 1. stanati -nituM), garjanaM kf, sPUrjanaM kf.
THUNDER-CLAP , s. sPUrjaTuH m., vajranirGozaH, vajranizpezaH, vajrAGAtaH, vajrajrAlA, vajrapAtaSabdaH, vajrastanitaM, vajranisvanaH.
THUNDER-CLOUD , s. GanaH, vajraGanaH, meGaH, vajrameGaH, vajrABra.
THUNDER-STORM , s. vajravarzaH, aSanivarzaH, kuliSavarzaH.
THUNDER-STRUCK: (1) vajrAhataH (tA, taM);(2) aSanitAqitaH (tA, taM) and sim. comp. s. N. B. In fig. sense, iva (= as if) is added.
THUNDERBOLT: (1) vajram, about to hurl t.: vajraM mumukzan, R. ii. 42.;(2) kuliSam, t. -holder: kuliSaBft (m.), Ki. x. 16.;(3) aSaniH, struck with t.: aSanihata (f. tA), K.

THUNDERBOLT , s. vajraH -jraM, vajrAGAtaH, kuliSaH -SaM, BiduraM, BidiH m., [Page803-b+ 51] BidiraM, BiduH m., aSaniH m. f., vajrASaniH m., Cidaka, mfdAkaraH, SataDAraM, SatAraM, bahuDAraH, SatakowiH m., zawkoRaM, aBrotTaM, tridaSANkuSaM, girijvaraH, giriDvajaH, girikaRwakaH, indrapraharaRaM, svaruH m., damBoliH m., hrAdinI, paviH m., SambaH, SamBaH, peSiH m., jasuriH m., vyADAnaH, meGaBUtiH f., dfmBUH m., daDIcyasTi n., vEdyuto -gniH; ‘fall of a thun- derbolt,’ vajrapAtaH; ‘like a thunderbolt,’ vajraprAyaH -yA -yaM.
THUNDERER: I Lit.: stanayitnuH: v. Roar.II Of gods:(1) vajrin (m.);(2) vajrapARiH, etc.
THUNDERER , s. vajrI m. (n), vajrapARiH m., vajraDaraH, kuliSaBft.
THUNDERING , s. sPUrjanaM, garjanaM, meGagarjanaM. See THUNDER.
THUNDERING , part. garjan -rjantI -rjat (t), sPUrjAvAn -vatI -vat (t).
THUNDERSTRUCK , a. vajrAhataH -tA -taM, vajrahataH &c., vajraprahataH &c., vajra- tAqitaH -tA -taM, vidyudDataH &c. See ASTOUNDED.
Thursday, s. guruvAsaraH.
THURSDAY: (1) guruvAraH;(2) bfhaspativAraH;(3) guruvAsaraH;(4) lakzmIvAsaraH.
THURSDAY , s. vfhaspativAraH, guruvAraH, guruvAsaraH, lakzmIvAraH.
Thus, adv. evaM, itTaM, iti, anena prakAreRa, anayA rItyA.

THUS: (1) itTam, the king first argued t.: itTaM nfpaH pUrvamavAluluce, B. i. 23.;(2) evam, while the divine sage was talking t.: evaMvAdini devarzO, Ku. vi. 84.;(3) iti (to connect a quotation), R. viii. 75. Ph.: t. much: etAvat: v. Much, so; t. far: etAvatIM BUmim, K.

THUS , adv. (In this manner) evaM, itTaM, anena prakAreRa, evamprakAreRa, uktena prakAreRa, uktaprakAreRa, anayA rItyA, anayartyA, ataeva. — (So) taTA, taTAhi, iti, etAdfSaM. — (Thus much) iyAn -yatI -yat (t), etAvAn &c.
THWACK: tAqayati (taq, c. 10.): v. To strike.
Thwart, v. t. KaMq 10, vi-prati-han 2 P, moGIkf 8 U, ni-prati-vi-ruD 7 U; pratikUlayati-pratIpayati (D.); ka IpsitArTasTiraniScayaM manaH pratIpayet (K. v. 5); See Frustrate, Baffle.
THWART (v.): moGIkarotiH v. To frustrate, defeat.
To THWART , v. a. KaRq, pratihan, pratiruD, see To FRUSTRATE, HINDER.
THWARTED , p. p. saMrudDacezwaH -zwA -zwaM, pratibadDaH &c. See FRUSTRATED.
THY , pron. tava gen. c. (yuzmat), tvadIyaH -yA -yaM.
THYME: suganDigulmaviSezaH.
THYSELF , pron. sa tvaM, AtmA m. (n). See MYSELF.
Tiara, s. mukuwaM, kirIwaH, mOliH.
TIARA: mukuwam: v. Crown.
TIARA , s. mukuwaM, kirIwaH, mOliH m. f., avataMsaH, lalAwapawwaM, cUqA.
TIBIA: jaNGAyA agrAsTi.
TIBIA , s. jaNGAyAH pUrvvAsTi n. or agrAsTi n.
Tick, s. yUkA. 2 Credit, q. v.
TICK: I An insect: yUkaH.II Credit: q. v. III A covering: AstaraRam.IV A noise: perh. wIkitam.
TICK (v.): perh. wIkate (wIk, c. 1.).: v. Also to beat.
TICK , s. (Credit), see CREDIT. — (Louse) yUkaH, lomakIwaH.
To TICK , v. n. (As a clock) kAlamApakavat kiwakiwaSabdaM kf or pawapa- waSabdaM kf, pawapawa (nom. pawapawAyate -ti).
Ticket, nirdarSanI, aBijYAnapatraM.
TICKET: I Subs.: *trikawam; nidarSanI: v. Also mark.II Verb: *trikawayati.
TICKET , s. patrakaM, patraM, sUcakapatraM, nidarSanapatraM, aNkapatraM.
To TICKET , v. a. aNkapatrayuktaM -ktAM kf, aNkapatraviSizwaM -zwAM kf.
Tickle, v. kutakUtayati (D.), kaMqUyati (D.); (fig.) Please, Gratify, q. v. [Tickl]er, s. kaMqUyanakaH.
TICKLE: I Lit.: perh. kutakutayati (nomi.), t. ing sensation: kutakutam. (?).II Fig.: v. To excite.
To TICKLE , v. a. kaRqU (nom. kaRqUyati), kaRqUyanaM kf, kaRqUyAM kf.
TICKLER , s. kaRqUyanakaH, kaRqUtikArI m. (n), kaRqUyAkft.
TICKLISH: expr. with kutakutam.
TICKLISH , a. kaRqUyanAsahanaH -nA -naM, kaRqUyAsahaH -hA -haM, kaRqUtyasahaH &c.
TID-BIT , s. sugrAsaH, viSizwagrAsaH, AhAraviSezaH, BojanaviSezaH.
Tide, s. velA (of the sea). 2 srotas n., oGaH, vegaH, rayaH; See Stream. v. t. (over) tF 1 P, saM-ut-°.

TIDE (subs.): I Lit.: velA, the sea-t. flows on the day of the full moon: pUrRimAdine samudravelA carati, P. i. 12.; rising t.: vardDamAnA velA, Raj.; the t. is coming on: veleyamAgacCati, Na.; spring- t.: pUrRavelA (?).II Fig.: current, stream: q. v.: srotas (n.).III Time: q. v.: velA.
TIDE , s. velA, srotas n., pravAhaH, rayaH; ‘of the sea,’ samudravelA; ‘against the tide,’ pratisrotas.
TIDE OVER (v.): tarati (tF, c. 1.).: v. To cross.
TIDING: vArttA: v. News.
Tidings, s. vArtA, pravftti f.; See News.
TIDINGS , s. vArttA, sandeSaH, samAcAraH. See NEWS, INTELLIGENCE.

Tie, v. t. ni-, baMD 9 P, pinah 4 P; (together) yoktrayati (D.), saMbaMD, saMSliz c., saMsaMj c., saM-yuj 7 U, 10, saM-DA 3 U; (flowers &c.) guMP 6 P, saMgraMT 9 P. s. nibaMDanaM, (dvitIyaM manaso nibaMDanaM); saMSlezaRaM, baMDaH-DanaM-nI, graMTiH; ‘t(ie) of a yoke’ yoktraM, AbaMDaH; ‘this (child) is the mutual t(ie) of parents’ etadanyonya-saMSlezaRaM pitroH (U. 3). 2 dAman f. n., guRaH, taMtuH. 2 Fetter, q. v. 4 saMgaH, baMDaH; ‘worldly t(ie)s’ saMsArabaMDaH; ‘free from t(ie)s’ niHsaMga, muktasaMga. [Ti]er, s. paMkti-SreRi f.; See Line.

TIE (v.): sometimes with up and down: (1) baGnAti (banD, c. 9.).: v. To bind, fasten; (2) yoktrayati (nomi.), t. d him up with the arms like a beast with a rope: enaM yoktrayAmAsa bAhuByAM paSuM rasanayA yaTA, Mah. iii. 9. 61.: v. Also restrain, check, string.
TIE (subs.): banDaH: v. Bond.

To TIE , v. a. banD (c. 9. baDnAti, bandDuM), nibanD, pinah; ‘together,’ sambanD, yoktra (nom. yoktrayati -yituM), saMyuj, saMSliz in caus., sanDA, saMlagnIkf, saMhf, granT, gumP, see To FASTEN, KNIT, &c.; ‘with a fetter,’ pASIkf, pASa (nom. pASayati -yituM); ‘to tie up a young deer,’ mfgapotakaM saMyojayituM; ‘to tie up in a bag,’ vastra- vadDaM -dDAM kf.

TIE , s. (A fastening, knot) banDaH -nDanaM -nI, granTiH m., banDanagranTiH m.; ‘of a yoke,’ AbanDaH, yoktraM, yotraM; ‘of a letter or parcel,’ tAlikaH. — (A fetter) pASaH, banDanaM. — (String) guRaH, dAma -mA, see STRING. — (Attachment, tie of affection, &c.) saNgaH; ‘free from ties,’ niHsaNgaH -NgA -NgaM, saNgavarjitaH -tA -taM, asajjitAtmA -tmA -tma (n).

TIED , p. p. badDaH -dDA -dDaM, nibadDaH &c., sannibadDaH &c., nibanDitaH -tA -taM, AbadDaH &c., pinadDaH -dDA -dDaM, AnadDaH &c., dfbDaH &c., guRavAn -vatI &c.; ‘together,’ sambadDaH -dDA -dDaM, AbadDaH &c., saMyojitaH -tA -taM, saMsaktaH -ktA -ktaM, saMlagnIkftaH -tA -taM, sanDAnitaH &c., sanDitaH &c., sanditaH &c.; ‘tied with a fetter,’ pASitaH -tA -taM, pASIkftaH &c.; ‘tied up in,’ nibadDaH -dDA -dDaM; ‘a quantity of money tied up in a bag,’ vastrabadDo mudrAsaYcayaH; ‘a man with his arms tied behind him,’ paScAdbadDabAhuH puruzaH.
TIER: paMktiH: v. Row, line.
TIER , s. paMktiH f., SreRiH -RI f., rAjiH -nI f. See ROW, LINE.
TIERCE: in music: gAnDAraH. (?).
Tiffin, s. upAhAraH.
Tiger, s. vyAGraH, SArdUlaH, dvIpin m.
TIGER: vyAGraH. Tigress: vyAGrI. T. -skin: vyAGracarma, M. n.; a sheet of t. -skin: vEyAGrakoSaH, Mah. iv. 42. 12.

TIGER , s. vyAGraH, SArdUlaH, dvIpI m. (n), vicitrANgaH, guhASayaH, mfgAriH m., mfgAd m., hiMsAruH m., BayAnakaH; ‘state of one,’ vyAGratA; ‘re- lating to one,’ vEyAGraH &c.; ‘its skin,’ vyAGracarmma n.

Tight, a. aSiTila, dfQa, gAQa, saMsakta, susaM-hata. 2 atipinadDa, gAQa-dfQa-badDa, saMnibadDa; ‘I am chained down by this t(ight) barkgarment’ atipinadDena valkalena niyaMtritAsmi (S. 1); ‘the coat sits t(ight) on your body’ aMgAnaMtaravartI-aMgasaMsaktaH-kaMcukaH. 3 Atata. 4 saMbADa. [Tight]en, v. t. dfQIkf 8 U, niyam 1 P, draQayati (D.). [Tight]ly, adv. dfQaM, pra-gAQaM, aSiTilaM; ‘tied t(ightly)’ dfQabadDa &c. [Tight]ness, s. dfQatA, GanatA, susaMsakti f., saMhati f., AnaMtaryaM.
TIGHT: (1) aSiTila (f. lA);(2) dfQa (f. QA) : v. Firm. Ph.: with the very t. bark: atipinadDena valkalena, Sa. i.

TIGHT , a. (Close, firm) dfQaH -QA -QaM, GanaH -nA -naM, saMhataH -tA -taM, aSiTilaH -lA -laM, gAQaH -QA -QaM, pragAQaH &c. — (Tied tight) dfQa- badDaH -dDA -dDaM, sannibadDaH &c., dfQasanDiH -nDiH -nDi. — (Tight-drawn) AtataH -tA -taM, dfQaH &c., see STRETCHED. — (Pinching) sambADakaH -kA -kaM, sambADaH -DA -DaM, saNkocakaH &c.
TIGHTEN: I To make firm: draQayati (nomi.). II As reins: niyacCati (yam, c. 1.): v. To restrain.
To TIGHTEN , v. a. dfQIkf, draQa (nom. draQayati -yituM), dfQatarIkf.
TIGHTLY: (1) aSiTilam;(2) dfQam: v. Firmly.
TIGHTLY , adv. dfQaM, gAQaM, pragAQaM; ‘tied tightly,’ dfQabadDaH -dDA -dDaM.
TIGHTNESS: (1) aSETilyam;(2) dArQyam: v. Firmness.
TIGHTNESS , s. dfQatA, dArQyaM, GanatA, saMhatatvaM, sambADatA -DakatA.
TIGRESS , s. vyAGrI, SArdUlI, dvIpinI, vicitrANgI.
TIGRINE , TIGRISH, a. vEyAGraH -GrI -GraM, vyAGropamaH -mA -maM.
TILE (subs.): *KapparaH.
TILE (v. t.): *KapparEH CAdayati (c. of Cad). T. d house: *Kapparagfham.
TILE , s. pakvezwakA, pakvezwikA, pakvamfttikAPalakaH.
To TILE , v. a. pakvezwakABir ACad, pakvezwakAcCAdanaM kf.
TILER (subs.): *KapparikaH.

sanskrit.slp1: yAvad fRaM na pariSoDayati tAvat taM kArAyAM badDavAn
sanskrit.word: यावद् ऋणं न परिशोधयति तावत् तं कारायां बद्धवान्
sanskrit.iast: yāvad ṛṇaṃ na pariśodhayati tāvat taṃ kārāyāṃ baddhavān

details.body: Till, adv., prep. yAvat (with acc. of noun) or yAvat na (followed by tAvat); ‘t(ill) now’ adyAvaDi, adya yAvat; gen. by A in comp. or with abl.; ‘t(ill) death’ AmaraRaM, AmftyoH; ‘t(ill) the learned are satisfied’ AparitozAdviduzAM (S. 1). v. t. kfz 1 P, 6 U. [Till]age, Tilth, s. kfzikarman a.; kfzi f. [Till]er, s. kfzakaH, karzakaH, kfzIvalaH; kzetrAjIvaH.
TILL (prep.): v. Until. T. now: adyAvaDi; t. death: A mftyoH.
TILL (v. t.): karzati (kfz, c. 1.): v. To culti- -vate.
TILL (subs.): i. e. money-box: *waNkapewI; waNkA- DAraH.
TILL , s. (Money-box) mudrABARqaM, mudrApAtraM, mudrADAraH.

TILL , prep. or adv. yAvat, paryyantaM, avaDi, A. The last is pre- fixed, and governs the abl. c.; ‘till now,’ adya yAvat, idAnI, yAvat, adyaparyyantaM, etatkAlaparyyantaM, adyAvaDi, AvarttamAnakAlAt; ‘till then,’ tadAnIM yAvat, tatkAlaM yAvat, tatkAlaparyyantaM; ‘till satisfied,’ AtfpteH; ‘till death,’ AmftyoH, AmaraRAt; ‘till the whole was mixed together,’ AsarvvamiSraRAt, sarvvamiSraRaparyyantaM; ‘abide ye there till you have to go to another place,’ sTAnAntaragama- naparyyantaM tatra tizWata; ‘he kept him in prison till he should pay the debt,’ yAvad fRaM na pariSoDayati tAvat taM kArAyAM badDavAn.
To TILL , v. a. kfz (c. 1. karzati, krazwuM), karzaRaM kf, kfziM kf, see To PLOUGH.
TILLAGE: (1) kfziH, -karman (n.);(2) karzaRam. (rare).
TILLAGE , TILLING. s. kfziH f., kfzikarmma n. (n), pramftaM. See PLOUGHING.
TILLED , p. p. kfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, karzitaH -tA -taM. See PLOUGHED.
TILLER: kfzaka or karzaka (f. zikA): v. Cultiva- -tor.
TILLER , s. kfzakaH, karzakaH, kzetrakarzakaH, kfzIbalaH, kfzijIvI m.
Tilt, s. vitAnaM, ullocaH. 2 prAsakrIqAyudDaM. v. t. Avfj 10. 2 prAsayudDe pravft 1 A. v. t. A-ava-nam 1 P, Buj 6 P.
TILT (subs.): I An awing: vitAnam.II A combat: v. Tournament.
TILT (v.): I To incline: Avarjayati (vfj, c. 10.).II To practise t.: prASayudDamaByasyati (as, c. 4.).
TILT , s. (Kind of awning) vitAnaM -nakaM, AcCAdanaM, ullocaH. — (Tour- nament) aSvArohiRAM krIqAyudDaM.
To TILT , v. a. (Incline) Avfj (c. 10. -varjayati -yituM).
To TILT , v. n. (Lean) nam, avanam. — (Fight) krIqAyudDaM kf.
TILTED , p. p. (Inclined) AvarjitaH -tA -taM. — (Covered) savitAnaH -nA -naM.
Timber, s. kAzWaM, dAru n.
TIMBER: kAzWam: v. Wood.
TIMBER , s. dAruH m. -ru n., kAzWaM, dalikaH, visAraM; ‘of a door,’ nAsA.
TIMBREL: qiRqimaH: v. Drum.
TIMBREL , s. mfdaNgaH, pawahaH, paRavaH. See TABOR, DRUM.

Time, s. kAlaH, samayaH, velA. 2 (Occasion) avasaraH, prasaMgaH, prastAvaH. 3 vAraH, vAsaraH. 5 avaDiH, maryAdA. 5 tAlaH, layaH. 6 (Personified) kAlaH. 7 (With numerals) guRaM, kftvaH, vAraM, in comp.; ‘10 t(ime)s’ daSakftvaH; sahasraguRaM, trivAraM, &c.; ‘from t(ime) to t(ime)’ kAle kAle; ‘losing or wasting t(ime)’ kAlaharaRaM kAlakzepaH-hAniH; ‘by this tby this t(ime)’ anena samayena, iyatA kAlena; ‘after a long t(ime)’ cirAt, bahoH kAlAt; ‘for a long t(ime)’ cira, mahAMtaM kAlaM; ‘of the same t(ime)’ samakAlIna, samakAlika (kI f.); ‘at the right t(ime)’ kAle, yaTA-vasaraM, prAptakAlaM; ‘in time’ yaTAsamayaM-avasaraM, kAle; ‘in a short t(ime)’ acireRa-rAt; ‘at the t(ime) when’ yadA-tadA; ‘at the same t(ime)’ samaM, ekAvasaraM, tatkAlaM, tatkzaRaM; ‘at all t(ime)s’ sadA, sarvadA; ‘at other t(ime)’ anyadA; ‘at t(ime)s’ kAle kAle, aMtarA aMtarA; ‘at this, that, t(ime)’ aDunA, tadA; ‘at any t(ime)’ yadA kadA; ‘come at any t(ime)’ yadA icCasi tadA-yaTe-zwakAle-AgacCa; ‘of our, those, t(ime)s’ idAnIMtana-tadAnIMtana- (nI f.); ‘high t(ime)’ ucitaH samayaH; ‘it is high t(ime) to bathe and take our meals’ samayaH snAnaBojanaM sevituM (V. 2); ‘good for the t(ime) being’ ApAtaramaRIya, ApAtato ramya; ‘hard t(ime)s’ ApatkAlaH; vipatsamayaH, Apad f.; ‘dark t(ime)s’ kalikAlaH; ‘from t(ime) to t(ime)’ anuvelaM, vAraMvAraM; ‘many t(ime)s’ bahuSaH, bahuvAraM, kAle kAle; ‘t(ime)-server’, ‘t(ime)-serving’ kAlA-nuvartin, samayAnuroDin; ‘I shall not do so next t(ime)’ nEvaM vArAMtaraM viDAsyAmi; ‘what is the t(ime) now’ kA velA aDunA vartate; ‘begging is out of t(ime)’ anavasaragrastorTiBAvaH (Mal. 9); ‘sign of the t(ime)’ kAlaDarmaH; ‘without loss of t(ime)’ akAla-kzepeRa, avilaMbitaM; ‘one keeping or beating t(ime) with the hands’ pARiGaH, pARivAdaH; karakisalayatAlErmugDayA nartyamAnaH (U. 3) ‘by keeping t(ime) with her hands’ &c.; ‘quick, mean, slow, t(ime)’ drutaM, maDyaM, vilaM-bitaM; ‘out of t(ime)’ vitAla, vEtAlika (kI f.). v. t. kAlaM, nirRI 1 P or parikxp c., kAlAnurUpa a. kf 8 U. [Time]ly, a. Ex. by (s.) in comp.; ‘showering t(imely)’ kAla-samaya-varziRaH; sAmayika (kI f.); kAlakftodyo-gAt ‘by t(imely) attempts’. adv. kAle, yaTA-samayaM-kAlaM.

TIME (subs.): I Lit.:(1) kAlaH, from t. to t.: kAle kAle, Me.; by this t.: iyatA kAlena, D. iii.; in the course of t.: kAlena, Ve. iii. or kAlakrameRa, Ku. or gacCati kAle, K.; t. should not be thrown away: na kAlaH parikzeptavyaH, Vi. ii.; without los- ing any t.: vihAya kAlaharaRam, Vi. iv.; I will not waste my t.: na kAlaM hAsyAmi, Sa. iii.; for a long t. (= for some hours): mahAntaM kAlam, K.; after a long t.: (= after many years): bahoH kAlAt, U. ii.; of the same t.: samakAlInaH (nA, naM);(2) samayaH (= definite t.), by this t.: anena samayena, K.; at the wrong t.: asamaye, Sa. i.; at the right t.: samaye, R. iii. 13. Ph.: pleasant for the t. being: ApAtaramyaH (myA, myaM), Ki. xi. 12. (note the position of ApAta); in a short t.: acireRa; in the mean t. (=meanwhile: q. v.); at the t. when: yadA...tadA, Ku.; at the same t.: samam or ekAvasaram; at onotheranother t., at other t. s: anyadA, R.; at t. s: v. Sometimes; at that t.: v. Then; at this t.: v. Now; at any t.: yadA, tadA; of the present t., of our t.: idAnIntanaH (nI, naM); of that time: tadAnIntanaH (nI, naM); hard t.s: ApatkAlaH; five t. s, six t. s, etc.: paYcakftvaH, zawkftvaH etc.; many t. s: bahuSaH. II Time of the day: velA, ascertain what is the t.: jYAyatAM kA velA vartata iti, Mu. iv.; dinner t.: mojanavelA, P. iii.: v. Musical measure: (1) layaH, in t. mean, slow and quick: maDya- vilambitalaye dutalaye ca, D. vi.; her steps keeping t.: padanyAso layamupagataH;(2) tAlaH (= beating t.).

TIME , s. (In general) kAlaH, samayaH, velA, dizwaH, anehAH m. (s), harimA m. (n), sarvvamUzakaH, BasantaH, amasaH, jahakaH; ‘lapse of time,’ kAlagatiH f., kAlacakraM, kAlAvfttiH f., kAlaparyyAyaH; ‘in the course of time,’ kAlagatyA, kAle gacCati, dinezu gacCatsu, kAlaparyyAyeRa;
